================================================
# Engine architecture

**Status:** draft. Describes the `:engine` module as of IR v5 (Ф4.7).
Ф2 (types), Ф3 (evaluator, invariants, dead conditions) and Ф4.1–Ф4.7
(choice templates, disabled choices, merge points/analysis, atomic
subroutines) are implemented;
sections marked "deferred" point at the phase that will pick each item
up. See [`roadmap.md`](./roadmap.md) for the phase plan.

This document is the **deep dive** into `:engine`: the IR, the parser,
the runtime, the analyzer, and the entry points that `:app` calls. It
is the companion to [`architecture.md`](./architecture.md), which
describes the layers at a higher level.

## Module boundary

`:engine` is a **pure Kotlin/JVM** module. It has no Android dependency,
no `context`, no file I/O. All file access lives in `:app`. `:engine`
operates on strings (JSON, conditions) and on in-memory data (IR,
`PlayerState`, `StepResult`).

This boundary is enforced by `engine/build.gradle.kts`: no
`com.android.*` plugin; `./gradlew :engine:build` succeeds without
Android SDK. If an engine class ever needs `android.*`, the answer is
"put it in `:app` instead" — the engine must remain testable on a
plain JVM and reusable by the planned JS runtime (E1.base, roadmap).

## Packages

```
com.myapp.adventure.engine
├── ir/                    — typed, serializable IR (Ф1.2)
├── parse/                 — condition parser, error types (Ф1.3.1)
├── format/                — JSON → IR (Ф1.3)
│   └── dto/               — wire-format DTOs
├── analyze/               — reachability, lint (Ф1.6)
├── CompiledAdventure.kt   — runtime indexes (Ф1.5.5.1)
├── CompileResult.kt       — compile errors
├── Engine.kt              — compile, step
├── Evaluator.kt           — condition evaluation
├── EffectsApplier.kt      — effect application
└── StepResult.kt          — outcome of Engine.step
```

## IR (`ir/`)

The typed representation of an adventure. Every field is `val`;
collections are immutable; `PlayerState` is a runtime value, distinct
from `InitialState`.

Key classes:

- `Adventure` — root. `version: Int` (CURRENT_VERSION = 5), `title`, `author`, `description`, `variables`, `choiceTemplates`, `invariants`, `tags`, `initialState`, `deathScene`, `startScene: SceneId`, `chapters`.
- `Chapter` — pure narrative grouping. No mechanical meaning. `id`,
  `title`, `scenes`.
- `Scene` — `id: SceneId`, `text`, `effects: List<Effect>`,
  `choices: List<Choice>`, `gate: Gate?`, `isEnding: Boolean`,
  `isMerge: Boolean` + `mergeSources: List<SceneId>` (Ф4.5, see
  §"Merge points" below).
- `Choice` — `id: ChoiceId`, `text`, `nextScene: SceneId`, `condition: Condition?` (enable), `visibilityCondition: Condition?` (show, Ф4.2), `effects: List<Effect>`, `templateRef: TemplateRef?` (Ф4.2, editor metadata), `call: SubroutineCall?` (Ф4.7 — atomic call executed after `effects`, `nextScene` is the return target).
- `Subroutine` — `id: String`, typed `inputs` / `outputs: List<VarDecl>`, `body: List<SubroutineStep>` (Ф4.7). A call creates a private local frame; the body sees only its parameters, never global variables directly. See §"Subroutines" below.
- `SubroutineStep` — `condition: Condition?`, `effects: List<Effect>`, `call: SubroutineCall?` (Ф4.7). Flat guarded steps: if the condition is false the step is skipped; otherwise effects run, then the nested call (if any).
- `SubroutineCall` — `subroutineId: String`, `args: Map<String, String>`, `outputs: Map<String, String>` (Ф4.7). On a `Choice` the names are globals; inside a body they are the caller frame's locals.
- `Condition` — sealed: `Has`, `Not`, `And`, `Or`, `Compare`,
  `InRange`. AST, not string.
- `Effect` — sealed: `SetFlag`, `RemoveFlag`, `ModifyStat`. List order
  is applied order.
- `Gate` — `requiredSteps: Int`, `repeatable: Boolean`. Steps on the
  **scene**, not the chapter (Ф1.5.4).
- `PlayerState` — runtime state: `flags: Set<String>`,
  `stats: Map<String, Int>`. Immutable.
- `ChoiceTemplate` — reusable choice template. `id`, `parameters: List<VarDecl>`, `text`, `visibilityCondition`, `availabilityCondition`, `effects`, `nextScene`. See §"Choice templates" below.
- `Invariant` — global rule. `condition: Condition`, `outcome: Outcome`. Fires when `condition` holds after a step (Ф3.5).
- `Outcome` — sealed: `Death` today (Ф3.5).

Value classes (`@JvmInline`, serialized transparently):
`SceneId`, `ChoiceId`.

Version history of the on-disk format is in
`Adventure.CURRENT_VERSION` KDoc. The version stayed at `5` for the
additive optional fields introduced in Ф3.5 (`invariants`), Ф4.1
(`choice_templates`), Ф4.5 (`merge` / `merge_sources`) and Ф4.7
(`subroutines` / `Choice.call`); each has an empty/false/null default
and an identity migration.

**Type system:** `Adventure.variables: Map<String, VarDecl>` and the six
`VarType` variants (`Bool`, `Integer`, `IntMin`, `IntRange`, `ItemCount`,
`ItemList`) are documented in [`engine-types.md`](./engine-types.md).
They were introduced in Ф2.1 (declarations), populated by the parser in
Ф2.8 (`JsonToIr`), and validated by `TypeChecker` in Ф2.2 / Ф2.3.

## Parser (`format/`, `parse/`)

### Single entry point: `JsonToIr.parse(text): ParseResult<Adventure>`

This is the only public function in `:engine` that turns raw JSON into
an `Adventure`. It is used by:

- the reader (`:app`) to load an adventure for playing;
- the editor (`:app`) to validate an in-progress JSON;
- the analyzer (Ф1.6) after parsing, to check reachability and
  duplicates;
- tests, including `test_adventure.json`.

Do not write a second parser alongside it. If a new format is needed
(YAML, binary, a future JS runtime), either add a `parse` overload
here or create a new `<Format>ToIr` with the same
`ParseResult<Adventure>` contract.

**Two-stage pipeline (Ф2.3).** Since Ф2.3, `parse` runs two checks in
sequence: JSON parsing (`JsonToIr.buildAdventure`) and type checking
(`TypeChecker.check`, Ф2.2). The order is strict — type checking only
runs when the JSON parses cleanly. A partial IR (a choice whose
condition string failed to parse has `condition = null`) would produce
false negatives at best and false positives at worst, so the parser
short-circuits on the first error (B1 decision, 2026-11-12).

Callers should look at both fields of `ParseResult.Failure`:

```kotlin
when (val result = JsonToIr.parse(json)) {
    is ParseResult.Success -> use(result.value)
    is ParseResult.Failure -> {
        if (result.typeErrors.isNotEmpty()) showTypeErrors(result.typeErrors)
        if (result.errors.isNotEmpty()) showParseErrors(result.errors)
    }
}
```

The two lists are mutually exclusive — exactly one is non-empty. This
is enforced in ParseResult.Failure.init, not just by convention.

### Two-stage parsing

1. **DTO layer** (`format/dto/Dto.kt`, `@Serializable`): mirrors the
   JSON exactly. Optional fields are non-null with defaults; `version`
   is the only nullable (to distinguish "no version" from an explicit
   version).
2. **Mapper** (`JsonToIr`): DTO → IR. Accumulates semantic errors
   (blank ids, empty chapters, unparseable conditions) into a
   `ParseResult.Failure` with **all** errors at once.

### Condition parser (`parse/ConditionParser`)

Syntactic only. Knows nothing about variable types; `TypeChecker`
validates the AST afterwards against `Adventure.variables`. The full
grammar shipped in Ф3.2 / N7.base:

| Input | Result |
|-------|--------|
| `has_X` | `Condition.Has("X")` |
| `!A`, `A && B`, `A \|\| B`, `(A)` | `Not`, `And`, `Or`, grouping |
| `X >= N` / `X > N` / `X <= N` / `X < N` / `X == N` / `X != N` | `Condition.Compare(X, op, N)` |
| `X in A..B` | `Condition.InRange(X, A, B)` |
| `true` / `false` | `Condition.Literal(...)` |

Precedence: `!` > `&&` > `\|\|`; `&&` / `\|\|` are left-associative.
The grammar, precedence table and `ConditionWriter` round-trip are
documented in [`engine-conditions.md`](./engine-conditions.md). Invalid
syntax returns a `ParseError.ConditionError` — **never** a silent pass.

## Runtime (`CompiledAdventure`, `Engine`, `StepResult`)

### `Engine.compile(adventure): CompileResult`

Builds the runtime indexes once per adventure:

- `scenesById: Map<SceneId, Scene>` — O(1) scene lookup.
- `chapterIndexBySceneId: Map<SceneId, Int>` — "which chapter is this
  scene in?".

O(n) in the number of scenes; n is thousands at most. Never call
`compile` from inside `step`.

**Compile errors** (the file cannot be played at all):
- `DuplicateSceneId(sceneId, chapterIndices)`
- `MissingStartScene(startSceneId)`
- `MissingNextScene(sceneId, choiceId, targetSceneId)`
- `MissingMergeSource(sceneId, mergeSourceId)` (Ф4.5 — a declared
  `merge_sources` entry names a scene that does not exist).
- `DuplicateSubroutineId(subroutineId)` (Ф4.7).
- `MissingSubroutine(subroutineId, caller… )` (Ф4.7 — a `Choice.call`
  or nested `SubroutineStep.call` names an unknown subroutine).
- `InvalidSubroutineCall(subroutineId, detail, caller… )` (Ф4.7 —
  missing/extra input arguments or unknown output names; type mismatches
  are `TypeError`s).
- `SubroutineCycle(path)` (Ф4.7 — `a -> b -> a` or self-call; recursion
  is not allowed in N6.base).

**Not compile errors:** unreachable scenes, unestablished items, dead
ends — those are `LintIssue`s (below). A file with a lint-only issue
must never prevent the player from opening it.

### `Engine.step(compiled, state, sceneId, choiceId, stepsInScene): StepResult`

The core transition. Order of checks:

1. Current scene exists → `Rejected(SceneNotFound)`.
2. Choice exists → `Rejected(ChoiceNotFound)`.
3. Collect all blockers (condition, gate) → `Rejected(Blocked(all))`.
4. Target scene exists → `Rejected(SceneNotFound)` — checked
   **before** applying effects.
5. Apply `choice.effects`.
6. If `choice.call` is present, run the subroutine **atomically**
   (`SubroutineExecutor`): a stack of local frames, nested calls write
   their outputs into the parent frame, the top-level frame writes into
   globals. Then `Success(state, currentScene, outcome)` (Ф3.5 added
   `outcome`; Ф4.7 adds the call). A runtime call failure is
   `Rejected(RejectReason.SubroutineFailure)` — structural, so compile
   normally prevents it.

**Scene effects are not applied by `step`.** They are applied by the
reader on first entry (`appliedSceneEffects` in progress). Doing it in
`step` would re-drain health on every re-entry — a data-loss bug.
Consequence: `Success.outcome` reflects only the choice's effects; the
reader applies the target scene's effects and then re-runs
`Engine.evaluateInvariants`.

**`stepsInScene`:** `null` means "unknown" → treated as 0 walked (safe
default: a caller that forgets to pass steps cannot bypass a gate).
Ignored for scenes without a gate.

### `StepResult` and `RejectReason`

```
StepResult.Success(state, currentScene, outcome: Outcome?)  ← Ф3.5
StepResult.Rejected(
  ChoiceNotFound | SceneNotFound          ← structural bug, log
  | Blocked(blockers: List<Blocker>)      ← UI shows disabled + reasons
)
Blocker.ConditionNotMet | GateNotPassed
```

`Blocked` carries **all** blockers, in order: persistent (condition)
before temporary (gate). UI (N4 / Ф4) shows them together on a
disabled choice — "requires sword; walk 100 more steps".

## Evaluator and EffectsApplier

Two objects, each with **one job**:

- `Evaluator.evaluate(condition, state): Boolean` — the single source
  of truth for `Condition`. Used by `Engine.step`, the reader UI, the
  analyzer, and (future) the JS runtime.
- `EffectsApplier.apply(state, effects): PlayerState` — the single
  source of truth for `Effect`. Applies in list order.

Unknown variables default to their zero-value (`0` / `false`). The
type checker (Ф2.2) is what reports "unknown variable" to the author;
the evaluator is not the place for that.

`Evaluator.isDead(state)` — the legacy hardcoded `health <= 0` check.
Since Ф3.5 the runtime uses `Engine.evaluateInvariants(adventure, state)`
instead: a non-empty `invariants` list replaces the fallback, and an
empty list preserves the old `health <= 0` behaviour.

`Evaluator.choiceState(choice, state): ChoiceState` (Ф4.4) is the
single source of truth for "can the player pick this choice, and if
not, why". It returns `Visible`, `Disabled(reason: Reason)` or `Hidden`;
the reader and the editor preview both use it. `Hidden` wins over
`Disabled` when both `visibilityCondition` and `condition` are false.

## Analyzer (`analyze/`)

### `Analyzer.reachable(compiled): ReachabilityReport`

BFS from `adventure.startScene` along `choice.nextScene` links.
Returns:

- `reachable: Set<SceneId>` — scenes the player can visit.
- `unreachable: List<SceneId>` — sorted; "written but never seen".
- `deadEnds: List<SceneId>` — reachable scenes with no choices.

### `Analyzer.lint(compiled): List<LintIssue>`

Each issue has `kind: LintKind`, `message`, `sceneId?`,
`severity: Severity`. Current checks (Ф1.6–Ф4.6):

| Kind | Severity | Meaning |
|------|----------|---------|
| `UnreachableScene` | WARNING | Not reachable from `startScene`. |
| `RemovingUnestablishedItem(var)` | WARNING | Reducing an ITEM/HEALTH that is never established. |
| `DeathSceneWithoutHealth` | WARNING | `death_scene` present, `health` never initialized/modified. |
| `ConditionOnUnestablishedFlag(flag)` | WARNING | `has_X` references a name that never appears anywhere. |
| `DeathWithoutDeathScene` | WARNING | `health` used, no `death_scene`. |
| `DeadEnd` | WARNING | Reachable terminal scene not marked `is_ending`. |
| `UnreachableInvariant(reason)` | WARNING | An invariant references a flag that is never set (Ф3.5). |
| `DeadCondition(condition, reason)` | WARNING | Contradictory / out-of-bounds / combined-numeric condition (Ф3.6). |
| `MergeConflict(reason, source?)` | WARNING | Merge declaration does not match the graph (Ф4.6). |
| `EndingSceneWithChoices(sceneId)` | ERROR | `is_ending: true` + non-empty choices. |

`lint()` includes the dead-condition check and the merge-conflict
check. `Analyzer.deadConditions(compiled)` and
`Analyzer.checkMerges(compiled)` are also public so the editor's
realtime linter (Ф9.2) can call them on their own.

Only `ERROR` blocks the reader from loading the file. Everything else
opens with a "N warnings — continue?" dialog once per fingerprint.

The analyzer returns issues sorted by (scene id, message) for stable
output. `test_adventure.json` is the reference: it must be lint-clean
under current rules (test `lint is clean on test_adventure.json`).

**Deferred to later phases:**
- **Ф5:** state compatibility between merge branches — needs the
  per-branch `StateDelta` model, not just graph reachability.
- **Ф4.10:** merge editing UI (toggle, source picker, map join).

**Type errors are not lint issues.** `TypeChecker` (Ф2.2, wired into
`JsonToIr.parse` in Ф2.3) rejects unknown variables and wrong types
**before** `Analyzer.lint` runs. The two error classes have different
lifecycles: type errors block the parse pipeline
(`ParseResult.Failure.typeErrors`), lint issues are reported on a
successfully-parsed file. See [`engine-types.md`](./engine-types.md)
and the "Error hierarchy" section above.

## Error hierarchy

```
ParseResult.Failure  (parse/ParseResult.kt:  the file cannot be opened)
├─ errors:     List<ParseError>    ← JSON syntax / structure / condition syntax
└─ typeErrors: List<TypeError>     ← unknown variables, wrong types (Ф2.3)

CompileError       (CompileResult.kt:   indexes cannot be built)
├─ DuplicateSceneId
├─ MissingStartScene
├─ MissingNextScene
├─ MissingMergeSource        ← Ф4.5: declared merge branch does not exist
├─ DuplicateSubroutineId     ← Ф4.7
├─ MissingSubroutine         ← Ф4.7: call to unknown id
├─ InvalidSubroutineCall     ← Ф4.7: arity/name mismatch
└─ SubroutineCycle           ← Ф4.7: recursion is not allowed in N6.base

LintIssue          (analyze/:   file plays, but is semantically wrong)
├─ Severity.ERROR   ← reader refuses to open
├─ Severity.WARNING ← reader warns, player decides
└─ Severity.INFO
```
Four layers, four questions:

Can I turn this into IR? (ParseError)

Do all variable references make sense? (TypeError)

Can I build runtime indexes? (CompileError)

Is the IR coherent? (LintIssue)

Two fields in ParseResult.Failure, not one. Parse errors and type
errors come from different layers of the pipeline (parser vs type
checker) and carry different structured data: ParseError has JSON
paths and condition fragments; TypeError has variable names and
types. Merging them would blur the I3 boundary between "the file
cannot be parsed" and "the file parses, but its variable references
are wrong". Two fields keep the boundary visible in the type system,
and they are mutually exclusive (enforced in Failure.init): the
parser stops at the first failing stage — type checking runs only on
a fully parsed IR (Ф2.3 / B1 decision, 2026-11-12).

Same boundary fixed in Ф1.3.4.1: putting a semantic check in the
parser makes both harder to test and blurs the error message the
author sees.

## Merge points (Ф4.5)

**Status:** shipped in IR + runtime + compile checks + analyzer (Ф4.6);
editor UI follows in Ф4.10.

A **merge point** is a scene where two or more narrative branches
deliberately converge. The IR represents it as an **explicit scene
attribute**, not a separate `MergeNode` (the checklist allows either):

```json
{
  "id": "after_fork",
  "text": "...",
  "merge": true,
  "merge_sources": ["left_path", "right_path"]
}
```

- `Scene.isMerge: Boolean` (JSON `merge`, default `false`) — "this scene
  is a declared convergence point". It is **metadata**; it does not
  change how the scene is rendered or stepped.
- `Scene.mergeSources: List<SceneId>` (JSON `merge_sources`, default
  empty) — the branches the author says lead here. Empty is allowed: a
  merge scene without a declaration still has incoming edges in the
  `nextScene` graph; the analyzer (Ф4.6) can collect them.

### Runtime: delta is transferred implicitly (decision B1 / C1)

There is **no runtime "merge operation"**. `Engine.step` applies the
chosen branch's `choice.effects` before the transition; the reader
applies the branch scene's `scene.effects` on first entry. The
`PlayerState` that arrives at the merge scene is therefore already the
pre-branch state plus the branch's delta. Nothing is copied, diffed or
merged at the merge point itself.

This is deliberate: the current state model is a single `PlayerState`,
not per-branch deltas. True branch tracking belongs to the delta/save
model in Ф5; introducing it here would force a save-format rewrite for
no gameplay benefit today. The DoD property "two branches with different
state changes → merge transfers delta" is pinned by
`EngineStepTest.merge point receives accumulated delta from either
branch`.

### Validation split

- **Compile (`Engine.compile`)** — every id in `merge_sources` must
  exist (`CompileError.MissingMergeSource`). This is a cross-scene
  reference, same layer as `MissingNextScene`; the parser cannot check
  it while building one scene.
- **Analyzer (Ф4.6)** — `Analyzer.checkMerges` reports three
  `MergeConflict` warnings: `NoIncomingBranches` (`merge: true`, but no
  choice leads here), `SourceDoesNotLeadHere` (a declared source has no
  choice pointing at the merge), and `SourceNotReachable` (a declared
  source exists and leads here but cannot be reached from
  `start_scene`; reported only when the merge itself is reachable, so
  `UnreachableScene` is not duplicated). State compatibility
  ("incompatible states") needs Ф5 deltas and is not analysed yet.
- **Editor (Ф4.10)** — visual join on the map; toggle / source editing.
  Until then `merge` / `mergeSources` only round-trip through
  `:app/data/Scene` and `EditorScene` so a hand-edited file is not lost
  on save; the editor's validation dialog already shows the three
  `MergeConflict` warnings through `Analyzer.lint`.
- **Reference sample (Ф4.11)** — `test_adventure.json` gains a real
  merge example together with templates, disabled choices and a
  subroutine.

No version bump: both fields are optional with defaults `false` /
`[]`, so the migration is the identity (same reasoning as `variables`,
`invariants`, `choice_templates`).

## Subroutines (Ф4.7)

**Status:** engine shipped — IR, JSON parsing, compile checks, type
checking and `Engine.step` execution; editor UI + JSON/draft/snapshot
round-trip shipped in Ф4.8. Reader integration (Ф4.9) and the
full N6 integration/sample (Ф4.10 / Ф4.11) remain. The Compose reader
currently applies effects directly instead of calling `Engine.step`, so
a call declared today is validated and saved but does not run in the
reader until Ф4.9 wires it in.

**Editor (Ф4.8).** The toolbar opens a dedicated "Подпрограммы"
destination: a list of subroutines plus a form for `id`, typed
inputs/outputs and a flat table of guarded body steps. Each step edits
its condition, effects (reusing the tag dialog) and optional nested call.
From a choice, "Подпрограмма:" opens the shared
`SubroutineCallDialog`; from a step, the same dialog binds local names.
The dialog hides blank-input mappings and empty ids, but deliberately
does not hide type errors — those appear in "Проверить" through the
engine. `subroutines` and `Choice.call` round-trip through
`:app/data/Adventure`, editor drafts and undo snapshots, so open → save
does not lose them.

A **subroutine** is a reusable, **atomic** procedure: it runs to
completion inside one `Engine.step` call. The player never sees
intermediate screens, saves cannot happen mid-call, and undo returns to
the state before the invoking choice. This preserves reading pace and
keeps the save format unchanged. Player-visible multi-step content is a
different feature (reusable scenes).

```json
{
  "id": "consume",
  "inputs":  [{"name": "item", "type": "item_count"},
              {"name": "health", "type": "int_min", "min": 0}],
  "outputs": [{"name": "item", "type": "item_count"},
              {"name": "health", "type": "int_min", "min": 0}],
  "body": [
    {
      "condition": "item > 0",
      "modify_stats": {"item": -1, "health": 5}
    }
  ]
}
```

Call from a choice (`next_scene` is the **return target**, use the same
scene id to stay in place):

```json
{
  "text": "Выпить зелье",
  "next_scene": "start",
  "call": {
    "subroutine_id": "consume",
    "args":    {"item": "potion", "health": "health"},
    "outputs": {"item": "potion", "health": "health"}
  }
}
```

### Local frame

- A call creates a private `PlayerState`-backed frame. `inputs` are
  copied **into** it; `outputs` start at their type defaults and are
  copied **out** on return. A name in both lists is an in-out parameter:
  it starts with the caller's value and is written back (types must
  match).
- The body sees **only** its parameters. It cannot read or write
  `Adventure.variables` directly; anything needed must be an input,
  anything changed must be an output. This is what makes a subroutine a
  predictable contract.
- On a `Choice`, argument sources and output targets are global variable
  names. Inside a body, they are the enclosing frame's local names.
  Nested calls therefore compose frames without reaching into globals.

### Flat guarded steps

`SubroutineStep` is a flat list, not a nested `if` tree:

1. If `condition` is present and false, skip the step.
2. Apply `effects` to the frame in order.
3. If `call` is present, push a child frame. On return, the child's
   outputs are written into the parent's locals; the parent resumes at
   the next step.

An `else` branch is a following step with the negated condition. This is
deliberately table-friendly for the Ф4.8 editor. No loops, nested
control flow or arbitrary local variables — those belong to Ф13
`Procedure`. Effect deltas are literals: an input parameter can drive a
condition, but there is no "add the value of X" effect yet. The common
in-out pattern (`item > 0` → `item -= 1`, `health += 5`) is fully
supported.

### Execution and validation split

- **Parser (`JsonToIr`)** — structural JSON: blank ids/names,
  duplicate parameter names, in-out type mismatch, unparseable
  conditions, blank call ids/argument names.
- **Compiler (`Engine.compile`)** — cross references and arity:
  unknown subroutine ids, missing/extra arguments, unknown output
  names, duplicate ids, and call-graph cycles
  (`CompileError.SubroutineCycle`). Recursion is forbidden in N6.base.
- **TypeChecker** — parameter/call types: top-level args/targets against
  the global table, nested args/targets against the local frame,
  writes to input-only parameters, `ItemList` parameters (unsupported in
  N6.base). Body errors are wrapped in `TypeError.InSubroutine`; call
  type mismatches are `TypeError.InvalidSubroutineSignature`.
- **Runtime (`SubroutineExecutor`)** — an explicit frame stack
  (`ArrayDeque<Frame>`) with a hard `MAX_DEPTH = 64` guard. Failures are
  `RejectReason.SubroutineFailure` (structural bug; compile should have
  caught it).

No version bump: `Adventure.subroutines` defaults to `[]` and
`Choice.call` to `null`, so existing files are unchanged (same reasoning
as `variables`, `invariants`, `choice_templates`, `merge`).

**User benefit.** Authors get reusable mechanical blocks (consume an
item, apply damage, run a common check) with explicit typed inputs and
outputs, conditions and nested composition — without adding screens for
the player, without changing saves, and with compile/type errors before
the adventure can be played. The local-frame contract prevents a shared
procedure from silently mutating unrelated global state.

## Choice templates (Ф4.2)

**Status:** shipped (Ф4.1–Ф4.3.2b); deferred items listed below.

An author can define a **choice template** once and reuse it in any number
of scenes with different arguments. The template is declared in
`Adventure.choiceTemplates` (JSON `choice_templates`); instantiation is
done by `applyTemplate`.

### Design: expansion

When a template is instantiated — programmatically via `applyTemplate`,
or by the editor (Ф4.3.2b), which writes the expanded choice plus
`template_ref` metadata — the resulting `Choice` is **fully expanded**.
Its `text`, `condition`, `visibilityCondition`, and `effects` are filled
in with substituted values. The runtime (`Engine.step`, `Evaluator`,
`EffectsApplier`) and the analyzer (`Analyzer.lint`) see only expanded
choices; they never look at `Choice.templateRef` or
`Adventure.choiceTemplates`.

`Choice.templateRef: TemplateRef?` records the source (template id + args)
for the editor's benefit (Ф4.3). It is metadata; the gameplay-relevant
content is already in the expanded fields.

**Why expansion over a live `TemplateRef` (decision A1).** A
`TemplateRef`-based `Choice` would force every consumer (evaluator,
effects applier, analyzer, save/load) to be template-aware. That is a large
surface for a feature whose main value is authoring convenience. Expansion
keeps the runtime simple and the save format flat. The trade-off: when an
author edits a template, existing expanded choices do not auto-update.
An explicit "update all uses" action would use `templateRef` to find the
affected choices; it is **not implemented** and not tracked as a
follow-up (it was not part of the Ф4.3 DoD).

### Substitution semantics (decision B1)

`applyTemplate(template, args, choiceId)` performs two kinds of
substitution. Args are `Map<String, String>` — parameter name → actual
variable name.

1. **Text** — `{paramName}` placeholders in `template.text` are replaced
   with the corresponding arg value. Example: `"Use {itemId}"` +
   `args = {itemId: "potion"}` → `"Use potion"`. Braces make parameter
   references unambiguous against ordinary prose.
2. **AST name slots** — `Condition.Has(name)`, `Condition.VarRef(name)`,
   `Condition.Compare(varName)`, `Condition.InRange(varName)`,
   `Effect.SetFlag(name)`, `Effect.RemoveFlag(name)`,
   `Effect.ModifyStat(name)`, `Effect.Set(name)` are checked for **exact**
   parameter-name matches. If the string equals a parameter name, it is
   replaced with the arg value; otherwise it is left as-is (a reference to
   a global variable). No braces here — an AST name slot is either a
   parameter or a global, and exact match is unambiguous.

`value` / `delta` / `min` / `max` slots (all `Int`) are **not**
parameterizable. Integer parameterization requires a placeholder syntax for
ints and is out of scope for Ф4.2; it can be added later if authors ask.

`nextScene` has two modes:

- **Normal `SceneId`** — copied verbatim. Parameterizing the target
  through args is out of scope.
- **`@self` sentinel** (`ChoiceTemplate.SELF` = `SceneId("@self")`) —
  "the scene where this template is applied". Resolved by
  `applyTemplate` from its `currentSceneId` argument. The canonical case
  is "use item" / "drink potion": the choice applies effects in place
  without moving the player. `@` is stripped by the editor's
  `transliterate`, so no real scene id can collide with `@self`. A
  non-template `Choice` with `next_scene: "@self"` is an ordinary
  dangling reference (`CompileError.MissingNextScene`) — `@self` is a
  template-only marker.
### Editor tracking

`Choice.templateRef` is preserved on the expanded choice and
round-trips through `:app/data/Choice.template_ref` (Ф4.3.2b). Without
it, the editor could not distinguish "this choice was written by hand to
look like the template" from "this choice came from the template".

Planned uses (not implemented today):

- Show "this choice uses template X" on the choice card — currently the
  metadata is stored but not rendered.
- **"Update all uses"** when a template is edited: find every choice with
  `templateRef.templateId == X`, re-run `applyTemplate`, replace. This
  was proposed as 4.3.3 but is **not** in the Ф4.3 DoD and has no
  follow-up tracked.

### Editor UI (Ф4.3.2a)

**Status:** first slice shipped.

The template list screen (`TemplateListFragment`) is opened from the
editor's "📦 Шаблоны" toolbar button. It lists templates as compact
rows (id mono, text bold, "N параметров · M эффектов" summary). Row
click opens the edit dialog; the `✕` button deletes with confirmation.

The edit dialog holds all template fields in one place:
`id`, `text`, two conditions, `nextScene`, the parameter sub-list,
and the effect sub-list. Parameters reuse `item_editor_variable.xml`
(same layout as `VariablesAdapter`); effects reuse `renderTagRow` from
`EditorHelpers`. The positive button is disabled until `id`, `text`,
and `nextSceneId` are non-empty (`F2` validation).

`nextScene` is picked via a search dialog (`ScenePickerDialog`) — not
a `Spinner`. Search matches `id` or `title`, case-insensitive,
debounced 200ms; empty query hides the list (never renders 500
scenes at once). Special rows at the top: `@self` (only for the
template editor, `allowSelf = true`) and "create new scene".
`ScenePickerDialog` is reusable — a future refactor of
`EditorChoice.nextSceneId` (separate batch) can use the same dialog.

**Apply to a scene (Ф4.3.2b).** Each scene card has "📦 Из шаблона".
The flow is: `TemplatePickerDialog` (card list, empty state) →
`TemplateArgsDialog` (one row per parameter, typed hint, positive button
disabled until all are filled) → `AdventureEditorViewModel.applyTemplateToChoice`
(engine `applyTemplate`) → the expanded `EditorChoice` is appended with
`templateUid` / `templateArgs` metadata. The reader plays the expanded
text/condition/effects; it never sees the template.

**Not implemented.** "Update all uses" on template edit (no follow-up
tracked), and the template badge on a choice card.

### Deferred

- **`TypeChecker.checkChoiceTemplate`** (Ф4.2.2): validate templates
  against a combined scope (`parameters + globalVariables`). Until then
  a template's own conditions/effects are not type-checked, only the
  expanded choices are.
- **Placeholder validation** in `template.text`: `{foo}` with no declared
  `foo` parameter survives expansion literally. The realtime linter
  (Ф9.2) is the intended home.
- **JSON-level `template_ref` re-expansion**: the editor and the reader
  treat `template_ref` as metadata; `:engine` does not re-apply the
  template on load. A hand-edited expanded choice is played as written.

## Testing strategy

- `RealAdventureTest` — parses the actual `test_adventure.json`
  shipped to every new user.
- `GoldenIrTest` — parses `test_adventure.json`, serializes the
  result, compares against `golden_ir.json` semantically. Regenerated
  via `./gradlew :engine:updateGolden` after an intentional IR change.
- `SchemaFingerprintTest` — pins the **names** of every serialized
  field. Catches added/removed fields with defaults (which
  `GoldenIrTest` misses due to `encodeDefaults = false`).
- `JsonToIrTest` — unit tests for the mapper: each error case, each
  migration, each boundary (`typo in flag name parses as Has — type
  check is F2`).
- `ConditionParserTest` — unit tests for the condition grammar.
- `EngineCompileTest` / `EngineStepTest` — runtime compile errors and
  transitions, including `MissingMergeSource`, the Ф4.5 delta test
  (two branches with different effects arrive at the same merge scene
  with their respective state), and Ф4.7 (one subroutine called from two
  scenes, nested frames, guarded step, invariants evaluated after
  outputs).
- `EvaluatorTest` / `EffectsApplierTest` — the two single-source-of-
  truth objects, plus `Evaluator.choiceState` (Ф4.4).
- `AnalyzerTest` — reachability and each `LintKind`, including the
  Ф4.6 merge-conflict reasons.
- `TypeCheckerTest` — global type errors plus Ф4.7 subroutine scopes:
  inputs/outputs are local, globals are invisible inside a body,
  input-only writes are rejected, top-level and nested call types are
  checked.
- `AdventureDtoTest` — DTO deserialization edge cases.

CI runs `./gradlew :engine:test` on every push and PR. Test reports
are uploaded as `engine-test-reports`.

# Engine conditions

**Status:** stable. Describes the condition grammar introduced in
Ф3.2 (N7.base, 2026-11-13). Changes here are breaking for every adventure
file — extend with care.

This document is the reference for **condition strings** in the adventure
JSON: the syntax that authors write in `"condition": "..."`, how the
parser turns it into a `Condition` AST, how the writer round-trips it
back, and what the type checker validates on top.

It is the companion to:
- [`engine-types.md`](./engine-types.md) — the variable type system;
  `has_X`, `Compare`, `InRange` in a condition are typed against the
  declared `VarType`s.
- [`engine-architecture.md`](./engine-architecture.md) — the module
  structure; `ConditionParser` (this doc) and `TypeChecker` (types doc)
  are two of its four pipeline stages.

## Grammar (Ф3.2 / N7.base)

```
expr    = or
or      = and ("||" and)*
and     = not ("&&" not)*
not     = "!" not | primary
primary = "(" expr ")"
        | "true"
        | "false"
        | "has_" IDENT
        | IDENT "in" INT ".." INT
        | IDENT COMPARE_OP INT

COMPARE_OP = ">=" | "<=" | "==" | "!=" | ">" | "<"
```

Whitespace between tokens is ignored. IDENT is any string without the
reserved characters (§"Reserved characters") — it may contain spaces,
so `has_my flag` is `Has("my flag")`.

**Precedence** (highest to lowest): `!` > `&&` > `||`. `&&` and `||` are
**left-associative**: `a && b && c` parses as `And(And(a, b), c)`.
Parentheses override precedence.

## Leaves

### `has_X` — Bool flag

`has_sword` → `Condition.Has("sword")`, true iff the player's
`flags` contains `"sword"` at evaluation time.

**Only for `Bool` variables.** A `has_` on an `ItemCount` / `IntMin` /
`IntRange` variable is a **type error** (`TypeError.HasOnNonBool`)
with a fix hint (`use 'sword > 0' instead`). The parser does not enforce
this — the type checker (Ф2.2) does.

`has_` is the **canonical** syntax for Bool variables. There is no bare
`sword` variable reference — see §"What is not supported (`VarRef`)" .

### `X <op> N` — comparison

`health >= 50` → `Condition.Compare("health", GE, 50)`, true iff
`stats["health"] >= 50`. `X` must be numeric (`Integer`, `IntMin`,
`IntRange`, `ItemCount`); `N` is a signed integer.

Operators: `>=`, `<=`, `==`, `!=`, `>`, `<`. Two-character operators are
parsed first, so `>=` is not consumed as `>` followed by `=`.
Variable names may contain spaces (`my stat > 0`); trailing `/ leading`
whitespace is trimmed.

### `X in A..B` — inclusive range

`health in 50..100` → `Condition.InRange("health", 50, 100)`, true iff
`stats["health"]` is in the inclusive range `[50, 100]`. `X` must be
numeric. `A` and `B` are signed integers. Spaces around `..` are
tolerated (`health in 50 .. 100`).

### `true` / `false` — literal

`Condition.Literal(true)` / `Condition.Literal(false)`.

Rarely useful directly — the author usually writes a condition that
**always holds** by using `has_some_permanent_flag` from initial state.
`Literal` is useful in generated IR and in future AST optimization (e.g.
`Literal(true) && X` → `X`). It is **not** a shortcut for "empty
condition": an empty `"condition"` string is an error; the choice must
either omit the field (meaning "always available") or set an explicit
condition.

## Operators

### `&&` — logical AND

`A && B` → `Condition.And(A, B)`. Short-circuits left-to-right in
`Evaluator.evaluate`: if `A` is false, `B` is not evaluated.

### `||` — logical OR

`A || B` → `Condition.Or(A, B)`. Short-circuits left-to-right.

### `!` — logical NOT

`!A` → `Condition.Not(A)`. **Unary prefix.** `!has_sword` is
`Not(Has("sword"))`. `!!has_x` is `Not(Not(Has("x")))`. `!(A && B)` is
`Not(And(A, B))`.

**What `!` binds to.** `!` applies to its immediate `primary` — the
"not" production recurses right, so `!A && B` is `And(Not(A), B)`, not
`Not(And(A, B))` (the second requires explicit parentheses). Likewise
`!health > 5` parses as `Not(Compare(health, GT, 5))`, **not**
`Compare(Not(health), GT, 5)` — the latter would be a type error
(`Not` returns Bool, `Compare` requires numeric), and the author almost
certainly meant "health is not greater than 5". If you want to negate a
comparison, either form works — `!(health > 5)` and `!health > 5` are
the **same AST**. Use the parenthesized form if you want to be
explicit.

## Precedence table

| Level | Operators | Associativity |
|---|---|---|
| 1 (highest) | `!` | right (prefix) |
| 2 | `&&` | left |
| 3 (lowest) | `\|\|` | left |

Examples:

| Input | Parsed as |
|---|---|
| `a && b \|\| c` | `Or(And(a, b), c)` — `&&` binds tighter |
| `a \|\| b && c` | `Or(a, And(b, c))` |
| `(a \|\| b) && c` | `And(Or(a, b), c)` — parentheses override |
| `!a && b` | `And(Not(a), b)` |
| `!(a && b)` | `Not(And(a, b))` |
| `a && b && c` | `And(And(a, b), c)` — left-associative |
| `a \|\| b \|\| c` | `Or(Or(a, b), c)` |

## Round-trip with `ConditionWriter`

The writer (`engine/.../parse/ConditionWriter.kt`, Ф3.1.2) produces a
**canonical** string for any `Condition`. The contract is:

```
parse(write(c)) == c    (structurally)
```

for the variants the parser can produce. As of Ф3.2, the supported set
is:

| Condition variant | Round-trips |
|---|---|
| `Has`, `Compare` (all 6 ops), `InRange` | ✅ |
| `Not(Has)` | ✅ |
| `And`, `Or` (any nesting) | ✅ |
| `Not(And)`, `Not(Or)`, `Not(Compare)`, `Not(InRange)`, `!!` | ✅ |
| `Literal(true)` / `Literal(false)` | ✅ |
| `VarRef` | ❌ — not produced by the parser (§below) |

The writer's canonical form uses **minimal brackets**: `a && b || c` is
`Or(And(a, b), c)` without brackets on the `And`; brackets appear only
where precedence requires them. A consequence: `parse(write(c)) == c`
holds, but `write(parse(s)) == s` does **not** — the writer normalizes
whitespace and adds only necessary brackets. This is intentional; the
canonical form is what the editor (Ф9.2) saves back to disk.

## Global invariants

**Status (Ф3.5).** Besides `"condition"` on choices, conditions are
used in a second place: `"invariants"` — global rules that fire
regardless of which scene the player is in.

```json
{
  "invariants": [
    { "condition": "health <= 0", "outcome": "death" },
    { "condition": "stamina <= 0 && has_poison", "outcome": "death" }
  ]
}
```

### Semantics

`Invariant(condition, outcome)` fires **when `condition` holds**,
evaluated after every step (choice effects) and after every scene
entry (scene effects). The first matching invariant in the list wins;
later invariants are not evaluated. The only outcome today is
`"death"` (`Outcome.Death`): the reader shows the death screen.

### Fallback when `invariants` is absent or empty

The runtime falls back to the **pre-Ф3.5** hardcoded rule
`health <= 0 => death`. This preserves behaviour for every old file
and for authors who do not declare invariants. A file with a
**non-empty** `invariants` list **replaces** the fallback entirely —
the author's rules are authoritative. If the author wants
`health <= 0 → death` **plus** `stamina <= 0 → death`, both must be
declared; the fallback will not add the health rule automatically.

### Why a list

Multiple invariants model different failure modes that coexist:
- the classic `health <= 0 → death` (always a good default for
  adventure games);
- a poison timer `has_poison && turn_count > 10 → death`;
- (future, Ф12) `roll(1d6) == 1 && has_trap → death`.

Future phases (Ф12 RNG, Ф13 combat, Ф15 external outcomes) will add
**outcome variants** (not "each mechanic is a new invariant") — the
list mechanism is already generic; the outcome is what grows.

### Limits (Ф3.5)

- **Numeric unreachability is not checked yet.** `Invariant(health <
  -100)` where `health` is `IntMin(0)` is dead code — `Analyzer` does
  not report it. Ф3.6 (`Analyzer.deadConditions`) will.
- **Flag unreachability is checked.** `Invariant(has_unknown_flag,
  ...)` where `unknown_flag` is never set → `LintKind.UnreachableInvariant`
  (WARNING, non-blocking, sceneId = null).
- **Order matters.** An author writing `[A, B]` where both might
  fire simultaneously sees `A`'s outcome (first match). Put specific
  rules before generic ones; the analyzer does not enforce order.

## Dead conditions

**Status (Ф3.6).** The analyzer
(`Analyzer.deadConditions`, also included in `Analyzer.lint`) detects
conditions that can **never** be true.

### What is detected

1. **Contradictory conjunction** — `has_sword && !has_sword`. Any
   `And`-tree containing both a subexpression `A` and its negation
   `!A`. Nested: `(a && b) && !a` — caught (`a` is a conjunct of the
   left side, and `!a` is on the right).

2. **Numeric out-of-bounds** — `health > 100` where `health` is
   `IntRange(0, 100)`. The condition's required range has no overlap
   with the declared type.

3. **Numeric combined contradiction** — `health >= 50 && health <= 30`.
   Both constraints on the same variable, no common value.

### What is NOT detected (deferred)

- **`Or`-tautologies** — `!(a || b) && a` requires normalization of
  `Or` into `And` of negations; the current check treats `Or` as
  opaque.
- **Cross-variable arithmetic** — `gold + health > 1000`; `Condition`
  has no arithmetic today. When Ф3.2 extends `Condition` with arithmetic,
  this analyzer will need a matching extension.
- **Path-sensitive deadness** — a condition that is dead *because*
  the state it checks is unreachable on any play-through path. The
  flag side is covered by `ConditionOnUnestablishedFlag` (existential:
  "flag is never set anywhere"); the numeric and structural side is
  a future extension.
- **`Integer` variables** — no declared bounds, any `Int` is
  representable; the numeric check skips them. `ItemCount` is treated
  as `IntMin(0)`, `IntMin` as `[min, Int.MAX_VALUE]`.

### Where it applies

- Every `"condition"` on a `choice` in every scene.
- Every `"condition"` in an `"invariants"` entry.

Nothing else carries a `Condition` (effects are not conditions).

### Severity

`WARNING`. The adventure opens and plays; the affected choice is
never available, or the affected invariant never fires. Non-blocking —
the author sees the warning in the editor's validation dialog and
decides whether to fix the condition or leave it as a placeholder.

### Example editor message

```
Предупреждений: 2
• Недостижимое условие — Condition can never be true
  (choice 'Go north' in scene 'crossroads'): contains both 'has_sword'
  and its negation in the same conjunction. Remove one side or check
  for a typo.
• Недостижимое условие — Condition can never be true
  (invariant #0): requires 'health' in '101..', but 'health' is
  IntRange(0..100).
```

The English `reason` (from `LintKind.DeadCondition.reason`) is
embedded into `LintIssue.message`; `StoryValidator.titleFor` maps the
issue kind to a Russian title. Same pattern as all other `LintKind`
variants.

## What is not supported (`VarRef`)

A bare identifier — `"health"`, `"sword"` — is **not** a valid condition.
The parser rejects it with `ConditionError` ("unrecognized syntax"). Only
`has_X` is accepted for Bool variable references.

**Why not `VarRef` now.** Accepting `"health"` as `VarRef("health")` is
a change that needs a plan for `has_X` disambiguation: if a variable is
named `has_seen`, the author has no way to reference it — the parser
would always see `Has("seen")`. This is a solvable problem (`has_` prefix
reserved, or explicit syntax), but it is **out of scope for Ф3.2**.

`Condition.VarRef` **exists in the AST** (Ф3.1) and is handled by
`Evaluator`, `TypeChecker` (no-op), `TypeInference`, `Analyzer`,
`ConditionWriter` (writes as bare name). Adding the parser branch is a
~30-line change in `ConditionParser` + ~15 lines in `TypeChecker`
(`TypeError.VarRefOnNonBool`) + the `has_`-prefix reservation. It is
tracked as a separate roadmap item — see
[`checklist-tracker.md`](./checklist-tracker.md) Appendix B ("VarRef +
has_X deprecation"). It will land when the first author requests "why
can't I write `sword && key`?" — not before.

## Reserved characters

The following characters are **part of the condition syntax** and cannot
appear in a variable or flag name:

```
&  |  !  <  >  =  (  )
```

A name containing one of these → `ConditionError` with a fix hint.
In particular, `has_sword && health` is **not** `Has("sword && health")`
(an old bug fixed in Ф1.3.3.2); the parser splits on `&&`, parses the
left as `Has("sword")`, then rejects the right (`"health"` is a bare
identifier — see §"What is not supported"). The author who meant
"has_sword AND has_health" writes `has_sword && has_health`.

## Common mistakes

| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `has_sword && health` fails to parse | `health` is a bare identifier, no `VarRef` support | Use `has_sword && health > 0` or `has_sword && has_health` |
| `has_sword` on an `ItemCount` variable; parse OK, typechecker error | `has_X` requires `Bool` | Use `sword > 0` |
| `!(health > 5)` vs `!health > 5` — same AST | `!` binds to `Compare` as a whole | Both are `Not(Compare(health, GT, 5))`; write whichever reads better |
| `"a & b"` fails to parse | `&` is not a valid operator | Use `&&` |
| `"a | b"` fails to parse | `\|` is not a valid operator | Use `\|\|` |
| `"a || "` fails to parse | Empty operand | Remove the trailing `\|\|`, or supply a right side |
| `"(a && b"` fails to parse | Unbalanced parentheses | Add the closing `)` |

  (`has_X` / `Compare` / `InRange` are typed against `VarType`).

# Engine types

**Status:** stable. Describes the type system introduced in Ф2 (2.1–2.8) of
[`checklist-tracker.md`](./checklist-tracker.md). Changes here are breaking
for every adventure file — extend with care.

This document is the reference for the **variable type system**: how
variables are declared, how the parser and type checker use them, what the
author must know when writing conditions and effects, and what is
enforced at runtime versus checked only at parse time.

It is the companion to [`engine-architecture.md`](./engine-architecture.md)
(which describes the module at a structural level) and to
[`gamebook-mechanics-coverage.md`](./gamebook-mechanics-coverage.md) (which
maps mechanics to phases, not types).

## Why a type system

Before Ф2, the author wrote:

```json
"choices": [{"text": "Enter", "condition": "has_sword", "next_scene": "b"}]
```

The parser accepted `has_sword`. At runtime, `has_sword` looked at the
player's flags. But `sword` was declared as an **item** — it lived in
`stats`, never in `flags`. So `has_sword` was always `false`, the button
was always disabled, and the author saw no error — just a "grey button
that should be active".

Ф2 closes this gap in two layers:

1. **Type checker** (parse time) — every reference is checked against
   the declared type: `has_sword` on `ItemCount` is a **blocking error**
   with a fix hint (`use 'sword > 0' instead`).
2. **Declarations** — the author states every variable's type in
   `"variables"`; there is no more "inferred from usage". Fallback mode
   exists for backward compatibility (see [Fallback](#fallback)).

## Where variables live

Variables are declared once in `"variables"` at the top of the adventure
file, and referenced by name from conditions (`"condition": "sword > 0"`)
and effects (`"modify_stats": {"sword": -1}`).

```json
{
  "title": "Example",
  "variables": {
    "health":    { "type": "int_range", "min": 0, "max": 100 },
    "sword":     { "type": "item_count" },
    "has_key":   { "type": "bool" },
    "gold":      { "type": "int_min", "min": 0 },
    "score":     { "type": "int" },
    "documents": { "type": "item_list" }
  },
  "initial_state": {
    "flags": ["has_key"],
    "stats": { "health": 100, "sword": 1, "gold": 10, "score": 0 }
  },
  "chapters": [  ]
}
```

In the IR, `"variables"` becomes `Adventure.variables: Map<String, VarDecl>`,
where each entry is `VarDecl(name, type)` with `type: VarType`.

`VarDecl.name` and the map key are identical by construction; the IR keeps
both so that `inferTypes` (see [Migration](#migration)) can return a
`Map<String, VarDecl>` directly comparable to the file's `variables`.

## The six types

| Type | JSON | IR | Default | Bounds (semantic) | When to use |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Bool** | `{"type": "bool"}` | `VarType.Bool` | `false` | n/a | Flags: "has sword", "met wizard". Referenced from `has_X` / `!has_X`, set with `set_flags` / `remove_flags`. |
| **Integer** | `{"type": "int"}` | `VarType.Integer` | `0` | none | Unbounded numbers: score, computed totals. Use when the variable genuinely has no min/max (rare). |
| **IntMin** | `{"type": "int_min", "min": N}` | `VarType.IntMin(N)` | `min` | `>= N` | Resources that cannot go negative but have no upper bound: gold, stamina, ammo, health (if the story never caps it). **Most common numeric type.** |
| **IntRange** | `{"type": "int_range", "min": A, "max": B}` | `VarType.IntRange(A, B)` | `min` | `[A, B]` | Bounded stats: health 0..100, skill 1..12, endurance 20..30, day 0..30. |
| **ItemCount** | `{"type": "item_count"}` | `VarType.ItemCount` | `0` | `>= 0` | Inventory items, stackable potions, arrows. Same runtime as `IntMin(0)`, kept distinct so the type checker can tell "how many" from "any number". |
| **ItemList** | `{"type": "item_list"}` | `VarType.ItemList` | `emptyList()` | n/a | Unordered collection of item identifiers. Reserved for Ф4 (N3, choice templates); today the type checker only knows "non-numeric". |

### Choosing between the numeric types

Ask two questions about the variable:

1. **Can it go below zero?** If no → `IntMin(0)` or `IntRange(0, N)`.
2. **Can it ever exceed some N?** If no → `IntMin(min)` (or `Integer` if
   the lower bound also doesn't apply). If yes → `IntRange(min, max)`.

For example:

| Variable | Question 1 | Question 2 | Type |
|---|---|---|---|
| `health` (0..100) | yes | yes (100) | `IntRange(0, 100)` |
| `gold` | yes | no | `IntMin(0)` |
| `score` | no | no | `Integer` |
| `skill` (1..12) | yes (1) | yes (12) | `IntRange(1, 12)` |
| `potion` (count) | yes | no | `ItemCount` |

**Rule of thumb: prefer `IntMin(0)` over `Integer`.** Most game variables
are resources that cannot go negative. `Integer` (no lower bound) should be
rare — it is useful for scores that may become negative after penalties,
and for variables whose bounds the author genuinely does not want to commit
to.

### Why three numeric variants, not one

- **Clarity at the JSON level.** `{"type": "int_range", "min": 0, "max": 100}`
  reads immediately as "health-like stat"; `{"type": "int"}` reads as
  "any integer". Six explicit variants make the intent visible.
- **Type-checker hints.** A `Compare` on `IntRange` can be validated
  against the range in a future phase (Ф3.6, `Analyzer.deadConditions`);
  this is impossible if all numerics collapse to one type.
- **Clamp policy.** Once type-aware clamping lands (see
  [Runtime clamp](#runtime-clamp)), the applier needs to know the bound.
  Today it clamps everything to `>= 0` regardless; the type is what will
  drive the policy.

## Type checking (parse time)

After the JSON parses cleanly, `JsonToIr.parse` runs
`TypeChecker.check(adventure)` (Ф2.3). The checker produces
`TypeError`s, not `ParseError`s: parse errors mean "the file cannot be
turned into IR"; type errors mean "the file is structurally sound, but its
variable references are wrong". Both are blocking — the reader refuses to
open the file, the editor shows the errors in the validation dialog.

### What is rejected

| Variant | Trigger | Example | Fix hint |
|---|---|---|---|
| `UnknownVariable` | A name in a condition or effect is not in `variables` | `condition: "has_swrod"` | Rename to `has_sword` |
| `HasOnNonBool` | `has_X` / `!has_X` where `X` is not `Bool` | `condition: "has_sword"` on `ItemCount` | Use `sword > 0` |
| `SetFlagOnNonBool` | `set_flags` on a non-`Bool` variable | `set_flags: ["gold"]` | Use `modify_stats: {"gold": 1}` |
| `RemoveFlagOnNonBool` | `remove_flags` on a non-`Bool` variable | `remove_flags: ["health"]` | Use `modify_stats: {"health": -health}` |
| `ModifyStatOnNonNumeric` | `modify_stats` on `Bool` or `ItemList` | `modify_stats: {"has_key": 1}` | Use `set_flags` / `remove_flags` |
| `CompareOnNonNumeric` | `X op N` where `X` is not numeric | `condition: "has_key > 0"` | Use `has_has_key` |
| `InRangeOnNonNumeric` | `X in a..b` where `X` is not numeric | (reserved for Ф3.2) | Use `has_X` or a `Compare` |
| `InitialFlagOnNonBool` | A non-`Bool` name in `initial_state.flags` | `"flags": ["health"]` | Move to `initial_state.stats` |
| `InitialStatOnNonNumeric` | A `Bool` / `ItemList` name in `initial_state.stats` | `"stats": {"has_key": 1}` | Move to `initial_state.flags` |
| `InSubroutine` | Wrapper around an error inside a subroutine body (Ф4.7); `cause` is the original `TypeError` | body uses `ghost` but the frame declares only `health` | Pass the value as an input or fix the local name |
| `InvalidSubroutineSignature` | Duplicate/in-out mismatched params, `ItemList` param, input-only write, or a call arg/output type mismatch (Ф4.7) | `outputs` says `health: Bool`, `inputs` says `health: IntMin` | Make the local types agree; write only to outputs |

Every error is scoped to a scene (`sceneId`) except `InitialState` ones
and subroutine-body/call errors that have no scene (`sceneId == null`);
those appear first in the sorted output. `InSubroutine` keeps the
`cause` for the editor title mapping.

### Error ordering

`TypeChecker.check` returns errors sorted by
`(sceneId == null, sceneId.value, message)`. This is stable across runs,
which matters for snapshot tests of the editor's validation dialog and
for `git diff` of golden outputs.

## Fallback

**What it is.** If `variables` is empty (or absent from the JSON — pre-Ф2.8
files), `TypeChecker` runs in **fallback mode**: it infers a provisional
type table from `tags` and `initialState`, and checks references against
that.

**Why keep it.** Two reasons:

1. **Backward compatibility.** Files written before Ф2.8 carry no
   `variables`. Without fallback, those files would fail parse with
   `UnknownVariable` on every reference. Fallback lets the reader open
   them; the editor shows a warning "types are not declared" and offers
   to declare them (Ф2.7).
2. **Incremental migration.** An author opening an old file in the editor
   sees the warning, clicks "Suggest types" (Ф9.2, future), gets a
   `variables` block pre-filled by `inferTypes`, reviews and saves.
   Fallback makes the file playable **while** the author migrates it.

**How the inferred table is built.** See `TypeChecker.buildTypeTable` KDoc;
summary:

- **`tags[].category`** — `HEALTH` → `IntMin(0)`, `ITEM` → `ItemCount`,
  `JOURNAL` → `Bool` (or `IntMin(0)` if the name appears in
  `initialState.stats`).
- **`initialState.flags`** → `Bool`.
- **`initialState.stats`** → `IntMin(0)`.

If the inferred table is **empty** (no tags, no initial state), the checker
returns no errors — there is nothing to check against, and pretending
otherwise would produce false positives. The "you have not declared
variables" signal is a **UI concern** (Ф2.7 warning, Ф9.2 realtime-linter),
not a `TypeError`.

**Fallback is not weaker.** Typo `has_swrod` still produces
`UnknownVariable` if `sword` is a tag. `has_sword` on `sword: ItemCount`
still produces `HasOnNonBool`. Fallback only loses the ability to check
**cross-field** consistency (e.g. "author declared `HEALTH` but used
`Bool`"), which strict mode sees.

## Migration

**Tool:** `inferTypes(adventure): Map<String, VarDecl>` — public in
`:engine/ir/types/TypeInference.kt` (Ф2.8.2).

Given a parsed `Adventure` with an empty or incomplete `variables`, it
proposes a `Map<String, VarDecl>` that the author can review and copy into
the JSON.

**Priority resolution** when signals conflict:
`HEALTH tag > ITEM tag > numeric usage > Bool usage`.

Rationale in `inferTypes` KDoc, summary:

- **`tags[].category`** is deliberate — the author wrote it. It beats
  incidental usage.
- **Numeric usage > Bool usage** — a Bool cannot appear in `modify_stats`
  (it is a type error), while a numeric can appear in `set_flags` only
  by mistake. When both signals are present, the type checker's
  subsequent error ("`SetFlagOnNonBool`") is a clearer fix-target than
  "`ModifyStatOnNonNumeric`".

**`inferTypes` never guesses bounds.** It emits only `Bool`,
`ItemCount`, or `IntMin(0)` — never `Integer` or `IntRange`. The author
who wants a bounded variable declares it explicitly.

**Idempotence.** On `test_adventure.json` (which now has both declarations
and usage), `inferTypes(adv) == adv.variables` — this is the tripwire test
`TypeInferenceTest > real test_adventure_json - inference matches declared variables`.
If it fails, either the file was edited inconsistently or the logic
drifted.

**What it is not.** `inferTypes` does not validate. It does not check
against an existing `variables` block; it does not resolve contradictions
in contradictory usage. It is a **suggestion engine**, not a validator.
Validation is `TypeChecker`.

## Runtime clamp

**Current state (as of Ф2).** `EffectsApplier.apply` clamps every
`Effect.ModifyStat` to `>= 0`, regardless of the variable's declared
type. This is the same policy as Ф1.5 (`EffectsApplier.kt` KDoc,
"Clamp policy (temporary, until Ф2.8)"). Ф2 did not change it — the DoD
for Ф2.8 was "inferTypes + test_adventure migration + type-clean
reference sample", not "type-aware clamp".

Consequence: a `IntRange(0, 100)` variable (`health`) can exceed its
`max` if the player walks through enough `+50` effects, because the
applier does not enforce the upper bound. The **type checker** sees the
range and will be able to flag out-of-range literals in a future phase
(Ф3.6, `Analyzer.deadConditions`), but the **runtime** today only knows
"not below zero".

**What is not enforced yet:**

| Type | Declared bound | Enforced at runtime | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Bool` | n/a | n/a | Flags are set/removed, not clamped |
| `Integer` | none | `>= 0` (over-eager) | No lower bound in type; applier clamps anyway |
| `IntMin(N)` | `>= N` | `>= 0` (**not `>= N`**) | `N > 0` (e.g. `skill: 1..12` but declared `IntMin(1)`) is not enforced |
| `IntRange(A, B)` | `[A, B]` | `>= 0` (**not `[A, B]`**) | Upper bound not enforced; lower bound only `>= 0` |
| `ItemCount` | `>= 0` | `>= 0` | Correct by coincidence (policy matches type) |
| `ItemList` | n/a | n/a | Applier does not touch lists |

**Why this is deferred.** Type-aware clamp needs a `VarType` lookup at
every `ModifyStat`, which means `EffectsApplier.apply` must take the
`Adventure` (or at least `variables`). That changes its signature and
every call site (`Engine.step`, the reader preview, the debug panel).
Worth doing — but tied to save/restore (Ф5.2, S5, delta model), because a
restored state must be clamped identically to a freshly-applied one.
Doing it now would double the work in Ф5.

**What the author should know today:**

- **Do not rely on `IntRange.max` being enforced.** If the story needs a
  hard cap, add an explicit `Compare` condition on the choice that
  raises the stat, or a scene effect that resets it.
- **Do not rely on `IntMin(N > 0)` being enforced.** A negative delta can
  bring a `skill: 1..12` variable down to `0`. Add an explicit guard if
  the range matters.
- **`ItemCount` is safe** — the applier's `>= 0` policy matches the type.
- **`Integer` will not go below 0** even though the type permits it.
  This is an over-eager policy, not a bug — it has the same explanation
  as above.

The clamp will be type-aware in a future phase; when it lands, this
section will change to "enforced" and the type declarations will become
fully authoritative.

## Common authoring mistakes

| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Choice is visible but always disabled; no error in editor | `condition: "has_sword"` on an `ItemCount` variable, but file still in fallback mode (no `variables`) | Add `variables` block; the checker will now reject it as `HasOnNonBool` |
| Choice is visible but always disabled; error in editor: "Variable 'swrod' is used but not declared" | Typo in condition | Rename to `sword` |
| Health rises indefinitely, upper bound ignored | `IntRange(0, 100)` declared, but applier does not enforce `max` (see [Runtime clamp](#runtime-clamp)) | Add explicit `Compare` guard, or wait for type-aware clamp |
| Stat goes to 0 but the story expected it to stay at `min: 1` | `IntMin(1)` declared, but applier clamps only `>= 0` | Same — explicit guard, or wait |
| `initial_state.flags` contains a numeric name; editor reports `InitialFlagOnNonBool` | Author put `health` in `flags` by mistake | Move to `initial_state.stats` |

# Gamebook mechanics — coverage

**Status:** evolving. Reference, not a contract. Update when a mechanic moves
between statuses.

This file records **which gamebook mechanics from
[`research/gamebook-mechanics.md`](./research/gamebook-mechanics.md)
Adventure supports today, which are partial, and which are planned** — and
for the unsupported ones, what architectural piece is missing. It is the
answer to "does the checklist need new items for this?" — the short answer
is **no** (see §"Why the checklist does not change"), but the long answer
is the table below.

**Not to be confused with:**
- [`progress/progress-log.md`](./progress/progress-log.md) — chronological
  log of "what was done". This file is a static status map, updated only
  when a mechanic changes status.
- [`roadmap.md`](./roadmap.md) — the full post-Ф10 plan (Ф12+). This file
  points to it; the roadmap defines the order and content of those phases.

## How to read

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Supported** | The mechanic is fully expressible with today's IR (`Condition`, `Effect`, `Scene`, `Choice`, `Gate`) and `Engine.step`. No future phase needed. |
| **Partial** | Expressible, but with caveats — e.g. no atomicity, no dedicated counter, semantics pushed onto author or reader. Usable today; a dedicated mechanic may follow in a later phase. |
| **Not supported** | Requires an architectural piece that does not exist yet. "Blocked by" names the piece; "Planned" points to the roadmap phase. |

**Blocked-by codes:**

| Code | What is missing | Where it would live |
|---|---|---|
| **RNG** | A `RandomSource` abstraction injected into `Engine.step` (deterministic in tests, real RNG in production) | `:engine` — Ф12 |
| **PROC** | A first-class `Procedure` node in IR for multi-step computations (combat rounds, complex crafting) | `:engine` — Ф13. Partially addressed by N6 (subroutines, Ф4.7–Ф4.8); not enough for combat |
| **EXT** | An "external outcome" hook on `Engine.step` (physical dexterity, visual puzzle) — engine receives a pre-decided boolean from `:app` | `:engine` + `:app` — Ф15 |
| **CROSS** | Cross-adventure / cross-run state: `LibraryState`, separate from `ProgressData` | `:engine` + `:app` — Ф16 |
| **MULTI** | Multiplayer mechanics (two-player simultaneous choices, shared state) | `:engine` + network — Ф17 |
| **UI** | Authoring UI for the mechanic (the engine may already support it, but authors cannot express it) | `:app` editor — Ф18 |
| **APP** | Concern that lives entirely in `:app` (wall-clock timing, notifications), not in `:engine` | `:app` — Ф15 or later |

**37 entries** (source doc calls them "34 mechanics"; its tables enumerate
37 — 34 base mechanics + 3 sub-variants of `M-RES-RNG`:
`HIGH`/`LOW`/`DVD`).

| Class | Total | Supported | Partial | Not supported |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| M1 Navigation | 7 | 3 | 1 | 3 |
| M2 Resolution | 10 | 2 | 0 | 8 |
| M3 State | 7 | 6 | 0 | 1 |
| M4 Combat | 4 | 0 | 0 | 4 |
| M5 Meta | 9 | 2 | 2 | 5 |
| **Total** | **37** | **13** | **3** | **21** |

## Architectural gaps (why "not supported")

Every "not supported" mechanic traces back to one of the six gaps below.
Closing a gap unlocks all mechanics that list it in "Blocked by".

| Gap | Mechanics it unblocks | Phase |
|---|---|---|
| **RNG** | `M-NAV-RANDOM`, `M-NAV-EVENT`, `M-RES-RNG*`, `M-RES-HYBRID`, `M-RES-BOOST`, `M-STATE-BUILD` | Ф12 |
| **PROC** | `M-COMBAT-ROUND`, `M-COMBAT-CMP`, `M-COMBAT-DRAIN`, `M-META-CRAFT` (atomicity) | Ф13 |
| **EXT** | `M-RES-PHYS`, `M-RES-PUZZLE` | Ф15.1 |
| **CROSS** | `M-META-XFER`, `M-META-PERSIST`, `M-META-LEGACY` | Ф16 |
| **MULTI** | `M-COMBAT-MULTI` | Ф17 |
| **APP** | `M-META-REALTIME` | Ф15.2 |

## What the foundation already supports (why no new Must)

Four pieces already in the plan make the roadmap feasible without
re-architecting:

1. **N6 (subroutines, Ф4.7–Ф4.8)** — a multi-step call/return mechanism
   from IR. Not enough for combat on its own (combat is a loop with state,
   not a single call), but it is the scaffolding for `Procedure` (Ф13).
2. **Sealed `Condition` / `Effect`** (Ф1.2) — a new variant (e.g.
   `Effect.Roll`) can be added without breaking existing code, and the
   parser rejects unknown variants via `@SerialName` rules. This is what
   makes "add a mechanic without rewriting the engine" possible.
3. **Versioned IR + migrations** (Ф5.3) — every new mechanic bumps
   `Adventure.CURRENT_VERSION` (v2 → v3 → …) and adds a migration for
   old files. `test_adventure.json` exercises each new mechanic (Rule 1
   of [`test-adventure-policy.md`](./test-adventure-policy.md)).
4. **`CompiledAdventure` with O(1) lookup** (Ф1.5.5.1) — the runtime
   indexes are the same shape regardless of how many mechanics exist.
   Combat, RNG, cross-adventure state do not change the "find scene by
   id" lookup — they change what happens **inside** a step, not how a
   scene is found.

**What would change the checklist:** if a future Must-hard requirement
("the app must support combat at release") appeared, Ф12–Ф13 would have
to be pulled before Ф10. There is no such requirement today. See
`docs/roadmap.md` for the full post-Ф10 plan.

## Update procedure

**When you implement a mechanic** (i.e. a gap closes or a new `Effect`/
`Condition`/`Procedure` variant lands):

1. Change its row's status: `Not supported` → `Supported` (or `Partial`).
2. Clear or adjust "Blocked by" (it may still be partial).
3. Move "Planned" to `—` (done).
4. **Add** a new entry to
   [`progress/progress-log.md`](./progress/progress-log.md) — this file
   is a snapshot, the progress log is the history.
5. If the mechanic has an authoring UI, update
   [`authoring-guide.md`](./authoring-guide.md) (Ф10.7) in the same PR.

**When you add a new mechanic to `research/gamebook-mechanics.md`:**

1. Add a row to the corresponding M-class table here with the initial
   status (`Not supported` unless it maps to existing IR).
2. Add it to the appropriate "Architectural gaps" bucket, or add a new
   bucket if no existing gap covers it.
3. Add a phase to [`roadmap.md`](./roadmap.md) if it is not covered by
   an existing one.

# Glossary

**Status:** evolving. Terms are added and refined as the app evolves.

This file is the single source of truth for:

- **Domain terminology** — how core concepts are named in code and docs.
- **UI strings** — Russian UI text mapped to English, so that adding an
  English locale later is a lookup, not a redesign.
- **Naming conventions** — spellings we commit to across the project.

When a new term is introduced anywhere in the project, add it here in the same
change. When in doubt about a spelling, follow this file — not your intuition.

## How to use

- **In docs**: use the English term from the "English" column. Do not invent
  synonyms.
- **In the app (Russian)**: the current UI uses Russian. When a string in the
  app matches a row here, treat the row as the canonical mapping.
- **For future i18n**: the Russian string is the source key. Keep the mapping
  up to date as the UI evolves.
- **In code**: keep the identifiers exactly as they appear in the
  "Identifier" columns. Renaming a data model or JSON field is a **breaking
  change** and requires a doc-update PR.

## 1. Domain terms

Concepts that appear across code, JSON and documentation.

| English            | Russian                   | Notes                                                                 |
|--------------------|---------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Adventure          | Приключение               | Also the project's name. Never translate "Adventure" when it refers to the app or the project. |
| Chapter            | Глава                     | A group of scenes. **Pure narrative grouping** — no gate of its own. Gates live on scenes (see Gate, Ф1.5.4). |
| Gate               | Шлюз                      | A step requirement on a single scene (`scenes[].gate`). The player must walk N steps after entering the scene before any exit is allowed. Can sit anywhere in a chapter (first, middle, last), or be absent. |
| Scene              | Сцена                     | One screen of text and (optionally) choices.                          |
| Choice             | Выбор / вариант действия  | A single selectable action in a scene.                                |
| Next scene         | Следующая сцена           | The scene a choice leads to (`next_scene`).                           |
| Condition          | Условие                   | A rule that must hold for a choice to be visible.                     |
| Tag                | Метка                     | An effect or flag used by a scene or choice.                          |
| Flag               | Флаг                      | A boolean-ish marker (`set_flags` / `remove_flags`).                  |
| Stat               | Стат                      | A numeric value (`modify_stats`).                                     |
| Item               | Предмет                   | A tag with `category=ITEM`. Shown in the inventory.                   |
| Journal entry      | Запись журнала            | A tag with `category=JOURNAL` and `visible=true`.                     |
| Health             | Здоровье                  | A tag with `category=HEALTH` (or the literal name `health`).          |
| Initial state      | Начальное состояние       | The player's starting flags and stats (`initial_state`).              |
| Player state       | Состояние игрока          | Current flags + stats + inventory of the player.                      |
| Death scene        | Сцена смерти              | Special scene shown when the player dies (`death_scene`).             |
| Chapter end        | Конец главы               | A scene that closes a chapter (`isChapterEnd`).                       |
| Step gate / Gate   | Шаговый шлюз / Гейт       | A step requirement on a **scene** (`scenes[].gate`), not on a chapter. The player must walk N steps after entering the scene before any exit is allowed. Can sit anywhere in a chapter. See also `Gate`. |
| Required steps     | Требуемые шаги            | The numeric threshold of a `Gate` (`gate.requiredSteps`). In v1 files this lived on `chapters[].required_steps`; the v1→v2 migration moves it to the last scene of the previous chapter. |
| Remaining steps    | Осталось шагов            | Steps left until the gate opens.                                      |
| Death (state)      | Смерть                    | The player's health has reached zero.                                 |
| Draft (editor)     | Черновик                  | Unsaved editor state, saved in `editor_draft_prefs`.                  |
| Validation issue   | Проблема валидации        | A warning or error reported by `StoryValidator`.                      |
| Story stats        | Статистика истории        | Scene/word/choice counts shown in the editor.                         |
| RandomSource       | Источник случайности      | **Planned (Ф12+).** Abstraction over randomness in `Engine.step`; injected so tests are deterministic. See `docs/roadmap.md`. |
| Procedure          | Процедура                 | **Planned (Ф13+).** A multi-step computation invoked from a scene or choice (e.g. combat rounds), modelled as a dedicated IR node. See `docs/roadmap.md`. |
| Combat             | Бой                       | **Planned (Ф13+).** A procedure that resolves a fight between player and enemy over several rounds. Requires RNG (Ф12) and procedures (Ф13). See `docs/roadmap.md`. |

## 2. JSON field names

These are the canonical field names of the adventure JSON. They are part of
the file format and must not be renamed without a migration plan.

| Field                                 | Meaning                                                     |
|---------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------|
| `title`                               | Adventure title.                                            |
| `author`                              | Adventure author.                                           |
| `description`                         | Short description.                                          |
| `initial_state`                       | Player's starting flags and stats.                          |
| `initial_state.flags`                 | Starting flags (list of strings).                           |
| `initial_state.stats`                 | Starting stats (map name → int).                            |
| `tags`                                | Registry of tag definitions for this adventure.             |
| `tags[].name`                         | Stable, machine-readable tag name.                          |
| `tags[].display_name`                 | Human-readable name shown in the UI.                        |
| `tags[].category`                     | `HEALTH` / `ITEM` / `JOURNAL`.                              |
| `tags[].visible`                      | Whether the tag is shown in the HUD.                        |
| `death_scene`                         | Optional. Death scene definition.                           |
| `death_scene.id`                      | Scene ID used for the death screen.                         |
| `death_scene.text`                    | Text shown when the player dies.                            |
| `death_scene.allow_step_back`         | Whether the "step back" button is shown.                    |
| `death_scene.allow_chapter_restart`   | Whether the "restart chapter" button is shown.              |
| `death_scene.allow_adventure_restart` | Whether the "restart adventure" button is shown.            |
| `chapters`                            | Ordered list of chapters.                                   |
| `chapters[].id`                       | Chapter ID.                                                 |
| `chapters[].title`                    | Chapter title.                                              |
| `chapters[].required_steps`           | **Legacy (v1 only).** Steps needed to enter this chapter. Migrated on load to `scenes[].gate` on the last scene of the previous chapter. Ignored in v2 files. |
| `scenes[].gate`                       | **v2+.** Positive integer: steps the player must walk after entering this scene before any exit is allowed. Absent = no gate. See `Gate`. |
| `chapters[].scenes`                   | Scenes in this chapter.                                     |
| `scenes[].id`                         | Scene ID (unique per adventure).                            |
| `scenes[].text`                       | Scene body text.                                            |
| `scenes[].set_flags`                  | Flags to add when the scene is entered.                     |
| `scenes[].remove_flags`               | Flags to remove when the scene is entered.                  |
| `scenes[].modify_stats`               | Stat changes when the scene is entered.                     |
| `scenes[].choices`                    | Available choices in this scene.                            |
| `choices[].text`                      | Choice label shown to the player.                           |
| `choices[].next_scene`                | ID of the scene this choice leads to.                       |
| `choices[].condition`                 | Optional condition gating this choice.                      |
| `choices[].set_flags`                 | Flags to add when this choice is taken.                     |
| `choices[].remove_flags`              | Flags to remove when this choice is taken.                  |
| `choices[].modify_stats`              | Stat changes when this choice is taken.                     |

## 3. Tag categories

| Value      | Russian  | Meaning                                                    |
|------------|----------|------------------------------------------------------------|
| `HEALTH`   | Здоровье | Numeric health-like value; shown in the HUD heart icon.    |
| `ITEM`     | Предмет  | Inventory item; shown in the HUD backpack.                 |
| `JOURNAL`  | Журнал   | Boolean-like flag or visible journal entry.                |

The literal tag name `health` is always treated as `HEALTH`, regardless of the
declared category.

## 4. Conditions (as strings in JSON)

| Syntax    | Meaning                                        |
|-----------|------------------------------------------------|
| `has_X`   | True if flag `X` is set or stat `X` > 0.       |
| `!has_X`  | True if flag `X` is not set and stat `X` ≤ 0.  |
| `X >= N`  | True if stat `X` is at least `N`.              |
| `X < N`   | True if stat `X` is less than `N`.             |
| *(empty)* | Always true.                                   |
