================================================
package com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir

import kotlinx.serialization.SerialName
import kotlinx.serialization.Serializable

/**
 * Reference from a [Choice] back to the [ChoiceTemplate] it was expanded from.
 *
 * **Why it exists.** With the expansion approach (Ф4.2 decision A1), the
 * `Choice` carries fully-expanded content (`text`, `condition`,
 * `visibilityCondition`, `effects`), not a live reference. `TemplateRef`
 * is metadata for the editor: it records *which* template and *which*
 * args produced this choice. The editor (Ф4.3) uses it to show "this
 * choice uses template X" and to offer "update all uses" when the
 * template changes.
 *
 * **Not used by the runtime.** `Engine.step`, `Evaluator`,
 * `EffectsApplier`, `Analyzer` never look at `templateRef` — they see
 * only the expanded content. The reference is inert from the gameplay
 * point of view.
 *
 * **Not serialized to the adventure JSON in Ф4.2.1.** The choice's JSON
 * form (`ChoiceDto`) does not have a `template_ref` field yet; parsing
 * `template_ref` from JSON is Ф4.3. In the IR, the field is
 * `@Serializable` so that `IrToJson` (Ф8) can carry it consistently.
 *
 * @property templateId the `ChoiceTemplate.id` this choice was expanded
 *   from.
 * @property args the arguments used for substitution. Keys are parameter
 *   names (matching `ChoiceTemplate.parameters[i].name`); values are the
 *   actual variable names that were substituted in.
 */
@Serializable
public data class TemplateRef(
    @SerialName("template_id")
    public val templateId: String,
    public val args: Map<String, String> = emptyMap(),
)


================================================
FILE: engine/src/main/kotlin/com/myapp/adventure/engine/ir/types/TypeChecker.kt
================================================
package com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.types

import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Adventure
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Condition
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Effect
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.SceneId
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Subroutine
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.SubroutineCall
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.TagCategory

/**
 * Semantic type checking: verifies that every name referenced from a
 * [Condition] or an [Effect] is declared, and that the type of the
 * reference matches the operation.
 *
 * **Where this sits in the pipeline** (per [com.myapp.adventure.engine]
 * architecture, invariant I3 — parser vs compiler vs analyzer):
 *
 * - **Parser** (`JsonToIr.parse`): "can I turn this into IR?" — JSON
 *   syntax, condition syntax, required fields.
 * - **TypeChecker** (this class): "does every reference make sense
 *   against the declared variables?" — unknown names, wrong type, wrong
 *   effect on the wrong type.
 * - **Compiler** (`Engine.compile`): "can I build runtime indexes?" —
 *   duplicate scene ids, missing start scene, dangling `nextScene`.
 * - **Analyzer** (`Analyzer.lint`): "is the IR coherent?" — reachability,
 *   dead ends, unestablished items.
 *
 * `TypeChecker` sits between the parser and the compiler and **is wired
 * into `JsonToIr.parse`** (Ф2.3): a successful parse runs this check and
 * returns `ParseResult.Failure(typeErrors = …)` if anything is wrong, so
 * `Engine.compile` only ever sees type-clean IR.
 *
 * **Ф4.7 subroutine scopes.** Subroutine bodies are checked against their
 * own local table (`inputs + outputs`), not `Adventure.variables`; a body
 * sees only its parameters. Top-level `Choice.call` args/targets are
 * checked against the global table, nested calls against the enclosing
 * frame. These checks run even when the global type table is empty,
 * because local types are explicit.
 *
 * **Two modes** (developed from the C4 decision, 2026-11-12):
 *
 * 1. **Strict** — `Adventure.variables` is non-empty. Every name
 *    referenced from a condition or effect must appear in
 *    `Adventure.variables`. `tags` and `initialState` are ignored for
 *    type inference; they are UI data, not the source of truth. This is
 *    the mode that lands in Ф2.8 once `JsonToIr` starts populating
 *    `variables` from JSON.
 * 2. **Fallback** — `Adventure.variables` is empty (current state of
 *    every existing file, since the JSON field is not parsed yet). The
 *    checker **infers** a provisional type table from:
 *    - `Adventure.tags`: `HEALTH` → `IntMin(0)`, `ITEM` → `ItemCount`,
 *      `JOURNAL` → `Bool` (or `IntMin(0)` if the name appears in
 *      `initialState.stats` instead of `flags`);
 *    - `Adventure.initialState.flags`: any flag not in `tags` is `Bool`;
 *    - `Adventure.initialState.stats`: any stat not in `tags` is `IntMin(0)`.
 *
 *    If even that table is empty (no tags, no initial state), the
 *    checker returns an empty list — there is nothing to check against,
 *    and pretending there is would produce false positives. The "you
 *    have not declared variables" signal is a **UI concern** and will
 *    land in the editor warning panel (Ф9.2), not here.
 *
 *    Fallback mode is deliberately **not weaker** than strict mode: the
 *    inferred table is used exactly as if it were `variables`. So a typo
 *    (`has_swrod` when `sword` is a tag) still produces
 *    [TypeError.UnknownVariable], which is the DoD requirement
 *    ("опечатка `has_swrod` → ошибка").
 *
 * **What is NOT checked** (deferred):
 * - `IntRange(min > max)` — a range that can never be satisfied. That
 *   is reachability / dead-condition analysis (Ф3.6
 *   `Analyzer.deadConditions`), not type checking.
 * - `Compare` with a literal outside the declared range
 *   (`skill > 20` on `IntRange(1, 12)`) — same, Ф3.6.
 * - `InitialState.stats` values that exceed `IntRange.max` — clamping
 *   policy (Ф2.8) not yet type-aware; the runtime currently clamps all
 *   `ModifyStat` to `>= 0` regardless of declared type.
 * - Cross-field constraints between `TagCategory` and `VarType`
 *   (`HEALTH` + `Bool` is semantically nonsense but mechanically
 *   possible). Until Ф2.8 populates `variables`, this cannot be checked
 *   without false positives — an author who declares a `JOURNAL` tag and
 *   uses it as a flag is fine.
 *
 * **Deterministic output.** [check] returns errors sorted by
 * `(sceneId == null, sceneId.value, message)` — same convention as
 * `Analyzer.lint`. Repeated runs on the same input produce identical
 * output.
 *
 * **Pure.** No I/O, no logging, no mutation of [adventure]. Takes the IR
 * (which by definition is immutable) and returns a fresh list.
 */
public object TypeChecker {

    /**
     * Checks all condition and effect references in [adventure].
     *
     * @return a list of [TypeError]s, empty if the adventure type-checks
     *   cleanly (or if there is nothing to check against — see the class
     *   KDoc, "fallback" mode).
     */
    public fun check(adventure: Adventure): List<TypeError> {
        val typeTable = buildTypeTable(adventure)
        val errors = mutableListOf<TypeError>()
        val subroutinesById = adventure.subroutines.associateBy { it.id }

        // `typeTable.isEmpty()` means there is nothing declared or
        // inferable to check scene/global references against. Do **not**
        // report every name as unknown — that would reject every legacy
        // file that relies on the implicit zero-value fallback. Subroutine
        // bodies are still checked below because their scope is explicit
        // (inputs + outputs), independent of the global table.
        if (typeTable.isNotEmpty()) {
            // 1. InitialState — must match the declared type (or inferred, in
            //    fallback mode). These are the only errors without a sceneId;
            //    they are reported first by the sort at the end.
            for (flag in adventure.initialState.flags) {
                val type = typeTable[flag] ?: continue
                if (type != VarType.Bool) {
                    errors += TypeError.InitialFlagOnNonBool(flag, type)
                }
            }
            for (stat in adventure.initialState.stats.keys) {
                val type = typeTable[stat] ?: continue
                if (!type.isNumeric()) {
                    errors += TypeError.InitialStatOnNonNumeric(stat, type)
                }
            }

            // 2. Scenes: scene effects, then each choice's condition and
            //    effects. Order within a scene follows the source (scene
            //    first, then choices), so that when the author opens the
            //    editor, the first reported error is the one "highest" in the
            //    visual hierarchy. Stable-sorted at the end.
            for (chapter in adventure.chapters) {
                for (scene in chapter.scenes) {
                    checkEffects(scene.effects, scene.id, typeTable, errors)
                    for (choice in scene.choices) {
                        choice.condition?.let {
                            checkCondition(it, scene.id, typeTable, errors)
                        }
                        checkEffects(choice.effects, scene.id, typeTable, errors)
                        choice.call?.let {
                            checkTopLevelSubroutineCall(
                                call = it,
                                sceneId = scene.id,
                                globalTypes = typeTable,
                                subroutinesById = subroutinesById,
                                errors = errors,
                            )
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
        }

        // Ф4.7: subroutine bodies have their own local scope
        // (inputs + outputs), not the global variable table. Always check
        // them: their types are explicit even when the adventure declares
        // no global variables.
        for (subroutine in adventure.subroutines) {
            checkSubroutine(subroutine, subroutinesById, errors)
        }

        return errors.sortedWith(
            // `sceneId != null` (initial-state errors have sceneId == null)
            // → false → 0 → sorted first. Scene errors → true → 1 →
            // sorted after. This matches "show the highest-level problems
            // first" in the editor error panel (Ф9.2): initial-state errors
            // are not tied to a specific scene, so they appear above the
            // per-scene ones.
            compareBy<TypeError> { it.sceneId != null }
                .thenBy { it.sceneId?.value ?: "" }
                .thenBy { it.message },
        )
    }

    // ---------- Type table construction ----------

    /**
     * Builds the name → type table used for checking.
     *
     * In **strict mode** (`variables` is non-empty), the table is exactly
     * `variables` — `tags` and `initialState` are ignored, because the
     * author declared the types explicitly.
     *
     * In **fallback mode** (`variables` is empty), the table is inferred
     * from `tags` + `initialState`. See class KDoc for the mapping.
     */
    private fun buildTypeTable(adventure: Adventure): Map<String, VarType> {
        if (adventure.variables.isNotEmpty()) {
            return adventure.variables.mapValues { it.value.type }
        }

        val table = mutableMapOf<String, VarType>()

        // 1. Tags: category determines the type, initial state refines
        //    JOURNAL (flag vs numeric).
        for (tag in adventure.tags) {
            val type = when (tag.category) {
                TagCategory.HEALTH -> VarType.IntMin(0)
                TagCategory.ITEM -> VarType.ItemCount
                TagCategory.JOURNAL -> when {
                    // A JOURNAL tag that appears in `initialState.flags` is
                    // a boolean marker (visible journal entry). One that
                    // appears in `initialState.stats` is a numeric journal
                    // value (counters, quest progress). If it is not in
                    // either, default to Bool — the most common case for
                    // journals.
                    tag.name in adventure.initialState.flags -> VarType.Bool
                    tag.name in adventure.initialState.stats -> VarType.IntMin(0)
                    else -> VarType.Bool
                }
            }
            table[tag.name] = type
        }

        // 2. Initial state: any name not covered by a tag is inferred from
        //    the side of `initialState` it appears in.
        for (flag in adventure.initialState.flags) {
            table.putIfAbsent(flag, VarType.Bool)
        }
        for (stat in adventure.initialState.stats.keys) {
            table.putIfAbsent(stat, VarType.IntMin(0))
        }

        return table
    }

    // ---------- Condition checking ----------

    private fun checkCondition(
        condition: Condition,
        sceneId: SceneId?,
        typeTable: Map<String, VarType>,
        errors: MutableList<TypeError>,
    ) {
        when (condition) {
            is Condition.Literal -> {
                // Ф3.1: `Literal` is Bool by construction. No variable
                // references, nothing to check against the type table.
                // Not produced by the parser (see `Condition.Literal`
                // KDoc) — appears only in hand-built IR.
            }
            is Condition.VarRef -> {
                // Ф3.1: `VarRef` was added to the AST as a forward-looking
                // node for Ф3.2 (`A && B` where `B` is a bare variable).
                // The parser does not produce it yet — a bare `"x"` in
                // JSON is still a `ConditionError` (see
                // `ConditionParser`). When Ф3.2 extends the grammar, this
                // branch must grow two checks:
                //   1. `TypeError.UnknownVariable` if `name` is not in
                //      `typeTable`.
                //   2. `TypeError.VarRefOnNonBool` if `name`'s type is
                //      not `Bool` (a new variant; `HasOnNonBool`'s
                //      message references `has_X` syntax specifically,
                //      which a bare `VarRef` does not have).
                // Until then: no-op, and safe by omission.
            }
            is Condition.Has -> {
                val type = typeTable[condition.name]
                if (type == null) {
                    errors += TypeError.UnknownVariable(condition.name, sceneId)
                } else if (type != VarType.Bool) {
                    errors += TypeError.HasOnNonBool(condition.name, type, sceneId)
                }
            }
            // Ф2.4 note: `Not` / `And` / `Or` recurse into their operands.
            // The parser does not produce these nodes today — `!X`, `A && B`,
            // `A || B` are rejected at parse time as reserved characters
            // (Ф1.3.3.2). They will start appearing once Ф3.2 (N7.base)
            // extends `ConditionParser` with the logical operators.
            //
            // At that point **two things must be added here**:
            //   1. `InvalidBooleanOperand(name, actualType)` — a check that
            //      each operand of `And` / `Or` / `Not` is Bool. Today the
            //      only condition nodes the parser can produce are
            //      `Has` / `Compare` / `InRange`, all three of which return
            //      Bool by AST shape — so no operand-type check is needed
            //      yet.
            //   2. A `Condition.VarRef(name)` branch — Ф3.2 will add a bare
            //      variable reference to the AST, at which point `A && B`
            //      where `B` is `VarRef("health")` becomes possible and
            //      **must** be rejected unless `health` is Bool.
            //
            // Do not add either pre-emptively: there is no `VarRef` node to
            // check, and adding a "Bool operand" check against the existing
            // AST would be a no-op (all current nodes are Bool). The
            // DoD-closing test for Ф2.4 (`ConditionParserTest >
            // has_sword_and_health is rejected`) pins the current
            // behaviour at the parse layer.
            is Condition.Not -> checkCondition(condition.inner, sceneId, typeTable, errors)
            is Condition.And -> {
                checkCondition(condition.left, sceneId, typeTable, errors)
                checkCondition(condition.right, sceneId, typeTable, errors)
            }
            is Condition.Or -> {
                checkCondition(condition.left, sceneId, typeTable, errors)
                checkCondition(condition.right, sceneId, typeTable, errors)
            }
            is Condition.Compare -> {
                val type = typeTable[condition.varName]
                if (type == null) {
                    errors += TypeError.UnknownVariable(condition.varName, sceneId)
                } else if (!type.isNumeric()) {
                    errors += TypeError.CompareOnNonNumeric(condition.varName, type, sceneId)
                }
            }
            is Condition.InRange -> {
                val type = typeTable[condition.varName]
                if (type == null) {
                    errors += TypeError.UnknownVariable(condition.varName, sceneId)
                } else if (!type.isNumeric()) {
                    errors += TypeError.InRangeOnNonNumeric(condition.varName, type, sceneId)
                }
            }
        }
    }

    // ---------- Effect checking ----------

    private fun checkEffects(
        effects: List<Effect>,
        sceneId: SceneId?,
        typeTable: Map<String, VarType>,
        errors: MutableList<TypeError>,
    ) {
        for (effect in effects) {
            when (effect) {
                is Effect.SetFlag -> {
                    val type = typeTable[effect.name]
                    if (type == null) {
                        errors += TypeError.UnknownVariable(effect.name, sceneId)
                    } else if (type != VarType.Bool) {
                        errors += TypeError.SetFlagOnNonBool(effect.name, type, sceneId)
                    }
                }
                is Effect.RemoveFlag -> {
                    val type = typeTable[effect.name]
                    if (type == null) {
                        errors += TypeError.UnknownVariable(effect.name, sceneId)
                    } else if (type != VarType.Bool) {
                        errors += TypeError.RemoveFlagOnNonBool(effect.name, type, sceneId)
                    }
                }
                is Effect.ModifyStat -> {
                    val type = typeTable[effect.name]
                    if (type == null) {
                        errors += TypeError.UnknownVariable(effect.name, sceneId)
                    } else if (!type.isNumeric()) {
                        errors += TypeError.ModifyStatOnNonNumeric(effect.name, type, sceneId)
                    }
                }
                is Effect.Set -> {
                    // Ф3.1: `Set` shares the "numeric required" rule with
                    // `ModifyStat`. Same `TypeError` variant — the type
                    // checker cares that the operation requires a number,
                    // not whether it is a delta or an absolute value.
                    val type = typeTable[effect.name]
                    if (type == null) {
                        errors += TypeError.UnknownVariable(effect.name, sceneId)
                    } else if (!type.isNumeric()) {
                        errors += TypeError.ModifyStatOnNonNumeric(effect.name, type, sceneId)
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }

    // ---------- Subroutine checking (Ф4.7) ----------

    /**
     * Checks one subroutine in its **local scope**: only `inputs` and
     * `outputs` are visible, never `Adventure.variables`. This enforces the
     * pure-function contract described in `Subroutine` KDoc.
     *
     * Body errors are wrapped in [TypeError.InSubroutine] so the message
     * names the subroutine even though there is no scene to jump to.
     */
    private fun checkSubroutine(
        subroutine: Subroutine,
        subroutinesById: Map<String, Subroutine>,
        errors: MutableList<TypeError>,
    ) {
        val localErrors = mutableListOf<TypeError>()
        val localTypes = mutableMapOf<String, VarType>()
        val inputNames = mutableSetOf<String>()

        for (input in subroutine.inputs) {
            if (input.type is VarType.ItemList) {
                localErrors += TypeError.InvalidSubroutineSignature(
                    subroutineId = subroutine.id,
                    detail = "ItemList input '${input.name}' is not supported in N6.base",
                )
            }
            if (localTypes.containsKey(input.name)) {
                localErrors += TypeError.InvalidSubroutineSignature(
                    subroutineId = subroutine.id,
                    detail = "duplicate parameter '${input.name}'",
                )
            } else {
                localTypes[input.name] = input.type
            }
            inputNames += input.name
        }

        for (output in subroutine.outputs) {
            if (output.type is VarType.ItemList) {
                localErrors += TypeError.InvalidSubroutineSignature(
                    subroutineId = subroutine.id,
                    detail = "ItemList output '${output.name}' is not supported in N6.base",
                )
            }
            val existing = localTypes[output.name]
            if (existing != null && existing != output.type) {
                localErrors += TypeError.InvalidSubroutineSignature(
                    subroutineId = subroutine.id,
                    detail = "parameter '${output.name}' has input type " +
                            "${existing.displayName()} but output type " +
                            output.type.displayName(),
                )
            } else {
                localTypes[output.name] = output.type
            }
        }

        val inputOnly = inputNames - subroutine.outputs.map { it.name }.toSet()

        for (step in subroutine.body) {
            step.condition?.let {
                checkCondition(it, null, localTypes, localErrors)
            }
            checkEffects(step.effects, null, localTypes, localErrors)
            checkInputOnlyWrites(step.effects, inputOnly, subroutine.id, localErrors)
            step.call?.let {
                checkNestedSubroutineCall(
                    call = it,
                    callerSubroutineId = subroutine.id,
                    localTypes = localTypes,
                    inputOnly = inputOnly,
                    subroutinesById = subroutinesById,
                    errors = localErrors,
                )
            }
        }

        errors += localErrors.map { TypeError.InSubroutine(subroutine.id, it) }
    }

    private fun checkInputOnlyWrites(
        effects: List<Effect>,
        inputOnly: Set<String>,
        subroutineId: String,
        errors: MutableList<TypeError>,
    ) {
        for (effect in effects) {
            val name = when (effect) {
                is Effect.SetFlag -> effect.name
                is Effect.RemoveFlag -> effect.name
                is Effect.ModifyStat -> effect.name
                is Effect.Set -> effect.name
            }
            if (name in inputOnly) {
                errors += TypeError.InvalidSubroutineSignature(
                    subroutineId = subroutineId,
                    detail = "effect writes input-only parameter '$name'",
                )
            }
        }
    }

    private fun checkNestedSubroutineCall(
        call: SubroutineCall,
        callerSubroutineId: String,
        localTypes: Map<String, VarType>,
        inputOnly: Set<String>,
        subroutinesById: Map<String, Subroutine>,
        errors: MutableList<TypeError>,
    ) {
        val callee = subroutinesById[call.subroutineId] ?: return
        val inputs = callee.inputs.associateBy { it.name }
        for ((parameter, source) in call.args) {
            val input = inputs[parameter] ?: continue
            val sourceType = localTypes[source]
            if (sourceType == null) {
                errors += TypeError.UnknownVariable(source, null)
            } else if (sourceType != input.type) {
                errors += TypeError.InvalidSubroutineSignature(
                    subroutineId = callee.id,
                    detail = "argument '$parameter' expects " +
                            "${input.type.displayName()}, but local '$source' is " +
                            sourceType.displayName(),
                    callerSubroutineId = callerSubroutineId,
                )
            }
        }

        val outputs = callee.outputs.associateBy { it.name }
        for ((parameter, target) in call.outputs) {
            val output = outputs[parameter] ?: continue
            val targetType = localTypes[target]
            if (targetType == null) {
                errors += TypeError.UnknownVariable(target, null)
                continue
            }
            if (target in inputOnly) {
                errors += TypeError.InvalidSubroutineSignature(
                    subroutineId = callee.id,
                    detail = "output '$parameter' targets input-only local '$target'",
                    callerSubroutineId = callerSubroutineId,
                )
            }
            if (targetType != output.type) {
                errors += TypeError.InvalidSubroutineSignature(
                    subroutineId = callee.id,
                    detail = "output '$parameter' expects " +
                            "${output.type.displayName()}, but local '$target' is " +
                            targetType.displayName(),
                    callerSubroutineId = callerSubroutineId,
                )
            }
        }
    }

    /**
     * Top-level call from a [com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Choice]: argument
     * sources and output targets are global variables from
     * [Adventure.variables] (or the inferred fallback table).
     */
    private fun checkTopLevelSubroutineCall(
        call: SubroutineCall,
        sceneId: SceneId,
        globalTypes: Map<String, VarType>,
        subroutinesById: Map<String, Subroutine>,
        errors: MutableList<TypeError>,
    ) {
        val callee = subroutinesById[call.subroutineId] ?: return

        val inputs = callee.inputs.associateBy { it.name }
        for ((parameter, source) in call.args) {
            val input = inputs[parameter] ?: continue
            val sourceType = globalTypes[source]
            if (sourceType == null) {
                errors += TypeError.UnknownVariable(source, sceneId)
            } else if (sourceType != input.type) {
                errors += TypeError.InvalidSubroutineSignature(
                    subroutineId = callee.id,
                    detail = "argument '$parameter' expects " +
                            "${input.type.displayName()}, but variable '$source' is " +
                            sourceType.displayName(),
                    sceneId = sceneId,
                )
            }
        }

        val outputs = callee.outputs.associateBy { it.name }
        for ((parameter, target) in call.outputs) {
            val output = outputs[parameter] ?: continue
            val targetType = globalTypes[target]
            if (targetType == null) {
                errors += TypeError.UnknownVariable(target, sceneId)
            } else if (targetType != output.type) {
                errors += TypeError.InvalidSubroutineSignature(
                    subroutineId = callee.id,
                    detail = "output '$parameter' expects " +
                            "${output.type.displayName()}, but variable '$target' is " +
                            targetType.displayName(),
                    sceneId = sceneId,
                )
            }
        }
    }

    // ---------- Helpers ----------

    /**
     * True for the numeric [VarType]s (`Integer`, `IntMin`, `IntRange`,
     * `ItemCount`). False for `Bool` and `ItemList` — both non-numeric
     * operands.
     */
    private fun VarType.isNumeric(): Boolean = when (this) {
        is VarType.Bool, is VarType.ItemList -> false
        is VarType.Integer, is VarType.IntMin, is VarType.IntRange, is VarType.ItemCount -> true
    }
}


================================================
FILE: engine/src/main/kotlin/com/myapp/adventure/engine/ir/types/TypeError.kt
================================================
package com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.types

import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.SceneId

/**
 * One type error found by [TypeChecker].
 *
 * **What this is.** A `TypeError` means the author wrote something the
 * type checker can prove wrong against the declared variables:
 * - a reference to a name that is not declared ([UnknownVariable]);
 * - an operation whose operand type does not match ([HasOnNonBool],
 *   [ModifyStatOnNonNumeric], …);
 * - an initial value that contradicts the declared type
 *   ([InitialFlagOnNonBool], [InitialStatOnNonNumeric]).
 *
 * Unlike [com.myapp.adventure.engine.analyze.LintIssue] (`WARNING`), a
 * `TypeError` is meant to be **blocking** for the reader: it is the same
 * class of "the file would misbehave at runtime" as
 * [com.myapp.adventure.engine.CompileError]. The reader must not open a
 * file with type errors. Ф2.3 wires this in (`parse → typecheck →
 * typed IR`); Ф2.2 only defines the check itself.
 *
 * **Rendering.** [message] is a fully-formed English string ready to
 * show to the author. [sceneId] is the navigation hook: clicking the
 * error in the editor (Ф9.2) jumps to this scene. `null` for
 * `InitialState` errors, which do not belong to a scene.
 *
 * **Why sealed class, not enum.** Like [com.myapp.adventure.engine.analyze.LintKind],
 * future checks need per-variant data (`name`, `actualType`, …) that an
 * enum cannot carry. A sealed class grows without breaking exhaustive
 * `when` in callers that want to react per variant.
 *
 * **Ordering.** [TypeChecker.check] returns errors sorted by
 * `(sceneId == null first, sceneId, message)` — the same stable ordering
 * used by `Analyzer.lint`, so that snapshot tests of checker output stay
 * green.
 *
 * **Not covered here** (deferred):
 * - `IntRange(min > max)` — Ф3.6 (`Analyzer.deadConditions` territory).
 * - `Compare` with a literal outside the declared range
 *   (`skill > 20` on `IntRange(1, 12)`) — Ф3.6.
 * - Unknown variables in `Condition.Has` inside a `Not` / `And` / `Or`
 *   — handled by recursion, not by a separate variant.
 */
public sealed class TypeError {

    /** Human-readable, English, one sentence. */
    public abstract val message: String

    /**
     * Scene where the error was found. `null` for `InitialState` errors
     * ([InitialFlagOnNonBool], [InitialStatOnNonNumeric]).
     */
    public abstract val sceneId: SceneId?

    /**
     * A name is referenced from a condition or an effect, but it is not
     * declared in [com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Adventure.variables]
     * (in strict mode) or in `tags` + `initialState` (in fallback mode,
     * see [TypeChecker] KDoc).
     *
     * Almost always a typo (`has_swrod` for `has_sword`), or a variable
     * the author removed from one place and forgot to remove from
     * another.
     */
    public data class UnknownVariable(
        public val name: String,
        override val sceneId: SceneId?,
    ) : TypeError() {
        override val message: String =
            "Variable '$name' is used but not declared" +
                    (sceneId?.let { " (scene '${it.value}')" } ?: "") +
                    "."
    }

    /**
     * `has_X` is used on a variable whose declared type is not [VarType.Bool].
     *
     * Common mistake: `has_sword` when `sword` is `ItemCount`. The
     * semantic intent is "the player has at least one sword", which in the
     * IR is `sword > 0` ([com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Condition.Compare]),
     * not `has_sword`.
     */
    public data class HasOnNonBool(
        public val name: String,
        public val actualType: VarType,
        override val sceneId: SceneId?,
    ) : TypeError() {
        override val message: String =
            "Condition 'has_$name' requires '$name' to be Bool, " +
                    "but it is ${actualType.displayName()}. " +
                    "For numeric variables use '$name > 0' instead."
    }

    /**
     * `set_flag` is used on a variable whose declared type is not [VarType.Bool].
     *
     * `set_flag` is for boolean markers; a numeric stat is changed with
     * `modify_stat`.
     */
    public data class SetFlagOnNonBool(
        public val name: String,
        public val actualType: VarType,
        override val sceneId: SceneId?,
    ) : TypeError() {
        override val message: String =
            "Effect 'set_flag' on '$name' requires Bool, " +
                    "but '$name' is ${actualType.displayName()}. " +
                    "Use 'modify_stat' for numeric variables."
    }

    /**
     * `remove_flag` is used on a variable whose declared type is not
     * [VarType.Bool]. Symmetric to [SetFlagOnNonBool].
     */
    public data class RemoveFlagOnNonBool(
        public val name: String,
        public val actualType: VarType,
        override val sceneId: SceneId?,
    ) : TypeError() {
        override val message: String =
            "Effect 'remove_flag' on '$name' requires Bool, " +
                    "but '$name' is ${actualType.displayName()}. " +
                    "Use 'modify_stat' with a negative delta for numeric variables."
    }

    /**
     * A numeric effect (`modify_stat` or `set`) is applied to a variable
     * whose declared type is [VarType.Bool] or [VarType.ItemList] — both
     * non-numeric.
     *
     * Both `ModifyStat` and `Set` (Ф3.1) share this variant: from the
     * type checker's point of view, the distinction between "add delta"
     * and "set absolute value" is irrelevant — the operation requires a
     * number, and the variable is not a number. Merging them keeps the
     * `TypeError` surface small; the [message] mentions `modify_stat`
     * because that is the only form the parser produces today.
     */
    public data class ModifyStatOnNonNumeric(
        public val name: String,
        public val actualType: VarType,
        override val sceneId: SceneId?,
    ) : TypeError() {
        override val message: String =
            "Effect 'modify_stat' on '$name' requires a numeric type, " +
                    "but '$name' is ${actualType.displayName()}. " +
                    "Use 'set_flag' / 'remove_flag' for Bool variables."
    }

    /**
     * A [com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Condition.Compare] uses a non-numeric
     * variable. `has_X` is the correct form for [VarType.Bool].
     */
    public data class CompareOnNonNumeric(
        public val name: String,
        public val actualType: VarType,
        override val sceneId: SceneId?,
    ) : TypeError() {
        override val message: String =
            "Comparison on '$name' requires a numeric type, " +
                    "but '$name' is ${actualType.displayName()}. " +
                    "For Bool variables use 'has_$name'."
    }

    /**
     * A [com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Condition.InRange] uses a non-numeric
     * variable. Ranges only make sense for numbers.
     */
    public data class InRangeOnNonNumeric(
        public val name: String,
        public val actualType: VarType,
        override val sceneId: SceneId?,
    ) : TypeError() {
        override val message: String =
            "'$name in a..b' requires a numeric type, " +
                    "but '$name' is ${actualType.displayName()}."
    }

    /**
     * A variable in [com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.InitialState.flags] has a
     * declared type other than [VarType.Bool].
     *
     * `initial_state.flags` is for boolean markers; numeric starting
     * values belong in `initial_state.stats`.
     */
    public data class InitialFlagOnNonBool(
        public val name: String,
        public val actualType: VarType,
    ) : TypeError() {
        override val sceneId: SceneId? = null
        override val message: String =
            "'$name' is listed in initial_state.flags, which requires Bool, " +
                    "but it is ${actualType.displayName()}. " +
                    "Move it to initial_state.stats."
    }

    /**
     * A variable in [com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.InitialState.stats] has a
     * declared type that is not numeric ([VarType.Bool] or
     * [VarType.ItemList]).
     */
    public data class InitialStatOnNonNumeric(
        public val name: String,
        public val actualType: VarType,
    ) : TypeError() {
        override val sceneId: SceneId? = null
        override val message: String =
            "'$name' is listed in initial_state.stats, which requires a numeric type, " +
                    "but it is ${actualType.displayName()}. " +
                    "Move it to initial_state.flags."
    }

    /**
     * Ф4.7: wraps an error found while checking a [com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Subroutine]
     * body. The body has no scene, so [sceneId] is usually `null`; the
     * wrapper adds the subroutine id to the message.
     *
     * The editor's title mapping delegates to [cause], so an unknown local
     * still shows the familiar "unknown variable" title, with the subroutine
     * context in the description.
     */
    public data class InSubroutine(
        public val subroutineId: String,
        public val cause: TypeError,
    ) : TypeError() {
        override val sceneId: SceneId? = cause.sceneId
        override val message: String =
            "In subroutine '$subroutineId': ${cause.message}"
    }

    /**
     * Ф4.7: a subroutine declaration or call is structurally inconsistent —
     * duplicate parameter names, an in-out parameter with mismatched types,
     * an unsupported `ItemList` parameter, a write to an input-only
     * parameter, or an argument/output whose type does not match.
     *
     * Arity errors (missing/extra args) are [com.myapp.adventure.engine.CompileError]s;
     * this variant is about types and parameter semantics.
     *
     * @property subroutineId the callee (or the subroutine being declared).
     * @property detail human-readable explanation.
     * @property sceneId set for a top-level call from a choice.
     * @property callerSubroutineId set for a nested call from a body.
     */
    public data class InvalidSubroutineSignature(
        public val subroutineId: String,
        public val detail: String,
        override val sceneId: SceneId? = null,
        public val callerSubroutineId: String? = null,
    ) : TypeError() {
        override val message: String = buildString {
            append("Subroutine '$subroutineId'")
            val sid = sceneId
            val caller = callerSubroutineId
            when {
                sid != null -> append(" (called from scene '${sid.value}')")
                caller != null -> append(" (called from subroutine '$caller')")
            }
            append(": ")
            append(detail.trimEnd('.'))
            append('.')
        }
    }
}

/**
 * Human-readable representation of a [VarType] for error messages.
 *
 * `data class` / `data object` already provide a `toString()`, but its
 * output is Kotlin-syntax (`IntRange(min=0, max=100)`), which reads poorly
 * in a message shown to an author. `IntRange(0..100)` is closer to the
 * authoring-level notation.
 */
internal fun VarType.displayName(): String = when (this) {
    is VarType.Bool -> "Bool"
    is VarType.Integer -> "Integer"
    is VarType.IntMin -> "IntMin($min)"
    is VarType.IntRange -> "IntRange($min..$max)"
    is VarType.ItemCount -> "ItemCount"
    is VarType.ItemList -> "ItemList"
}

FILE: engine/src/main/kotlin/com/myapp/adventure/engine/ir/types/TypeInference.kt

package com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.types

import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Adventure
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Condition
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Effect
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.TagCategory

/**
 * Infers variable types from usage across [adventure].
 *
 * **Purpose.** Ф2.8 DoD: "скрипт/утилита `inferTypes(ir)` предлагает
 * типы по использованию". This is the migration tool for adventures
 * written before explicit variable declarations existed (or for files
 * where the author has not yet declared types). Given a fully-parsed
 * [Adventure], it returns a **suggestion** — the caller decides whether
 * to apply it (write into `Adventure.variables`) or to compare it with
 * the existing declarations to spot conflicts.
 *
 * **What it does.** Scans every place a variable can appear and
 * collects two kinds of signals:
 *
 * 1. **Explicit tag categories** — the strongest signal, because the
 *    author wrote them on purpose:
 *    - `HEALTH` → [VarType.IntMin]`(0)` (health-like, cannot go negative);
 *    - `ITEM` → [VarType.ItemCount] (stackable item);
 *    - `JOURNAL` → [VarType.Bool] if the name is **not** in
 *      [Adventure.initialState.stats], otherwise [VarType.IntMin]`(0)`.
 *      Rationale: a JOURNAL variable that starts as a number
 *      (`quest_steps = 3`) is a counter, not a flag; one that starts
 *      as a flag, or is only ever set, is a flag.
 * 2. **Usage signals** — what the author actually does with the name:
 *    - [Adventure.initialState.flags] → [VarType.Bool];
 *    - [Adventure.initialState.stats] → [VarType.IntMin]`(0)`;
 *    - [Effect.SetFlag] / [Effect.RemoveFlag] / [Condition.Has] →
 *      [VarType.Bool];
 *    - [Effect.ModifyStat] / [Condition.Compare] / [Condition.InRange]
 *      → [VarType.IntMin]`(0)`.
 *
 * **Priority when signals conflict.**
 * `HEALTH tag > ITEM tag > numeric usage > Bool usage`.
 *
 * Why:
 * - **`tags[].category`** is an explicit, deliberate declaration by the
 *   author. It beats incidental usage. If an item is declared `ITEM` and
 *   also appears in `set_flag`, the author made a mistake — but the
 *   intent (`ITEM`) is clearer than the accident (`set_flag`), and the
 *   type checker will report the mistake as
 *   `SetFlagOnNonBool`.
 * - **`numeric usage > Bool usage`** because "used in `modify_stat` /
 *   `compare`" is a stronger indicator of "this is a number" than "used
 *   in `set_flag`" is of "this is a flag" — a Bool cannot appear in
 *   `modify_stat` at all (it is a type error), while a numeric can
 *   legitimately appear in `set_flag` **only** by mistake.
 *
 * `inferTypes` does not try to resolve contradictions; it proposes the
 * most likely type so that migration succeeds in the common case. When
 * the result contradicts `tags` or `initialState`, the type checker
 * (which runs after migration) reports the contradiction with a
 * concrete fix-hint — that is the correct place to surface it.
 *
 * **Not `IntRange`.** We do not guess upper bounds. An author who wants
 * a bounded variable (`health 0..100`) declares `IntRange` explicitly
 * in `variables`. Inferred types are always either `Bool`,
 * `ItemCount`, or `IntMin(0)` — the safe, non-negotiable bounds.
 * `inferTypes` never returns `Integer` or `IntRange`: "no bounds known"
 * is not the same as "unbounded on purpose", and `IntMin(0)` is a
 * strict superset of `Integer` for the vast majority of game variables
 * (health, gold, ammo, items — none go negative).
 *
 * **Pure.** No I/O, no logging, no mutation of [adventure]. Safe to call
 * from tests, CLI tooling, or a future editor "Suggest types" button.
 *
 * **Not part of `TypeChecker`.** `TypeChecker` validates **declared**
 * types; `inferTypes` proposes **missing** ones. Keeping them separate
 * means the migration tool does not accidentally weaken validation:
 * `TypeChecker` still rejects references to names that no one ever
 * declared, even if `inferTypes` could "invent" a type for them.
 *
 * **Deterministic output.** The returned map has no meaningful order
 * guarantee (it is a `Map`, not a list), but two calls on the same
 * [Adventure] produce an `==`-equal map.
 *
 * @param adventure a fully-parsed IR. The parser is expected to have
 *   already succeeded — `inferTypes` does not validate.
 * @return `name → VarDecl` for every name that appears at least once
 *   in `tags`, `initialState`, or usage. Names that appear **nowhere**
 *   cannot be inferred and are not included; a variable that only the
 *   author knows about must be declared explicitly.
 */
public fun inferTypes(adventure: Adventure): Map<String, VarDecl> {
    val healthSignals = mutableSetOf<String>()
    val itemSignals = mutableSetOf<String>()
    val numericSignals = mutableSetOf<String>()
    val boolSignals = mutableSetOf<String>()

    // 1. Explicit tag categories.
    for (tag in adventure.tags) {
        when (tag.category) {
            TagCategory.HEALTH -> healthSignals.add(tag.name)
            TagCategory.ITEM -> itemSignals.add(tag.name)
            TagCategory.JOURNAL -> {
                // A JOURNAL that starts as a number is a counter; one that
                // starts as a flag, or is not in stats at all, is a flag.
                if (tag.name in adventure.initialState.stats) {
                    numericSignals.add(tag.name)
                } else {
                    boolSignals.add(tag.name)
                }
            }
        }
    }

    // 2. Initial state.
    boolSignals.addAll(adventure.initialState.flags)
    numericSignals.addAll(adventure.initialState.stats.keys)

    // 3. Usage in scenes and choices.
    for (chapter in adventure.chapters) {
        for (scene in chapter.scenes) {
            collectEffectSignals(scene.effects, boolSignals, numericSignals)
            for (choice in scene.choices) {
                choice.condition?.let {
                    collectConditionSignals(it, boolSignals, numericSignals)
                }
                collectEffectSignals(choice.effects, boolSignals, numericSignals)
            }
        }
    }

    // 4. Resolve by priority: HEALTH > ITEM > numeric > Bool.
    val allNames = healthSignals + itemSignals + numericSignals + boolSignals
    val result = mutableMapOf<String, VarDecl>()
    for (name in allNames) {
        val type: VarType = when {
            name in healthSignals -> VarType.IntMin(0)
            name in itemSignals -> VarType.ItemCount
            name in numericSignals -> VarType.IntMin(0)
            name in boolSignals -> VarType.Bool
            else -> continue // unreachable: allNames is the union of the four sets
        }
        result[name] = VarDecl(name = name, type = type)
    }
    return result
}

private fun collectEffectSignals(
    effects: List<Effect>,
    boolSignals: MutableSet<String>,
    numericSignals: MutableSet<String>,
) {
    for (effect in effects) {
        when (effect) {
            is Effect.SetFlag -> boolSignals.add(effect.name)
            is Effect.RemoveFlag -> boolSignals.add(effect.name)
            is Effect.ModifyStat -> numericSignals.add(effect.name)
            // Ф3.1: `Set` is a numeric operation (absolute value), same
            // signal class as `ModifyStat`.
            is Effect.Set -> numericSignals.add(effect.name)
        }
    }
}

private fun collectConditionSignals(
    condition: Condition,
    boolSignals: MutableSet<String>,
    numericSignals: MutableSet<String>,
) {
    when (condition) {
        // Ф3.1: `Literal` has no variable reference — no signal.
        is Condition.Literal -> Unit
        // Ф3.1: `VarRef` reads a Bool variable, same signal class as `Has`.
        is Condition.VarRef -> boolSignals.add(condition.name)
        is Condition.Has -> boolSignals.add(condition.name)
        is Condition.Not -> collectConditionSignals(
            condition.inner, boolSignals, numericSignals,
        )
        is Condition.And -> {
            collectConditionSignals(condition.left, boolSignals, numericSignals)
            collectConditionSignals(condition.right, boolSignals, numericSignals)
        }
        is Condition.Or -> {
            collectConditionSignals(condition.left, boolSignals, numericSignals)
            collectConditionSignals(condition.right, boolSignals, numericSignals)
        }
        is Condition.Compare -> numericSignals.add(condition.varName)
        is Condition.InRange -> numericSignals.add(condition.varName)
    }
}

package com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.types

import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Adventure
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Condition
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Effect
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.InitialState
import kotlinx.serialization.Serializable

/**
 * Declaration of a variable used by an adventure.
 *
 * Variables are declared once in [Adventure.variables] and referenced by
 * name from [Condition] and [Effect]. The type checker (Ф2) resolves
 * every reference against this map and reports unknown or mistyped
 * variables.
 *
 * A declaration does **not** carry a default value: defaults are
 * determined by [type] (see [VarType] KDoc for the per-type defaults).
 * Explicit initial values belong to [InitialState], not here.
 *
 * @property name stable, machine-readable variable name (e.g. `"health"`).
 * @property type declared type used by the type checker.
 */
@Serializable
public data class VarDecl(
    public val name: String,
    public val type: VarType,
)

FILE: engine/src/main/kotlin/com/myapp/adventure/engine/ir/types/VarType.kt
================================================
package com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.types

import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Condition
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Effect
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.InitialState
import kotlinx.serialization.SerialName
import kotlinx.serialization.Serializable

/**
 * Declared type of a variable used in an adventure.
 *
 * The type is what the type checker (Ф2) uses to validate that references
 * in [Condition] and [Effect] are consistent with each other. For example,
 * a `has_sword` condition requires `sword` to be of type [Bool] or
 * [ItemCount]; a `health >= 50` comparison requires `health` to be
 * [Integer], [IntMin], or [IntRange].
 *
 * **Default values** (used when a variable is not present in
 * [InitialState], e.g. before the first scene that sets it):
 *
 * - [Bool] → `false`
 * - [Integer] → `0`
 * - [IntMin] → [IntMin.min] (the lowest allowed value)
 * - [IntRange] → [IntRange.min] (the lowest allowed value)
 * - [ItemCount] → `0`
 * - [ItemList] → `emptyList()`
 *
 * **Why three "numeric" variants.** They encode how the type checker and
 * the runtime should clamp / bound the value:
 *
 * - [Integer] — unbounded. Used for quantities that are not resource-like
 *   (score, computed totals) and for variables whose boundaries are not
 *   the author's concern. No clamp applied by the runtime.
 * - [IntMin] — lower bound only. Used for resources that cannot go
 *   negative but have no natural upper bound (`gold`, some turn counters
 *   before a limit is imposed). Clamp: `>= min`.
 * - [IntRange] — both bounds. Used for resources with an inherent cap
 *   (`health 0..100`, `skill 1..12`, `endurance 20..30`) and for bounded
 *   counters (`turns 0..30`). Clamp: `min..max`.
 *
 * **Why not `IntRange(min: Int, max: Int?)`.** Encoding "no upper bound"
 * as `null` would mix two different semantics in one variant and make the
 * "no lower bound, no upper bound" case ambiguous (both `null` — which is
 * what [Integer] already is). Three explicit variants make every case
 * readable at the JSON level: `"int"`, `"int_min": {min}`,
 * `"int_range": {min, max}`.
 *
 * **Authoring hint.** Ask yourself two questions about the variable:
 * "can it go below zero?" and "can it ever exceed some N?". No to both →
 * [Integer]; yes to the first, no to the second → [IntMin]; yes to both
 * → [IntRange].
 */
@Serializable
public sealed class VarType {

    /** Boolean flag. `true`/`false`. */
    @Serializable
    @SerialName("bool")
    public data object Bool : VarType()

    /**
     * Whole number without bounds. Used for stats like score, totals, or
     * quantities whose boundaries are not the author's concern.
     */
    @Serializable
    @SerialName("int")
    public data object Integer : VarType()

    /**
     * Whole number with a lower bound only ("at least [min], no upper
     * bound").
     *
     * Used for resources that cannot go negative but have no natural
     * upper bound: gold, inventory-like counters the author does not
     * want to cap, turn counters before a limit is imposed.
     *
     * @property min lowest allowed value (inclusive).
     */
    @Serializable
    @SerialName("int_min")
    public data class IntMin(
        public val min: Int,
    ) : VarType()

    /**
     * Whole number clamped to `[min, max]`. Used for stats like health
     * that must stay within a sensible range.
     *
     * @property min lowest allowed value (inclusive).
     * @property max highest allowed value (inclusive).
     */
    @Serializable
    @SerialName("int_range")
    public data class IntRange(
        public val min: Int,
        public val max: Int,
    ) : VarType()

    /**
     * Count of a stackable item (e.g. "3 potions"). Non-negative
     * [Integer] by semantics; kept as a separate type so the type checker
     * can distinguish "how many" from "any number".
     */
    @Serializable
    @SerialName("item_count")
    public data object ItemCount : VarType()

    /**
     * Unordered list of item identifiers. Used for inventory-like
     * variables when the order does not matter.
     *
     * Not to be confused with [ItemCount], which is a single number.
     */
    @Serializable
    @SerialName("item_list")
    public data object ItemList : VarType()
}

package com.myapp.adventure.engine.parse

import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.CompareOp
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Condition

/**
 * Parses a condition string into a [Condition] AST node.
 *
 * **Syntactic only.** This parser knows nothing about variable types or
 * declared variables — that is the type checker's job (Ф2.2). It accepts
 * `has_sword` and produces [Condition.Has] even if `sword` is declared as
 * `ItemCount`; Ф2.2 rejects that with a hint to use `sword > 0` instead.
 *
 * **Grammar (Ф3.2 / N7.base):**
 *
 * ```
 * expr    = or
 * or      = and ("||" and)*
 * and     = not ("&&" not)*
 * not     = "!" not | primary
 * primary = "(" expr ")"
 *         | "true"
 *         | "false"
 *         | "has_" IDENT
 *         | IDENT "in" INT ".." INT
 *         | IDENT COMPARE_OP INT
 * ```
 *
 * **Precedence:** `!` (highest) > `&&` > `||` (lowest). `&&` and `||`
 * are **left-associative**: `a && b && c` parses as `And(And(a, b), c)`,
 * same for `||`.
 *
 * **Associativity and round-trip with [ConditionWriter].**
 * [ConditionWriter] produces a canonical minimal-bracket form; this
 * parser accepts it back. `parse(write(c))` is structurally equal to `c`
 * for the variants listed below.
 *
 * **Round-trip status (as of Ф3.2):**
 *
 * | Variant | Round-trips |
 * |---|---|
 * | `Has`, `Not(Has)`, `Compare` (all 6 ops) | ✅ |
 * | `And`, `Or`, `Not(And)`, `Not(Or)`, `Not(Compare)`, `!!`, `InRange`, `Literal` | ✅ |
 * | `VarRef` | ❌ — not produced by the parser, see below |
 *
 * **`VarRef` is deliberately NOT parsed in Ф3.2.** Bare identifiers
 * (e.g. `"health"`, `"sword && key"` where `sword` / `key` are Bool
 * flags) are parsed as `ConditionError`. Reason: accepting a bare name
 * would be ambiguous with `has_X` (an author with a variable named
 * `has_seen` would have no way to reference it — parser would see
 * `Has("seen")`). `VarRef` is planned for a future phase (see roadmap /
 * progress log), along with `TypeError.VarRefOnNonBool` and the
 * `has_`-prefix reservation. Until then: `has_X` is the only way to
 * reference a Bool variable, and that is the canonical syntax authors
 * have been using since Ф1.3.
 *
 * **Reserved characters.** Flag names (`has_X`) and variable names in
 * `X in A..B` / `X op N` must not contain `&`, `|`, `!`, `<`, `>`, `=`,
 * `(`, `)`. These are part of the condition syntax. A name containing
 * one → `ConditionError` with a fix hint. This catches `has_sword &&
 * health` if the author meant `has_sword && has_health`.
 *
 * **Not supported yet (post-Ф3.2):** `VarRef` (bare Bool reference);
 * `Set`/`Add`/`Sub` as effects (those are not conditions — `ConditionParser`
 * is condition-only); `roll(...)` (Ф12, RNG).
 */
public object ConditionParser {

    /**
     * Parses [input] as a single condition.
     *
     * @return [ParseResult.Success] with the AST node, or
     *   [ParseResult.Failure] with exactly one [ParseError.ConditionError].
     */
    public fun parse(input: String): ParseResult<Condition> {
        val s = input.trim()
        if (s.isEmpty()) {
            return fail("Empty condition string", input, 0)
        }
        return parseExpr(s, input)
    }

    // ---------- Grammar ----------

    private fun parseExpr(text: String, original: String): ParseResult<Condition> {
        val orParts = splitTopLevel(text, "||")
        if (orParts.size > 1) {
            val conditions = mutableListOf<Condition>()
            for (part in orParts) {
                val trimmed = part.trim()
                if (trimmed.isEmpty()) {
                    return fail("Empty operand of '||' in '$original'", original, 0)
                }
                when (val r = parseAnd(trimmed, original)) {
                    is ParseResult.Success -> conditions.add(r.value)
                    is ParseResult.Failure -> return r
                }
            }
            var result = conditions[0]
            for (i in 1 until conditions.size) {
                result = Condition.Or(result, conditions[i])
            }
            return ParseResult.Success(result)
        }
        return parseAnd(text, original)
    }

    private fun parseAnd(text: String, original: String): ParseResult<Condition> {
        val andParts = splitTopLevel(text, "&&")
        if (andParts.size > 1) {
            val conditions = mutableListOf<Condition>()
            for (part in andParts) {
                val trimmed = part.trim()
                if (trimmed.isEmpty()) {
                    return fail("Empty operand of '&&' in '$original'", original, 0)
                }
                when (val r = parseNot(trimmed, original)) {
                    is ParseResult.Success -> conditions.add(r.value)
                    is ParseResult.Failure -> return r
                }
            }
            var result = conditions[0]
            for (i in 1 until conditions.size) {
                result = Condition.And(result, conditions[i])
            }
            return ParseResult.Success(result)
        }
        return parseNot(text, original)
    }

    private fun parseNot(text: String, original: String): ParseResult<Condition> {
        val trimmed = text.trim()
        if (trimmed.isEmpty()) {
            return fail("Empty condition in '$original'", original, 0)
        }
        if (trimmed.startsWith("!") && !trimmed.startsWith("!=")) {
            val inner = trimmed.substring(1).trim()
            if (inner.isEmpty()) {
                return fail("Missing operand after '!' in '$original'", original, 0)
            }
            return when (val r = parseNot(inner, original)) {
                is ParseResult.Success -> ParseResult.Success(Condition.Not(r.value))
                is ParseResult.Failure -> r
            }
        }
        return parsePrimary(trimmed, original)
    }

    private fun parsePrimary(text: String, original: String): ParseResult<Condition> {
        val trimmed = text.trim()
        if (trimmed.isEmpty()) {
            return fail("Empty condition in '$original'", original, 0)
        }

        // Parentheses
        if (trimmed.startsWith("(")) {
            if (!trimmed.endsWith(")")) {
                return fail("Unclosed parenthesis in '$original'", original, 0)
            }
            if (!isMatchingParens(trimmed)) {
                return fail(
                    "Parentheses in '$trimmed' do not form a single group. " +
                            "If you meant to join multiple conditions, use '&&' or '||'.",
                    original,
                    0,
                )
            }
            return parseExpr(trimmed.substring(1, trimmed.length - 1), original)
        }

        // Literal
        if (trimmed == "true") return ParseResult.Success(Condition.Literal(true))
        if (trimmed == "false") return ParseResult.Success(Condition.Literal(false))

        // has_X
        if (trimmed.startsWith("has_")) {
            val name = trimmed.removePrefix("has_").trim()
            if (name.isEmpty()) {
                return fail("Missing variable name after 'has_' in '$original'", original, 0)
            }
            checkNoReservedChars(name, original, "Flag name")?.let { return it }
            return ParseResult.Success(Condition.Has(name))
        }

        // InRange: X in A..B
        val inRangeMatch = IN_RANGE_REGEX.find(trimmed)
        if (inRangeMatch != null) {
            val varName = inRangeMatch.groupValues[1].trim()
            if (varName.isEmpty()) {
                return fail("Missing variable name before 'in' in '$original'", original, 0)
            }
            checkNoReservedChars(varName, original, "Variable name")?.let { return it }
            val minStr = inRangeMatch.groupValues[2]
            val maxStr = inRangeMatch.groupValues[3]
            val min = minStr.toIntOrNull()
                ?: return fail("Expected integer after 'in', got '$minStr' in '$original'", original, 0)
            val max = maxStr.toIntOrNull()
                ?: return fail("Expected integer after '..', got '$maxStr' in '$original'", original, 0)
            return ParseResult.Success(Condition.InRange(varName, min, max))
        }

        // Compare: X <op> N. Two-char ops first so `>=` is not consumed as `>` + `=`.
        val compareOps = listOf(
            ">=" to CompareOp.GE,
            "<=" to CompareOp.LE,
            "==" to CompareOp.EQ,
            "!=" to CompareOp.NE,
            ">" to CompareOp.GT,
            "<" to CompareOp.LT,
        )
        for ((opStr, op) in compareOps) {
            val idx = trimmed.indexOf(opStr)
            if (idx <= 0) continue
            val varName = trimmed.substring(0, idx).trim()
            val valueStr = trimmed.substring(idx + opStr.length).trim()
            val value = valueStr.toIntOrNull() ?: continue
            if (varName.isEmpty()) continue
            checkNoReservedChars(varName, original, "Variable name")?.let { return it }
            return ParseResult.Success(Condition.Compare(varName, op, value))
        }

        return fail(
            "Unrecognized condition syntax: '$trimmed'. " +
                    "Expected one of: 'has_X', '!has_X', 'X <op> N', " +
                    "'X in A..B', 'true', 'false', a parenthesized expression, " +
                    "or '&&' / '||' joining any two of the above.",
            original,
            0,
        )
    }

    // ---------- Helpers ----------

    private val IN_RANGE_REGEX = Regex("""^(.+?)\s+in\s+(-?\d+)\s*\.\.\s*(-?\d+)$""")

    /**
     * Splits [input] by [op] at the top parenthesis level. `||` / `&&`
     * inside `(...)` do not split the outer expression:
     * `(a || b) && c` splits only by `&&`.
     */
    private fun splitTopLevel(input: String, op: String): List<String> {
        val parts = mutableListOf<String>()
        var depth = 0
        var start = 0
        var i = 0
        while (i < input.length) {
            when (input[i]) {
                '(' -> { depth++; i++ }
                ')' -> { depth--; i++ }
                else -> {
                    if (depth == 0 && input.startsWith(op, i)) {
                        parts.add(input.substring(start, i))
                        i += op.length
                        start = i
                    } else {
                        i++
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        parts.add(input.substring(start))
        return parts
    }

    /**
     * True iff [s] starts with `(`, ends with `)`, and the opening `(`
     * matches the final `)`. `"(a) && (b)"` returns false — the first
     * `(` matches the `)` at index 2, not the last `)`.
     */
    private fun isMatchingParens(s: String): Boolean {
        if (!s.startsWith("(") || !s.endsWith(")")) return false
        var depth = 0
        for (i in s.indices) {
            when (s[i]) {
                '(' -> depth++
                ')' -> {
                    depth--
                    if (depth == 0 && i < s.length - 1) return false
                }
            }
        }
        return depth == 0
    }

    private val RESERVED_CHARS: Set<Char> = setOf('&', '|', '!', '<', '>', '=', '(', ')')

    private fun checkNoReservedChars(
        value: String,
        input: String,
        forWhat: String,
    ): ParseResult.Failure? {
        val bad = value.firstOrNull { it in RESERVED_CHARS }
        if (bad != null) {
            return fail(
                "$forWhat '$value' contains reserved character '$bad'. " +
                        "Logical operators (&&, ||, !), comparisons, and parentheses " +
                        "are part of the condition syntax, not the variable name.",
                input,
                0,
            )
        }
        return null
    }

    private fun fail(message: String, input: String, position: Int): ParseResult.Failure =
        ParseResult.Failure(listOf(ParseError.ConditionError(message, input, position)))
}

package com.myapp.adventure.engine.parse

import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.CompareOp
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Condition

/**
 * Writes a [Condition] AST back into a string in the format accepted by
 * [ConditionParser].
 *
 * **Symmetry with [ConditionParser].** The two objects form a round-trip:
 * for a condition that the parser can produce today, `parse(write(c)) ==
 * c` (structurally). This is the contract that makes the editor (Ф9.2)
 * able to represent a condition in JSON: the editor holds a
 * `Condition` in memory, and when the author saves, [write] serializes
 * it back into the `"condition"` field. If the two sides did not
 * round-trip, saving a file would silently change the meaning of a
 * condition — the worst possible failure mode.
 *
 * **What round-trips today.** Only the variants the parser produces:
 * - [Condition.Has]
 * - [Condition.Not]`(`[Condition.Has]`)`
 * - [Condition.Compare] (all 6 [CompareOp] values)
 *
 * **What does NOT round-trip today** (writer produces a string, parser
 * rejects it):
 * - [Condition.And] → `"a && b"` (parser: `&` is a reserved char).
 * - [Condition.Or] → `"a || b"` (`|` is reserved).
 * - [Condition.Not] where the inner is not `Has` — e.g.
 *   `Not(Compare(...))` → `"!(health >= 50)"` (parser: `!` only
 *   recognized as `!has_`).
 * - `Not(Not(...))` → `"!!has_x"` (parser: `!!` not recognized).
 * - [Condition.Literal] → `"true"` / `"false"` (no literal syntax).
 * - [Condition.VarRef] → bare name, e.g. `"sword"` (parser: a bare
 *   name without an operator is `ConditionError`).
 * - [Condition.InRange] → `"x in 0..10"` (parser: `in` / `..` not
 *   supported yet).
 *
 * These are all resolved by **Ф3.2 (N7.base)**, which extends
 * [ConditionParser] with `&&`, `||`, `!`, parentheses, and `X in a..b`.
 * The writer's output for these variants is already **canonical** — it
 * is the syntax that Ф3.2 will accept. Tests in
 * [ConditionWriterTest] pin both the string output (which is already
 * correct) and the current round-trip failure (which will flip to
 * success when Ф3.2 lands).
 *
 * **Canonical form.** The writer produces the **minimal-bracket** form
 * that respects precedence: `!` (highest) > `&&` > `||` (lowest).
 * Leaves ([Condition.Has], [Condition.Compare], [Condition.InRange],
 * [Condition.Literal], [Condition.VarRef]) are always at the top, no
 * brackets around them.
 *
 * For example:
 * - `And(Has("a"), Or(Has("b"), Has("c")))` → `"has_a && (has_b || has_c)"`.
 * - `Or(And(Has("a"), Has("b")), Has("c"))` → `"has_a && has_b || has_c"`.
 * - `Not(And(Has("a"), Has("b")))` → `"!(has_a && has_b)"`.
 * - `And(And(Has("a"), Has("b")), Has("c"))` → `"has_a && has_b && has_c"`
 *   (associative, no extra brackets).
 *
 * **What is NOT the writer's job.**
 * - **No simplification.** `And(Literal(true), Has("x"))` is written as
 *   `"true && has_x"`, not `"has_x"`. Simplification is a separate
 *   concern (`ConditionSimplifier`, future — Ф3.2 or later).
 * - **No effect writing.** `Effect` AST → string (the `"set_flags"` /
 *   `"modify_stats"` fields) is `IrToJson` (Ф8), not this writer.
 * - **No whitespace preferences.** `"a && b"` (single spaces) is what
 *   the writer produces; the parser accepts any whitespace. The writer
 *   is canonical, the parser is lenient.
 *
 * **Known corner case** (documented, not fixed): a variable whose name
 * starts with `"has_"` cannot be referenced from [Condition.VarRef] or
 * [Condition.Compare] unambiguously — the parser will interpret
 * `"has_x"` as `Has("x")`, not as `VarRef("has_x")` or as the start of a
 * comparison. This is a naming collision in the author's file, not a bug
 * in the writer. Ф3.2 will define the disambiguation rule (probably:
 * reserved prefix, rejected by [com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.types.TypeChecker]).
 */
public object ConditionWriter {

    /**
     * Serializes [condition] into the condition-string format accepted
     * by [ConditionParser.parse].
     *
     * The output is **canonical**: single spaces around binary operators,
     * no trailing whitespace, minimal brackets (only where precedence
     * requires them).
     */
    public fun write(condition: Condition): String =
        writeWithPrecedence(condition, minPrecedence = PREC_OR)

    // ---------- Precedence ----------

    /** Leaves: no internal boolean operators. */
    private const val PREC_LEAF = 3

    /** Unary prefix `!`. */
    private const val PREC_NOT = 2

    /** `&&`. */
    private const val PREC_AND = 1

    /** `||`. */
    private const val PREC_OR = 0

    private fun precedence(c: Condition): Int = when (c) {
        is Condition.Literal,
        is Condition.VarRef,
        is Condition.Has,
        is Condition.Compare,
        is Condition.InRange,
            -> PREC_LEAF
        is Condition.Not -> PREC_NOT
        is Condition.And -> PREC_AND
        is Condition.Or -> PREC_OR
    }

    // ---------- Core writer ----------

    /**
     * Writes [c] and, if its precedence is **strictly lower** than
     * [minPrecedence], wraps the result in `(…)`.
     *
     * Precedence is a partial order: `!` > `&&` > `||`. A child whose
     * precedence equals the parent's does **not** get brackets — `&&`
     * and `||` are associative, so `a && b && c` is unambiguous
     * regardless of the tree shape.
     */
    private fun writeWithPrecedence(c: Condition, minPrecedence: Int): String {
        val body = when (c) {
            is Condition.Literal -> if (c.value) "true" else "false"
            is Condition.VarRef -> c.name
            is Condition.Has -> "has_${c.name}"
            is Condition.Compare -> "${c.varName} ${opSymbol(c.op)} ${c.value}"
            is Condition.InRange -> "${c.varName} in ${c.min}..${c.max}"
            is Condition.Not -> "!" + writeNotChild(c.inner)
            is Condition.And ->
                writeWithPrecedence(c.left, PREC_AND) + " && " +
                        writeWithPrecedence(c.right, PREC_AND)
            is Condition.Or ->
                writeWithPrecedence(c.left, PREC_OR) + " || " +
                        writeWithPrecedence(c.right, PREC_OR)
        }
        return if (precedence(c) < minPrecedence) "($body)" else body
    }

    /**
     * Writes the child of a `!` prefix.
     *
     * Precedence alone is **not** enough for this position. `!` is a
     * prefix operator, and `!x > 5` reads as `(!x) > 5` in most
     * languages, not `!(x > 5)`. Bracket decisions are therefore made
     * per-variant, not by precedence:
     *
     * - `Has`, `VarRef`, `Literal`, `Not` → **no brackets**
     *   (`!has_x`, `!x`, `!true`, `!!y` — all unambiguous).
     * - `Compare`, `InRange`, `And`, `Or` → **brackets**
     *   (`!(x >= 5)`, `!(x in 0..10)`, `!(a && b)`, `!(a || b)` — a
     *   bare `!` would bind to the first token of the child, not the
     *   whole expression).
     *
     * `Not` recurses here rather than via `writeWithPrecedence` so that
     * `Not(Not(Has("a")))` produces `"!!has_a"` (no parenthesised
     * `"!(!has_a)"`), which is the canonical form the parser will
     * accept once Ф3.2 supports `!!`.
     */
    private fun writeNotChild(c: Condition): String = when (c) {
        is Condition.Has -> "has_${c.name}"
        is Condition.VarRef -> c.name
        is Condition.Literal -> if (c.value) "true" else "false"
        is Condition.Not -> "!" + writeNotChild(c.inner)
        is Condition.Compare, is Condition.InRange, is Condition.And, is Condition.Or ->
            "(" + writeWithPrecedence(c, PREC_OR) + ")"
    }

    // ---------- Operator symbols ----------

    private fun opSymbol(op: CompareOp): String = when (op) {
        CompareOp.LT -> "<"
        CompareOp.LE -> "<="
        CompareOp.GT -> ">"
        CompareOp.GE -> ">="
        CompareOp.EQ -> "=="
        CompareOp.NE -> "!="
    }
}

package com.myapp.adventure.engine.parse

/**
 * A single error produced by the JSON parser ([JsonToIr]) or by the
 * condition parser ([ConditionParser]).
 *
 * The parser never throws. It accumulates errors and returns them all at
 * once in [ParseResult.Failure], so that the editor and the analyzer can
 * show the author every problem in one pass instead of one at a time.
 *
 * **Not** `@Serializable`: parse errors are an API for the caller, not part
 * of the on-disk format. If they ever need to be persisted (e.g. in a
 * validation report), serialize them separately.
 */
public sealed class ParseError {

    /** Human-readable, English, one sentence. */
    public abstract val message: String

    /**
     * JSON-level syntax error: malformed input, unknown field with
     * strict mode, wrong type for a well-known field.
     *
     * @property path JSON path to the offending value
     *   (e.g. `"chapters[0].scenes[2].choices[0].condition"`), when known.
     */
    public data class Syntax(
        override val message: String,
        public val path: String? = null,
    ) : ParseError()

    /**
     * Structural problem that is not a JSON syntax error: empty chapter
     * list, blank scene id, empty `next_scene`, etc.
     *
     * @property path same convention as [Syntax.path].
     */
    public data class Structure(
        override val message: String,
        public val path: String? = null,
    ) : ParseError()

    /**
     * Condition string could not be parsed into
     * [com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Condition].
     *
     * @property input the raw condition string from JSON.
     * @property position 0-based offset in [input] where the parser gave up,
     *   when determinable.
     * @property path JSON path to the offending condition
     *   (e.g. `"chapters[1:c2].scenes[0:start].choices[2].condition"`),
     *   filled in by [JsonToIr] when accumulating errors. `null` when the
     *   error came from a standalone [ConditionParser] call.
     */
    public data class ConditionError(
        override val message: String,
        public val input: String,
        public val position: Int? = null,
        public val path: String? = null,
    ) : ParseError()
}

package com.myapp.adventure.engine.parse

import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.types.TypeError

/**
 * Result of a parse operation: either a value of type [T] or an error
 * describing why parsing failed.
 *
 * Chosen over Kotlin's stdlib [Result] because:
 * - [Result.Failure] carries a single [Throwable], not a list of errors.
 * - Wrapping [ParseError] in an exception would lose the structured type
 *   (the caller wants to pattern-match on [ParseError.ConditionError] etc.).
 *
 * **Two-stage pipeline (Ф2.3).** Starting with Ф2.3,
 * [com.myapp.adventure.engine.format.JsonToIr.parse] performs **two**
 * checks in sequence:
 * 1. **Parse** (JSON syntax, structural problems, condition syntax) —
 *    produces [ParseError]s.
 * 2. **Type check** ([com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.types.TypeChecker.check],
 *    Ф2.2) — unknown variables, wrong types — produces
 *    [TypeError]s.
 *
 * The two stages are sequential and mutually exclusive in [Failure]:
 * - if parsing fails, type checking is **not attempted** — a partial IR
 *   has missing conditions and effects (a choice whose condition string
 *   failed to parse has `condition = null`), so type checking it would
 *   produce false negatives at best, and false positives at worst. Result:
 *   `Failure(errors = [...], typeErrors = emptyList())`.
 * - if parsing succeeds, type checking runs on the full IR. Result:
 *   `Success(ir)` when there are no type errors, or
 *   `Failure(errors = emptyList(), typeErrors = [...])` otherwise.
 *
 * **Invariant (enforced in `init`):** [Failure] contains **exactly one**
 * non-empty list — either [Failure.errors] or [Failure.typeErrors].
 * Both empty would be a `Success`; both non-empty would mean the two
 * stages overlapped, which contradicts the sequential design.
 *
 * **Why not a single `List<ParseError>` that includes type errors as a
 * variant.** The two error kinds come from different layers of the
 * pipeline (parser vs type checker) and carry different structured data
 * ([ParseError] has JSON paths and condition fragments; [TypeError] has
 * variable names and types). Merging them into one list would blur the
 * I3 boundary between "the file cannot be parsed" and "the file parses,
 * but its variable references are wrong". Two fields keep the boundary
 * visible in the type system.
 */
public sealed class ParseResult<out T> {

    /** Successful parse + type check. */
    public data class Success<T>(public val value: T) : ParseResult<T>()

    /**
     * Failed parse or failed type check.
     *
     * @property errors JSON syntax / structural / condition-syntax errors,
     *   produced by the parser. Non-empty iff parsing failed.
     * @property typeErrors type errors from
     *   [com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.types.TypeChecker.check], produced
     *   after a fully successful parse. Non-empty iff parsing succeeded
     *   but the IR has semantic problems. See class KDoc for the pipeline.
     *
     * **Exactly one** of [errors] / [typeErrors] is non-empty; enforced by
     * the `init` block below.
     */
    public data class Failure(
        public val errors: List<ParseError>,
        public val typeErrors: List<TypeError> = emptyList(),
    ) : ParseResult<Nothing>() {
        init {
            require(errors.isNotEmpty() || typeErrors.isNotEmpty()) {
                "ParseResult.Failure must contain at least one error in " +
                        "`errors` (parse) or `typeErrors` (type check)"
            }
            require(!(errors.isNotEmpty() && typeErrors.isNotEmpty())) {
                "ParseResult.Failure must not contain both parse errors and type errors: " +
                        "type checking runs only on a fully parsed IR (Ф2.3 / B1 decision). " +
                        "Got ${errors.size} parse errors and ${typeErrors.size} type errors."
            }
        }
    }
}
