            SceneId("a"),
            ChoiceId("c"),
        )
        val success = assertIs<StepResult.Success>(result)
        assertEquals(false, success.isDead)
        assertEquals(90, success.state.stats["health"])
    }

    @Test
    fun `no health declared - not dead`() {
        val a = scene("a", listOf(choice("c", next = "b")))
        val b = scene("b")
        val compiled = compile(adventure(chapter("ch", a, b)))

        val result = Engine.step(compiled, state(), SceneId("a"), ChoiceId("c"))
        val success = assertIs<StepResult.Success>(result)
        assertEquals(false, success.isDead)
    }

    // ---------- cross-chapter ----------

    @Test
    fun `cross-chapter transition - success`() {
        val a = scene("a", listOf(choice("c", next = "b")))
        val b = scene("b")
        val compiled = compile(adventure(chapter("ch1", a), chapter("ch2", b)))

        val result = Engine.step(compiled, state(), SceneId("a"), ChoiceId("c"))
        val success = assertIs<StepResult.Success>(result)
        assertEquals(SceneId("b"), success.currentScene.id)
    }

    // ---------- real test_adventure.json: documented pre-Continue state ----------

    @Test
    fun `chapter_end_1 has explicit Continue choice - player can proceed after gate`() {
        // Ф1.5.5.0: chapter_end_1 and chapter_end_2 now have explicit
        // "Continue" choices. This is the "test first, then fix" pattern:
        // the previous test asserted "no choices"; after the fix, the
        // scene must have exactly one Continue choice, and step() with it
        // must succeed once the gate (5 steps) is passed.
        val json = loadResource("/test_adventure.json")
        val parseResult = JsonToIr.parse(json)
        val adventure = assertIs<ParseResult.Success<Adventure>>(parseResult).value
        val compiled = assertIs<CompileResult.Success>(Engine.compile(adventure)).compiled

        val chapterEnd1 = assertNotNull(compiled.scenesById[SceneId("chapter_end_1")])
        assertEquals(1, chapterEnd1.choices.size, "chapter_end_1 should have one Continue choice")
        val continueChoice = chapterEnd1.choices.single()
        assertEquals("Продолжить", continueChoice.text)
        assertEquals(SceneId("conditions_test"), continueChoice.nextScene)

        // Gate 1 (Ф1.7.0.4 simplified all test gates to 1 step so the
        // reference sample can be checked by walking — one step is
        // enough to exercise the mechanic). stepsInScene = 0 → blocked.
        val blocked = rejected(
            Engine.step(
                compiled,
                state = adventure.initialState.toPlayerState(),
                sceneId = SceneId("chapter_end_1"),
                choiceId = continueChoice.id,
                stepsInScene = 0,
            ),
        )
        val blockedReason = assertIs<RejectReason.Blocked>(blocked)
        assertEquals(1, (blockedReason.blockers.single() as Blocker.GateNotPassed).remainingSteps)

        // Gate 1, stepsInScene = 1 → success, moves to conditions_test.
        val success = assertIs<StepResult.Success>(
            Engine.step(
                compiled,
                state = adventure.initialState.toPlayerState(),
                sceneId = SceneId("chapter_end_1"),
                choiceId = continueChoice.id,
                stepsInScene = 1,
            ),
        )
        assertEquals(SceneId("conditions_test"), success.currentScene.id)
    }

    @Test
    fun `chapter_end_2 has explicit Continue choice going to final`() {
        val json = loadResource("/test_adventure.json")
        val parseResult = JsonToIr.parse(json)
        val adventure = assertIs<ParseResult.Success<Adventure>>(parseResult).value
        val compiled = assertIs<CompileResult.Success>(Engine.compile(adventure)).compiled

        val chapterEnd2 = assertNotNull(compiled.scenesById[SceneId("chapter_end_2")])
        assertEquals(1, chapterEnd2.choices.size)
        val continueChoice = chapterEnd2.choices.single()
        assertEquals("Продолжить", continueChoice.text)
        assertEquals(SceneId("final"), continueChoice.nextScene)
    }

    // ---------- Ф4.5: merge points ----------

    @Test
    fun `merge point receives accumulated delta from either branch`() {
        val left = scene(
            "left",
            choices = listOf(
                choice(
                    id = "take_left",
                    next = "merge",
                    effects = listOf(
                        Effect.ModifyStat("health", -10),
                        Effect.SetFlag("chose_left"),
                    ),
                ),
            ),
        )
        val right = scene(
            "right",
            choices = listOf(
                choice(
                    id = "take_right",
                    next = "merge",
                    effects = listOf(
                        Effect.ModifyStat("health", 5),
                        Effect.SetFlag("chose_right"),
                    ),
                ),
            ),
        )
        val merge = scene(
            id = "merge",
            isMerge = true,
            mergeSources = listOf(SceneId("left"), SceneId("right")),
        )
        val compiled = compile(adventure(chapter("ch", left, right, merge)))
        val initial = state(stats = mapOf("health" to 100))

        val fromLeft = assertIs<StepResult.Success>(
            Engine.step(compiled, initial, SceneId("left"), ChoiceId("take_left")),
        )
        assertEquals(SceneId("merge"), fromLeft.currentScene.id)
        assertEquals(90, fromLeft.state.stats["health"])
        assertEquals(setOf("chose_left"), fromLeft.state.flags)

        val fromRight = assertIs<StepResult.Success>(
            Engine.step(compiled, initial, SceneId("right"), ChoiceId("take_right")),
        )
        assertEquals(SceneId("merge"), fromRight.currentScene.id)
        assertEquals(105, fromRight.state.stats["health"])
        assertEquals(setOf("chose_right"), fromRight.state.flags)
    }

    // ---------- Ф4.7: subroutines ----------

    private fun consumeSubroutine(): Subroutine = Subroutine(
        id = "consume",
        inputs = listOf(
            VarDecl("item", VarType.ItemCount),
            VarDecl("health", VarType.IntMin(0)),
        ),
        outputs = listOf(
            VarDecl("item", VarType.ItemCount),
            VarDecl("health", VarType.IntMin(0)),
        ),
        body = listOf(
            SubroutineStep(
                condition = Condition.Compare("item", CompareOp.GT, 0),
                effects = listOf(
                    Effect.ModifyStat("item", -1),
                    Effect.ModifyStat("health", 5),
                ),
            ),
        ),
    )

    @Test
    fun `subroutine called from two scenes returns state to each caller`() {
        val consume = consumeSubroutine()
        val a = scene(
            "a",
            choices = listOf(
                choice(
                    id = "use_a",
                    next = "a",
                    call = SubroutineCall(
                        subroutineId = "consume",
                        args = mapOf("item" to "potion", "health" to "health"),
                        outputs = mapOf("item" to "potion", "health" to "health"),
                    ),
                ),
            ),
        )
        val b = scene(
            "b",
            choices = listOf(
                choice(
                    id = "use_b",
                    next = "b",
                    call = SubroutineCall(
                        subroutineId = "consume",
                        args = mapOf("item" to "elixir", "health" to "health"),
                        outputs = mapOf("item" to "elixir", "health" to "health"),
                    ),
                ),
            ),
        )
        val compiled = compile(
            adventure(chapter("ch", a, b), subroutines = listOf(consume)),
        )
        val initial = state(
            stats = mapOf("potion" to 1, "elixir" to 2, "health" to 10),
        )

        val fromA = assertIs<StepResult.Success>(
            Engine.step(compiled, initial, SceneId("a"), ChoiceId("use_a")),
        )
        assertEquals(SceneId("a"), fromA.currentScene.id)
        assertEquals(0, fromA.state.stats["potion"])
        assertEquals(2, fromA.state.stats["elixir"])
        assertEquals(15, fromA.state.stats["health"])

        val fromB = assertIs<StepResult.Success>(
            Engine.step(compiled, initial, SceneId("b"), ChoiceId("use_b")),
        )
        assertEquals(SceneId("b"), fromB.currentScene.id)
        assertEquals(1, fromB.state.stats["potion"])
        assertEquals(1, fromB.state.stats["elixir"])
        assertEquals(15, fromB.state.stats["health"])
    }

    @Test
    fun `nested subroutine calls preserve the frame stack`() {
        val addFive = Subroutine(
            id = "add_five",
            inputs = listOf(VarDecl("health", VarType.IntMin(0))),
            outputs = listOf(VarDecl("health", VarType.IntMin(0))),
            body = listOf(
                SubroutineStep(effects = listOf(Effect.ModifyStat("health", 5))),
            ),
        )
        val addTen = Subroutine(
            id = "add_ten",
            inputs = listOf(VarDecl("health", VarType.IntMin(0))),
            outputs = listOf(VarDecl("health", VarType.IntMin(0))),
            body = listOf(
                SubroutineStep(
                    call = SubroutineCall(
                        subroutineId = "add_five",
                        args = mapOf("health" to "health"),
                        outputs = mapOf("health" to "health"),
                    ),
                ),
                SubroutineStep(
                    call = SubroutineCall(
                        subroutineId = "add_five",
                        args = mapOf("health" to "health"),
                        outputs = mapOf("health" to "health"),
                    ),
                ),
            ),
        )
        val s = scene(
            "s",
            choices = listOf(
                choice(
                    id = "boost",
                    next = "s",
                    call = SubroutineCall(
                        subroutineId = "add_ten",
                        args = mapOf("health" to "health"),
                        outputs = mapOf("health" to "health"),
                    ),
                ),
            ),
        )
        val compiled = compile(
            adventure(chapter("ch", s), subroutines = listOf(addFive, addTen)),
        )

        val result = assertIs<StepResult.Success>(
            Engine.step(
                compiled,
                state(stats = mapOf("health" to 10)),
                SceneId("s"),
                ChoiceId("boost"),
            ),
        )
        assertEquals(20, result.state.stats["health"])
    }

    @Test
    fun `invariants are evaluated after subroutine outputs`() {
        val kill = Subroutine(
            id = "kill",
            inputs = listOf(VarDecl("health", VarType.IntMin(0))),
            outputs = listOf(VarDecl("health", VarType.IntMin(0))),
            body = listOf(
                SubroutineStep(effects = listOf(Effect.Set("health", 0))),
            ),
        )
        val s = scene(
            "s",
            choices = listOf(
                choice(
                    id = "die",
                    next = "s",
                    call = SubroutineCall(
                        subroutineId = "kill",
                        args = mapOf("health" to "health"),
                        outputs = mapOf("health" to "health"),
                    ),
                ),
            ),
        )
        val compiled = compile(
            adventure(chapter("ch", s), subroutines = listOf(kill)),
        )

        val result = assertIs<StepResult.Success>(
            Engine.step(
                compiled,
                state(stats = mapOf("health" to 10)),
                SceneId("s"),
                ChoiceId("die"),
            ),
        )
        assertEquals(0, result.state.stats["health"])
        assertEquals(Outcome.Death, result.outcome)
    }

    @Test
    fun `guarded subroutine step is skipped when condition is false`() {
        val consume = consumeSubroutine()
        val s = scene(
            "s",
            choices = listOf(
                choice(
                    id = "try",
                    next = "s",
                    call = SubroutineCall(
                        subroutineId = "consume",
                        args = mapOf("item" to "potion", "health" to "health"),
                        outputs = mapOf("item" to "potion", "health" to "health"),
                    ),
                ),
            ),
        )
        val compiled = compile(
            adventure(chapter("ch", s), subroutines = listOf(consume)),
        )

        val result = assertIs<StepResult.Success>(
            Engine.step(
                compiled,
                state(stats = mapOf("potion" to 0, "health" to 10)),
                SceneId("s"),
                ChoiceId("try"),
            ),
        )
        assertEquals(0, result.state.stats["potion"])
        assertEquals(10, result.state.stats["health"])
    }

    private fun loadResource(path: String): String {
        val stream = javaClass.getResourceAsStream(path)
            ?: error("Resource '$path' not found on classpath")
        return stream.bufferedReader().use { it.readText() }
    }

package com.myapp.adventure.engine

import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.CompareOp
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Condition
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.PlayerState
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Choice
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.ChoiceId
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.SceneId
import kotlin.test.Test
import kotlin.test.assertEquals
import kotlin.test.assertFalse
import kotlin.test.assertIs
import kotlin.test.assertTrue

class EvaluatorTest {

    private fun state(
        flags: Set<String> = emptySet(),
        stats: Map<String, Int> = emptyMap(),
    ): PlayerState = PlayerState(flags = flags, stats = stats)

    // ---------- evaluate(): Boolean wrapper (Ф1.5) ----------

    @Test
    fun `has flag true when present`() {
        val s = state(flags = setOf("sword"))
        assertTrue(Evaluator.evaluate(Condition.Has("sword"), s))
    }

    @Test
    fun `has flag false when absent`() {
        assertFalse(Evaluator.evaluate(Condition.Has("sword"), state()))
    }

    @Test
    fun `has does not look at stats - sword in stats but not flags is false`() {
        // Regression for the Ф1.5 decision: `has_X` is only for Bool flags.
        // `sword` in `stats` (ItemCount) is NOT a flag; type checker in
        // Ф2.2 will reject `has_sword` on `sword: ItemCount`, but until
        // then the evaluator is strict.
        val s = state(stats = mapOf("sword" to 1))
        assertFalse(Evaluator.evaluate(Condition.Has("sword"), s))
    }

    @Test
    fun `not inverts`() {
        val s = state(flags = setOf("sword"))
        assertFalse(Evaluator.evaluate(Condition.Not(Condition.Has("sword")), s))
        assertTrue(Evaluator.evaluate(Condition.Not(Condition.Has("bow")), s))
    }

    @Test
    fun `and requires both`() {
        val s = state(flags = setOf("a"))
        assertTrue(
            Evaluator.evaluate(
                Condition.And(Condition.Has("a"), Condition.Not(Condition.Has("b"))),
                s,
            ),
        )
        assertFalse(
            Evaluator.evaluate(
                Condition.And(Condition.Has("a"), Condition.Has("b")),
                s,
            ),
        )
    }

    @Test
    fun `or requires one`() {
        val s = state(flags = setOf("a"))
        assertTrue(
            Evaluator.evaluate(
                Condition.Or(Condition.Has("a"), Condition.Has("b")),
                s,
            ),
        )
    }

    @Test
    fun `compare all operators`() {
        val s = state(stats = mapOf("health" to 50))
        assertTrue(Evaluator.evaluate(Condition.Compare("health", CompareOp.GE, 50), s))
        assertTrue(Evaluator.evaluate(Condition.Compare("health", CompareOp.LE, 50), s))
        assertTrue(Evaluator.evaluate(Condition.Compare("health", CompareOp.EQ, 50), s))
        assertTrue(Evaluator.evaluate(Condition.Compare("health", CompareOp.NE, 49), s))
        assertTrue(Evaluator.evaluate(Condition.Compare("health", CompareOp.GT, 49), s))
        assertTrue(Evaluator.evaluate(Condition.Compare("health", CompareOp.LT, 51), s))
        assertFalse(Evaluator.evaluate(Condition.Compare("health", CompareOp.GT, 50), s))
        assertFalse(Evaluator.evaluate(Condition.Compare("health", CompareOp.LT, 50), s))
    }

    @Test
    fun `compare unknown stat defaults to zero`() {
        assertTrue(Evaluator.evaluate(Condition.Compare("mana", CompareOp.EQ, 0), state()))
        assertTrue(Evaluator.evaluate(Condition.Compare("mana", CompareOp.GE, 0), state()))
        assertFalse(Evaluator.evaluate(Condition.Compare("mana", CompareOp.GT, 0), state()))
    }

    @Test
    fun `in range inclusive`() {
        val s = state(stats = mapOf("health" to 50))
        assertTrue(Evaluator.evaluate(Condition.InRange("health", 50, 50), s))
        assertTrue(Evaluator.evaluate(Condition.InRange("health", 0, 100), s))
        assertFalse(Evaluator.evaluate(Condition.InRange("health", 51, 100), s))
    }

    @Test
    fun `is dead only when health at or below zero`() {
        assertFalse(Evaluator.isDead(state(stats = mapOf("health" to 1))))
        assertTrue(Evaluator.isDead(state(stats = mapOf("health" to 0))))
        assertTrue(Evaluator.isDead(state(stats = mapOf("health" to -5))))
    }

    @Test
    fun `is dead is false when health not declared`() {
        // "no health" means the adventure does not use death.
        assertFalse(Evaluator.isDead(state()))
    }

    // ---------- Ф3.1: Literal and VarRef ----------

    @Test
    fun `literal true evaluates to true`() {
        assertTrue(Evaluator.evaluate(Condition.Literal(true), state()))
    }

    @Test
    fun `literal false evaluates to false`() {
        assertFalse(Evaluator.evaluate(Condition.Literal(false), state()))
    }

    @Test
    fun `var ref reads flags same as has`() {
        val s = state(flags = setOf("sword"))
        assertTrue(Evaluator.evaluate(Condition.VarRef("sword"), s))
        assertFalse(Evaluator.evaluate(Condition.VarRef("bow"), s))
    }

    // ---------- Ф3.3: evaluateWithReason ----------

    @Test
    fun `success result for true condition`() {
        val result = Evaluator.evaluateWithReason(
            Condition.Has("sword"),
            state(flags = setOf("sword")),
        )
        assertEquals(EvaluationResult.Success, result)
    }

    @Test
    fun `has failed reason`() {
        val result = Evaluator.evaluateWithReason(Condition.Has("sword"), state())
        assertEquals(
            EvaluationResult.Failure(Reason.HasFailed("sword")),
            result,
        )
    }

    @Test
    fun `var ref failed reason`() {
        val result = Evaluator.evaluateWithReason(Condition.VarRef("sword"), state())
        assertEquals(
            EvaluationResult.Failure(Reason.VarRefFailed("sword")),
            result,
        )
    }

    @Test
    fun `literal false reason`() {
        val result = Evaluator.evaluateWithReason(Condition.Literal(false), state())
        assertEquals(
            EvaluationResult.Failure(Reason.LiteralFailed),
            result,
        )
    }

    @Test
    fun `compare failed reason carries actual and expected`() {
        val result = Evaluator.evaluateWithReason(
            Condition.Compare("health", CompareOp.GE, 50),
            state(stats = mapOf("health" to 30)),
        )
        assertEquals(
            EvaluationResult.Failure(
                Reason.CompareFailed(
                    varName = "health",
                    op = CompareOp.GE,
                    actualValue = 30,
                    expectedValue = 50,
                )
            ),
            result,
        )
    }

    @Test
    fun `compare failed on missing stat reports actual zero`() {
        val result = Evaluator.evaluateWithReason(
            Condition.Compare("mana", CompareOp.GT, 0),
            state(),
        )
        assertEquals(
            EvaluationResult.Failure(
                Reason.CompareFailed(
                    varName = "mana",
                    op = CompareOp.GT,
                    actualValue = 0,
                    expectedValue = 0,
                )
            ),
            result,
        )
    }

    @Test
    fun `in range failed reason`() {
        val result = Evaluator.evaluateWithReason(
            Condition.InRange("health", 50, 100),
            state(stats = mapOf("health" to 30)),
        )
        assertEquals(
            EvaluationResult.Failure(
                Reason.InRangeFailed(
                    varName = "health",
                    actualValue = 30,
                    min = 50,
                    max = 100,
                )
            ),
            result,
        )
    }

    @Test
    fun `not failed reason when inner succeeds`() {
        val inner = Condition.Has("sword")
        val result = Evaluator.evaluateWithReason(
            Condition.Not(inner),
            state(flags = setOf("sword")),
        )
        assertEquals(
            EvaluationResult.Failure(Reason.NotFailed(inner)),
            result,
        )
    }

    @Test
    fun `not succeeds when inner fails`() {
        val result = Evaluator.evaluateWithReason(
            Condition.Not(Condition.Has("sword")),
            state(),
        )
        assertEquals(EvaluationResult.Success, result)
    }

    @Test
    fun `and failed on left reports left reason`() {
        val result = Evaluator.evaluateWithReason(
            Condition.And(Condition.Has("a"), Condition.Has("b")),
            state(),
        )
        assertEquals(
            EvaluationResult.Failure(
                Reason.AndFailed(Reason.HasFailed("a")),
            ),
            result,
        )
    }

    @Test
    fun `and failed on right reports right reason`() {
        val result = Evaluator.evaluateWithReason(
            Condition.And(Condition.Has("a"), Condition.Has("b")),
            state(flags = setOf("a")),
        )
        assertEquals(
            EvaluationResult.Failure(
                Reason.AndFailed(Reason.HasFailed("b")),
            ),
            result,
        )
    }

    @Test
    fun `and short circuits on false left`() {
        // Left fails, right not evaluated. Reason is left's, not
        // OrFailed or anything from right.
        val result = Evaluator.evaluateWithReason(
            Condition.And(
                Condition.Has("a"),
                Condition.Compare("health", CompareOp.GE, 50),
            ),
            state(stats = mapOf("health" to 0)),
        )
        // Only "a" missing is reported; health=0 comparison not attempted.
        assertEquals(
            EvaluationResult.Failure(
                Reason.AndFailed(Reason.HasFailed("a")),
            ),
            result,
        )
    }

    @Test
    fun `or failed both sides reports both reasons`() {
        val result = Evaluator.evaluateWithReason(
            Condition.Or(Condition.Has("a"), Condition.Has("b")),
            state(),
        )
        assertEquals(
            EvaluationResult.Failure(
                Reason.OrFailed(
                    leftReason = Reason.HasFailed("a"),
                    rightReason = Reason.HasFailed("b"),
                )
            ),
            result,
        )
    }

    @Test
    fun `or short circuits on true left`() {
        val result = Evaluator.evaluateWithReason(
            Condition.Or(Condition.Has("a"), Condition.Has("b")),
            state(flags = setOf("a")),
        )
        assertEquals(EvaluationResult.Success, result)
    }

    @Test
    fun `or short circuits on true right`() {
        val result = Evaluator.evaluateWithReason(
            Condition.Or(Condition.Has("a"), Condition.Has("b")),
            state(flags = setOf("b")),
        )
        assertEquals(EvaluationResult.Success, result)
    }

    @Test
    fun `nested and inside or reason is or of left-and and right`() {
        // `(a && b) || c` with `a=false, b=false, c=false`:
        // Left (And) fails with AndFailed(HasFailed("a"));
        // Right (c) fails with HasFailed("c");
        // Whole thing: OrFailed(AndFailed(HasFailed("a")), HasFailed("c")).
        val result = Evaluator.evaluateWithReason(
            Condition.Or(
                Condition.And(Condition.Has("a"), Condition.Has("b")),
                Condition.Has("c"),
            ),
            state(),
        )
        assertEquals(
            EvaluationResult.Failure(
                Reason.OrFailed(
                    leftReason = Reason.AndFailed(Reason.HasFailed("a")),
                    rightReason = Reason.HasFailed("c"),
                )
            ),
            result,
        )
    }

    @Test
    fun `double not on true inner succeeds`() {
        // !!true = true
        val result = Evaluator.evaluateWithReason(
            Condition.Not(Condition.Not(Condition.Has("a"))),
            state(flags = setOf("a")),
        )
        assertEquals(EvaluationResult.Success, result)
    }

    @Test
    fun `double not on false inner fails with nested not reason`() {
        // !!false = false; reason structure:
        // Not(Not(Has("a"))) where a=false:
        //   inner=Has("a") → Failure(HasFailed("a"))
        //   Not(inner) → Success
        //   Not(Not(inner)) → Failure(NotFailed(Not(Has("a"))))
        val innerNot = Condition.Not(Condition.Has("a"))
        val result = Evaluator.evaluateWithReason(
            Condition.Not(innerNot),
            state(),
        )
        assertEquals(
            EvaluationResult.Failure(Reason.NotFailed(innerNot)),
            result,
        )
    }

    @Test
    fun `failure reason is well typed for when - impossible state is rejected by construction`() {
        // Sanity check: `EvaluationResult.Success` cannot carry a reason.
        // The assertion is that the compiler accepts this line — if
        // someone changes `Success` to `data class Success(reason:
        // Reason?)`, this test would still compile but the semantic
        // invariant would be lost. Keeping it as a **compile-time** test
        // by usage: constructing `Success` with an argument is a syntax
        // error, so the only valid form is `EvaluationResult.Success`.
        val success: EvaluationResult = EvaluationResult.Success
        assertIs<EvaluationResult.Success>(success)

    }

        @Test
        fun `choiceState visible when no conditions`() {
            val choice = Choice(

        }

            val choice = Choice(

                visibilityCondition = Condition.Has("sword"),
            )
            assertEquals(ChoiceState.Hidden, Evaluator.choiceState(choice, state()))
        }

        @Test

            // Decision G1: both conditions are false → Hidden, not Disabled.
            val choice = Choice(
                id = ChoiceId("c"),
                text = "Go",
                nextScene = SceneId("next"),
                condition = Condition.Has("magic"),
                visibilityCondition = Condition.Has("sword"),
            )
            assertEquals(ChoiceState.Hidden, Evaluator.choiceState(choice, state()))
        }

package com.myapp.adventure.engine

import java.io.File
import kotlin.test.Test
import kotlin.test.assertTrue
import kotlin.test.fail

/**
 * Ф3.7 — sandbox criterion for `:engine` main sources.
 *
 * **What this test is.** A static scan of every `.kt` file under
 * `engine/src/main/kotlin` for imports and identifiers that break the
 * engine's determinism / purity contract. The engine is the only
 * component that must run identically on device, in JVM tests, and
 * (future) in a JS runtime (E1.base); anything that touches the wall
 * clock, the filesystem, the network, the OS, or non-deterministic
 * randomness would make that impossible.
 *
 * **DoD (Ф3.7, checklist-tracker).** "`evaluate()` в `:engine` не
 * имеет `java.lang.reflect`, `System.*`, файлового IO; статический
 * тест подтверждает; это **не** полный Q1 (экранирование — Ф10), но
 * sandbox готов."
 *
 * **What is forbidden** (see [forbiddenImports] / [forbiddenIdentifiers]):
 *
 * - **Reflection** (`java.lang.reflect`) — sandbox must not inspect
 *   or invoke arbitrary code at runtime.
 * - **File I/O** (`java.io.*`, `java.nio.file.*`) — the engine is a
 *   pure function library; persistence lives in `:app`
 *   (`ProgressManager`, `StepHistoryManager`, `Logger`).
 * - **Network** (`java.net.*`) — the engine has no server calls, and
 *   must not gain any.
 * - **Android** (`android.*`) — `:engine` builds without the Android
 *   SDK (`engine/build.gradle.kts` has no `com.android.*` plugin).
 *   The import check is a cheap redundant guard for that invariant.
 * - **Process execution** (`Runtime.getRuntime`, `ProcessBuilder`) —
 *   side effects on the host OS.
 * - **System side effects** (`System.exit`, `System.getenv`,
 *   `System.getProperties`) — the engine must not depend on
 *   environment; anything that does, gets injected (e.g. a future
 *   `RandomSource` for Ф12 RNG, a `Clock` for time).
 * - **Non-deterministic randomness** (`kotlin.random.Random`,
 *   `java.util.Random`) — using them makes tests flaky and
 *   save/restore non-deterministic. Ф12 will inject a `RandomSource`
 *   explicitly.
 * - **Wall-clock time** (`System.currentTimeMillis`,
 *   `System.nanoTime`) — same reason. If a future feature needs "time
 *   of day" (e.g. "the door is open only after 22:00"), a `Clock` will
 *   be injected; direct `System.currentTimeMillis` from `:engine` is a
 *   sandbox violation.
 *
 * **What is allowed, and why:**
 *
 * - **`java.util.UUID`** — uses `SecureRandom` internally, but UUIDs
 *   are not used in `evaluate` / `Engine.step` today. If a future
 *   feature needs ID generation for logging, that is fine — the
 *   sandbox concern is *evaluation determinism*, not all randomness
 *   everywhere. (If `UUID.randomUUID()` ever appears inside
 *   `Evaluator` / `Engine`, that will be caught by code review, and
 *   the pattern list here can be extended.)
 * - **`java.time.*`** — `LocalDate`, `Duration`, `Instant` as *value
 *   types* are deterministic and side-effect-free. However,
 *   `LocalDate.now()` / `Instant.now()` / `ZonedDateTime.now()`
 *   **indirectly call `System.currentTimeMillis()`**. Today `:engine`
 *   does not use any of the `*.now()` variants, so the sandbox is
 *   clean. **TODO (roadmap):** when the engine first uses time (e.g.
 *   a "night only" invariant), add `LocalDate.now` / `Instant.now` /
 *   etc. to [forbiddenIdentifiers], and inject a `Clock` parameter
 *   instead of reading the wall clock.
 * - **`kotlinx.serialization`** — the `@Serializable` compiler plugin
 *   generates code without runtime reflection for all common cases.
 *   Edge cases (polymorphic deserialization of certain shapes) can
 *   fall back to reflective fallback inside the library. **This is
 *   not our code** — the sandbox check scans our sources, not our
 *   dependencies. If the library ever uses reflection at runtime, that
 *   is outside the scope of this criterion (it would show up as a
 *   failure on a JS runtime that has no reflection, in E1.base).
 * - **`java.util.Locale`** — deterministic value type; if locale-
 *   dependent formatting is ever needed in the engine, that is a
 *   design decision (and would violate i18n separation anyway), not
 *   a sandbox violation.
 * - **`kotlin.*`** — stdlib, no side effects.
 *
 * **How the check works.** Line-based scan:
 *
 * 1. For every `.kt` file under `engine/src/main/kotlin`:
 *    - For every line whose trimmed form starts with `import`, apply
 *      every regex in [forbiddenImports].
 *    - For every line that is **not** a comment (does not start with
 *      `//`, `*`, or a block-comment opener after trimming), apply
 *      every regex in [forbiddenIdentifiers].
 * 2. Collect all violations with file path and line number.
 * 3. If non-empty, `fail()` with the full list — a single failing
 *    test run shows every offender at once, not just the first.
 *
 * **Limitations of the line-based approach (documented, not bugs):**
 *
 * - **Comments are approximated, not parsed.** A KDoc line starting
 *   with ` * System.exit` is skipped (a valid comment); a string
 *   literal `"System.exit"` on a code line is *not* skipped and would
 *   be a false positive. The `:engine` codebase does not contain such
 *   strings today, and the probability of introducing one is low.
 * - **Block comments on the same line as code** are not handled: a
 *   line like `val x = 1 // System.exit` would be flagged. Not the
 *   case in practice.
 * - **Multi-line strings** (`"""..."""`) are not handled. Not used in
 *   `:engine` today.
 *
 * If any of these become real, replace with an AST-based scan
 * (`kotlin-compiler-embeddable` + `KtFile.visitChildren`) — an
 * overkill for the current code size and value, but a clean upgrade
 * path.
 *
 * **What this test does NOT cover** (deliberately, per Ф3.7 DoD):
 *
 * - **HTML escaping / XSS** — Q1 proper, Ф10.2. That is a
 *   `:app` / exporter concern, not `:engine`.
 * - **JS runtime sandbox** (`window` / `document` / `eval` / `fetch`)
 *   — E1.base (Ф8.9). Same principle, different source language.
 * - **Dependency-level reflection** — see "kotlinx.serialization"
 *   above.
 * - **Threat model / docs** — `docs/security.md` (Ф10.9). This test
 *   is the machine-checkable part; the human-readable side lands with
 *   Ф10.
*/
class SandboxTest {

/**
 * Import patterns forbidden in `:engine/src/main/kotlin`.
 *
 * Each entry pairs a short label (for failure messages) with a
 * regex that matches the `import`-line. Regex is anchored at
 * `^import\s+` so that `// import java.io.File` (a comment) does
 * not match — the caller already filters comments before applying
 * this list, but the anchor makes the intent explicit.
*/
private val forbiddenImports: List<Pair<String, Regex>> = listOf(
"reflection" to Regex("""^import\s+java\.lang\.reflect\b"""),
"java.io" to Regex("""^import\s+java\.io\b"""),
"java.nio.file" to Regex("""^import\s+java\.nio\.file\b"""),
"network" to Regex("""^import\s+java\.net\b"""),
"android" to Regex("""^import\s+android\b"""),
"kotlin.random.Random" to Regex("""^import\s+kotlin\.random\.Random\b"""),
"java.util.Random" to Regex("""^import\s+java\.util\.Random\b"""),
)

/**
 * Identifier patterns forbidden in non-comment lines of
 * `:engine/src/main/kotlin`.
 *
 * These cover cases the import scan cannot catch: `System` and
 * `Runtime` live in `java.lang`, auto-imported, so `System.exit`
 * would appear without an `import`. `ProcessBuilder` is in
 * `java.lang` too. The regex is anchored with `\b` on both sides
 * so `System.exitCode` (hypothetical) does not match
 * `System.exit` and `ProcessBuilderFactory` does not match
 * `ProcessBuilder` — deliberate.
*/
private val forbiddenIdentifiers: List<Pair<String, Regex>> = listOf(
"System.exit" to Regex("""\bSystem\.exit\b"""),
"System.getenv" to Regex("""\bSystem\.getenv\b"""),
"System.getProperties" to Regex("""\bSystem\.getProperties\b"""),
"System.currentTimeMillis" to Regex("""\bSystem\.currentTimeMillis\b"""),
"System.nanoTime" to Regex("""\bSystem\.nanoTime\b"""),
"Runtime.getRuntime" to Regex("""\bRuntime\.getRuntime\b"""),
"ProcessBuilder" to Regex("""\bProcessBuilder\b"""),
)

@Test
fun `main sources have no forbidden imports or identifiers`() {
val root = locateMainSources()
val violations = mutableListOf<String>()

root.walkTopDown()
.filter { it.isFile && it.extension == "kt" }
.sortedBy { it.relativeTo(root).path }
.forEach { file ->
val relative = file.relativeTo(root).path
file.readLines(Charsets.UTF_8).forEachIndexed { index, line ->
val lineNumber = index + 1
val trimmed = line.trimStart()
val isComment = trimmed.startsWith("//") ||
trimmed.startsWith("*") ||
trimmed.startsWith("/*")
if (!isComment && trimmed.startsWith("import")) {
for ((label, regex) in forbiddenImports) {
if (regex.containsMatchIn(line)) {
violations += "$relative:$lineNumber — forbidden import ($label): ${line.trim()}"
}
}
}
if (!isComment) {
for ((label, regex) in forbiddenIdentifiers) {
if (regex.containsMatchIn(line)) {
violations += "$relative:$lineNumber — forbidden identifier ($label): ${line.trim()}"
}
}
}
}
}

if (violations.isNotEmpty()) {
fail(
"Sandbox violated: :engine main sources must not use reflection, " +
"IO, network, process execution, wall-clock time, or " +
"non-deterministic randomness (see SandboxTest KDoc for the " +
"full rule). If this is intentional, add an exemption with a " +
"written rationale — do not silently extend the pattern list.\n" +
"Violations (${violations.size}):\n" +
violations.joinToString("\n") { "  • $it" },
)
}
}

/**
 * Sanity check: without this, a wrong [locateMainSources] path or a
 * silently-empty scan would pass [main sources have no forbidden
 * imports or identifiers] vacuously.
 *
 * Pins:
 * - the source root is discoverable;
 * - it contains a plausible number of `.kt` files (≥ 10 — the
 *   engine currently has ~20, so the check catches "everything
 *   deleted");
 * - `Evaluator.kt` exists at the root of the engine package — the
 *   file the sandbox criterion is named after. If it is missing,
 *   either the package moved (update this test) or the scan is
 *   looking at the wrong directory.
*/
@Test
fun `main sources exist and are discoverable`() {
val root = locateMainSources()
assertTrue(
root.isDirectory,
"Expected directory: ${root.absolutePath}",
)
val ktFiles = root.walkTopDown()
.filter { it.isFile && it.extension == "kt" }
.toList()
assertTrue(
ktFiles.size >= 10,
"Expected at least 10 .kt files under ${root.absolutePath}, found ${ktFiles.size}. " +
"If the engine was refactored, update this threshold; if the path is wrong, " +
"fix locateMainSources().",
)
assertTrue(
ktFiles.any { it.name == "Evaluator.kt" },
"Evaluator.kt not found under ${root.absolutePath}. " +
"Either the package layout changed (update this test) or the scan is " +
"looking at the wrong directory.",
)
}

/**
 * Locates `engine/src/main/kotlin` from the test's working
 * directory.
 *
 * Two candidates, tried in order:
 * - `src/main/kotlin` — Gradle runs `:engine:test` with
 *   `workingDir = engine/` (module directory), so this resolves
 *   directly.
 * - `engine/src/main/kotlin` — a fallback for running the test from
 *   the repository root (e.g. IDE "Run" on the test class without
 *   the Gradle project working directory).
 *
 * Validates by checking that the engine package subdirectory
 * exists; a directory with no `.kt` files is not a valid root.
*/
private fun locateMainSources(): File {
val candidates = listOf(
File("src/main/kotlin"),
File("engine/src/main/kotlin"),
)
for (candidate in candidates) {
if (candidate.isDirectory &&
candidate.resolve("com/myapp/adventure/engine").isDirectory
) {
return candidate
}
}
error(
"Cannot locate :engine main sources. Tried: " +
candidates.joinToString { it.absolutePath } +
". Current working directory: ${File(".").absolutePath}. " +
"If Gradle ran the test from an unexpected location, add a candidate " +
"in locateMainSources().",
)
}
}

package com.myapp.adventure.engine.analyze

import com.myapp.adventure.engine.CompileResult
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.CompiledAdventure
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.Engine
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.format.JsonToIr
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Adventure
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Chapter
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Choice
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.ChoiceId
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Condition
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.DeathScene
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Effect
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.InitialState
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.CompareOp
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Invariant
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Outcome
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Scene
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.SceneId
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.TagCategory
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.TagDefinition
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.types.VarDecl
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.types.VarType
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.parse.ParseResult
import kotlin.test.Test
import kotlin.test.assertEquals
import kotlin.test.assertIs
import kotlin.test.assertTrue

class AnalyzerTest {

    // ---------- helpers ----------

    private fun scene(
        id: String,
        choices: List<Choice> = emptyList(),
        effects: List<Effect> = emptyList(),
        isEnding: Boolean = false,
        isMerge: Boolean = false,
        mergeSources: List<SceneId> = emptyList(),
    ): Scene = Scene(
        id = SceneId(id),
        text = "text of $id",
        choices = choices,
        effects = effects,
        isEnding = isEnding,
        isMerge = isMerge,
        mergeSources = mergeSources,
    )

    private fun choice(
        id: String,
        next: String,
        condition: Condition? = null,
    ): Choice = Choice(
        id = ChoiceId(id),
        text = "to $next",
        nextScene = SceneId(next),
        condition = condition,
    )

    private fun chapter(id: String, vararg scenes: Scene): Chapter =
        Chapter(id = id, title = id, scenes = scenes.toList())

    private fun adventure(start: String, vararg chapters: Chapter): Adventure =
        Adventure(
            title = "T",
            startScene = SceneId(start),
            chapters = chapters.toList(),
        )

    private fun adventureWithLintSetup(
        start: String,
        tags: List<TagDefinition> = emptyList(),
        variables: Map<String, VarDecl> = emptyMap(),
        initialState: InitialState = InitialState(),
        deathScene: DeathScene? = null,
        vararg chapters: Chapter,
    ): Adventure = Adventure(
        title = "T",
        startScene = SceneId(start),
        tags = tags,
        variables = variables,
        initialState = initialState,
        deathScene = deathScene,
        chapters = chapters.toList(),
    )

    private fun itemTag(name: String): TagDefinition =
        TagDefinition(name = name, category = TagCategory.ITEM)

    private fun healthTag(name: String = "health"): TagDefinition =
        TagDefinition(name = name, category = TagCategory.HEALTH)

    private fun journalTag(name: String): TagDefinition =
        TagDefinition(name = name, category = TagCategory.JOURNAL)

    private fun compile(adventure: Adventure): CompiledAdventure =
        assertIs<CompileResult.Success>(Engine.compile(adventure)).compiled

    // ---------- reachable ----------

    @Test
    fun `linear chain - all scenes reachable`() {
        val a = scene("a", listOf(choice("c1", "b")))
        val b = scene("b", listOf(choice("c2", "c")))
        val c = scene("c")
        val compiled = compile(adventure("a", chapter("ch", a, b, c)))

        val report = Analyzer.reachable(compiled)
        assertEquals(setOf(SceneId("a"), SceneId("b"), SceneId("c")), report.reachable)
        assertEquals(emptyList(), report.unreachable)
        assertEquals(listOf(SceneId("c")), report.deadEnds)
    }

    @Test
    fun `orphan scene is unreachable`() {
        val a = scene("a", listOf(choice("c1", "b")))
        val b = scene("b")
        val orphan = scene("orphan")
        val compiled = compile(adventure("a", chapter("ch", a, b, orphan)))

        val report = Analyzer.reachable(compiled)
        assertEquals(setOf(SceneId("a"), SceneId("b")), report.reachable)
        assertEquals(listOf(SceneId("orphan")), report.unreachable)
        assertEquals(listOf(SceneId("b")), report.deadEnds)
    }

    @Test
    fun `cross-chapter transition is reachable`() {
        val a = scene("a", listOf(choice("c1", "b")))
        val b = scene("b")
        val compiled = compile(
            adventure("a", chapter("ch1", a), chapter("ch2", b)),
        )

        val report = Analyzer.reachable(compiled)
        assertEquals(setOf(SceneId("a"), SceneId("b")), report.reachable)
        assertEquals(emptyList(), report.unreachable)
    }

    @Test
    fun `self-loop is reachable and terminates`() {
        val a = scene("a", listOf(choice("c1", "a")))
        val compiled = compile(adventure("a", chapter("ch", a)))

        val report = Analyzer.reachable(compiled)
        assertEquals(setOf(SceneId("a")), report.reachable)
        assertEquals(emptyList(), report.unreachable)
        // a has choices (self-loop), so it is not a dead end.
        assertEquals(emptyList(), report.deadEnds)
    }

    @Test
    fun `two-way cycle is reachable`() {
        val a = scene("a", listOf(choice("c1", "b")))
        val b = scene("b", listOf(choice("c2", "a")))
        val compiled = compile(adventure("a", chapter("ch", a, b)))

        val report = Analyzer.reachable(compiled)
        assertEquals(setOf(SceneId("a"), SceneId("b")), report.reachable)
        assertEquals(emptyList(), report.unreachable)
        assertEquals(emptyList(), report.deadEnds)
    }

    @Test
    fun `missing start scene - everything unreachable`() {
        // Engine.compile rejects this (CompileError.MissingStartScene,
        // Ф1.6.2.1), so in production the reader never sees this state.
        // But CompiledAdventure is a public data class; anyone can
        // construct one by hand (tests, future tooling). This test
        // documents that Analyzer.reachable is **defensive**: with a
        // missing start scene, `reachable` is empty and every existing
        // scene is unreachable.
        val a = scene("a")
        val adv = adventure("ghost", chapter("ch", a))
        val compiled = CompiledAdventure(
            adventure = adv,
            scenesById = mapOf(SceneId("a") to a),
            chapterIndexBySceneId = mapOf(SceneId("a") to 0),
        )

        val report = Analyzer.reachable(compiled)
        assertEquals(emptySet(), report.reachable)
        assertEquals(listOf(SceneId("a")), report.unreachable)
        assertEquals(emptyList(), report.deadEnds)
    }

    @Test
    fun `nextScene to missing scene is not added to reachable`() {
        // Engine.compile rejects this (CompileError.MissingNextScene,
        // Ф1.6.2.1). Documenting Analyzer's defensive behaviour on a
        // manually-built CompiledAdventure: a missing target does not
        // enter `reachable` — it cannot be visited.
        val a = scene("a", listOf(choice("c1", "ghost")))
        val adv = adventure("a", chapter("ch", a))
        val compiled = CompiledAdventure(
            adventure = adv,
            scenesById = mapOf(SceneId("a") to a),
            chapterIndexBySceneId = mapOf(SceneId("a") to 0),
        )

        val report = Analyzer.reachable(compiled)
        assertEquals(setOf(SceneId("a")), report.reachable)
        assertEquals(emptyList(), report.unreachable)
        assertEquals(emptyList(), report.deadEnds)
    }

    @Test
    fun `missing nextScene does not produce a false unreachable lint`() {
        // Same setup as above; no lint issues. Missing references are
        // compile errors (Ф1.6.2.1), not lint issues. The analyzer sees a
        // valid CompiledAdventure with one dangling edge, but that edge
        // does not create a phantom scene, so nothing to lint.
        val a = scene("a", listOf(choice("c1", "ghost")))
        val adv = adventure("a", chapter("ch", a))
        val compiled = CompiledAdventure(
            adventure = adv,
            scenesById = mapOf(SceneId("a") to a),
            chapterIndexBySceneId = mapOf(SceneId("a") to 0),
        )

        assertEquals(emptyList(), Analyzer.lint(compiled))
    }

    // ---------- lint ----------

    @Test
    fun `lint empty when everything reachable`() {
        val a = scene("a", listOf(choice("c1", "b")))
        val b = scene("b", isEnding = true)
        val compiled = compile(adventure("a", chapter("ch", a, b)))

        assertEquals(emptyList(), Analyzer.lint(compiled))
    }

    @Test
    fun `lint reports unreachable scene`() {
        // Ф1.6.2.3 fix: `a` used to be terminal, which now also triggers
        // DeadEnd (reachable terminal not at the end of the last chapter).
        // Adding a self-loop keeps `a` reachable and non-terminal, so the
        // test focuses on its intent: orphan is reported as
        // UnreachableScene and nothing else fires.
        val a = scene("a", choices = listOf(choice("loop", "a")))
        val orphan = scene("orphan")
        val compiled = compile(adventure("a", chapter("ch", a, orphan)))

        val issues = Analyzer.lint(compiled)
        assertEquals(1, issues.size)
        val issue = issues.single()
        assertIs<LintKind.UnreachableScene>(issue.kind)
        assertEquals(SceneId("orphan"), issue.sceneId)
        assertEquals(Severity.WARNING, issue.severity)
        assertTrue(issue.message.contains("orphan"), issue.message)
        assertTrue(issue.message.contains("a"), issue.message)
    }

    @Test
    fun `lint issues are sorted by scene id`() {
        // Ф1.6.2.3 fix: `a` used to be terminal → also triggers DeadEnd,
        // which is sorted to the front and broke the expected list. A
        // self-loop keeps `a` reachable and non-terminal, so the only
        // issues are the two orphan scenes, which is what the test is
        // actually about (stable sorting).
        val a = scene("a", choices = listOf(choice("loop", "a")))
        val orphanZ = scene("z_orphan")
        val orphanA = scene("a_orphan")
        val compiled = compile(
            adventure("a", chapter("ch", a, orphanZ, orphanA)),
        )

        val ids = Analyzer.lint(compiled).map { it.sceneId }
        assertEquals(listOf(SceneId("a_orphan"), SceneId("z_orphan")), ids)
    }

    // ---------- lint: removing unestablished item ----------

    @Test
    fun `lint reports removing unestablished item`() {
        val a = scene(
            "a",
            effects = listOf(Effect.ModifyStat("sword", -1)),
        )
        val compiled = compile(
            adventureWithLintSetup(
                start = "a",
                tags = listOf(itemTag("sword")),
                chapters = arrayOf(chapter("ch", a)),
            ),
        )

        val issue = Analyzer.lint(compiled)
            .single { it.kind is LintKind.RemovingUnestablishedItem }
        assertEquals(
            LintKind.RemovingUnestablishedItem("sword"),
            issue.kind,
        )
        assertEquals(SceneId("a"), issue.sceneId)
        assertEquals(Severity.WARNING, issue.severity)
        assertTrue(issue.message.contains("sword"), issue.message)
    }

    @Test
    fun `lint does not report removing item established in initial state`() {
        val a = scene(
            "a",
            effects = listOf(Effect.ModifyStat("sword", -1)),
            isEnding = true,
        )
        val compiled = compile(
            adventureWithLintSetup(
                start = "a",
                tags = listOf(itemTag("sword")),
                initialState = InitialState(stats = mapOf("sword" to 1)),
                chapters = arrayOf(chapter("ch", a)),
            ),
        )

        assertEquals(emptyList(), Analyzer.lint(compiled))
    }

    @Test
    fun `lint does not report removing item established by positive effect`() {
        // 'sword' is given in scene 'give' and reduced in scene 'use'.
        val give = scene(
            "give",
            choices = listOf(choice("c", "use")),
            effects = listOf(Effect.ModifyStat("sword", 1)),
        )
        val use = scene(
            "use",
            effects = listOf(Effect.ModifyStat("sword", -1)),
            isEnding = true,
        )
        val compiled = compile(
            adventureWithLintSetup(
                start = "give",
                tags = listOf(itemTag("sword")),
                chapters = arrayOf(chapter("ch", give, use)),
            ),
        )

        assertEquals(emptyList(), Analyzer.lint(compiled))
    }

    @Test
    fun `lint does not report removing item established by Set effect`() {
        // Ф3.1: `Set("sword", 1)` establishes a positive value, so a
        // later `ModifyStat("sword", -1)` is legitimate. Parallel to
        // `lint does not report removing item established by positive effect`,
        // but with `Set` as the establishing effect.
        val give = scene(
            "give",
            choices = listOf(choice("c", "use")),
            effects = listOf(Effect.Set("sword", 1)),
        )
        val use = scene(
            "use",
            effects = listOf(Effect.ModifyStat("sword", -1)),
            isEnding = true,
        )
        val compiled = compile(
            adventureWithLintSetup(
                start = "give",
                tags = listOf(itemTag("sword")),
                chapters = arrayOf(chapter("ch", give, use)),
            ),
        )

        assertEquals(emptyList(), Analyzer.lint(compiled))
    }

    @Test
    fun `lint reports removing item when Set effect value is zero`() {
        // Ф3.1: `Set("sword", 0)` does NOT establish sword. A later
        // `ModifyStat("sword", -1)` should be reported as
        // RemovingUnestablishedItem — same as if there was no `Set` at
        // all. (This mirrors `lint reports removing unestablished item`.)
        val use = scene(
            "start",
            effects = listOf(
                Effect.Set("sword", 0),
                Effect.ModifyStat("sword", -1),
            ),
            isEnding = true,
        )
        val compiled = compile(
            adventureWithLintSetup(
                start = "start",
                tags = listOf(itemTag("sword")),
                chapters = arrayOf(chapter("ch", use)),
            ),
        )

        val issue = Analyzer.lint(compiled)
            .single { it.kind is LintKind.RemovingUnestablishedItem }
        assertEquals(
            LintKind.RemovingUnestablishedItem("sword"),
            issue.kind,
        )
    }

    @Test
    fun `lint ignores negative change on journal variable`() {
        // 'mana' is JOURNAL, not ITEM/HEALTH; reducing it is not this check's job.
        val a = scene(
            "a",
            effects = listOf(Effect.ModifyStat("mana", -5)),
            isEnding = true,
        )
        val compiled = compile(
            adventureWithLintSetup(
                start = "a",
                tags = listOf(journalTag("mana")),
                chapters = arrayOf(chapter("ch", a)),
            ),
        )

        assertEquals(emptyList(), Analyzer.lint(compiled))
    }

    @Test
    fun `lint does not report death scene when health modified in scene`() {
        // Ф1.6.2.2 fix: the previous version had only a negative
        // ModifyStat("health", -10), which legitimately triggers
        // RemovingUnestablishedItem — a *different* check that lives in
        // the same lint() call. The test's intent is narrow: verify that
        // DeathSceneWithoutHealth stays silent when health is modified
        // anywhere (the check does not care about the sign). Adding a
        // positive ModifyStat makes health "established", so
        // RemovingUnestablishedItem does not fire either, and
        // assertEquals(emptyList(), …) again means "this sample is
        // semantically clean" — the convention used by every other
        // clean-sample test in this file.
        val a = scene(
            "a",
            effects = listOf(
                Effect.ModifyStat("health", 10),
                Effect.ModifyStat("health", -10),
            ),
            isEnding = true,
        )
        val compiled = compile(
            adventureWithLintSetup(
                start = "a",
                tags = listOf(healthTag()),
                deathScene = DeathScene(),
                chapters = arrayOf(chapter("ch", a)),
            ),
        )

        assertEquals(emptyList(), Analyzer.lint(compiled))
    }

    @Test
    fun `lint does not report condition on name that appears as stat`() {
        // Shim behavior (see LintKind.ConditionOnUnestablishedFlag KDoc):
        // has_sword is not a flag, but sword appears in initial_state.stats,
        // so we treat it as "known name". Type mismatch is Ф2.2's job.

        // updating — the intent shifts to "sword exists, but using has_*
        // on it is a type error, not an unknown-name error".

            adventureWithLintSetup(

                chapters = arrayOf(chapter("ch", a)),

    }

    // ---------- lint: dead end ----------

    @Test
    fun `lint does not report dead end on last scene of last chapter`() {
        // Ф1.7.0: "last scene of the last chapter" is no longer an
        // implicit ending — the scene must be explicitly marked.
        val a = scene("a", isEnding = true) // terminal, last scene, explicitly an ending
        val compiled = compile(adventure("a", chapter("ch", a)))

        assertEquals(emptyList(), Analyzer.lint(compiled))
    }

    @Test
    fun `lint reports reachable dead end mid-adventure`() {
        val a = scene("a", choices = listOf(choice("c1", "b")))
        val b = scene("b") // terminal, reachable, not last scene
        val c = scene("c") // last scene, but unreachable from a
        val compiled = compile(
            adventure("a", chapter("ch1", a, b), chapter("ch2", c)),
        )

        val issues = Analyzer.lint(compiled)
        val kinds = issues.map { it.kind }
        assertTrue(LintKind.DeadEnd in kinds, "expected DeadEnd, got $kinds")
        assertTrue(
            LintKind.UnreachableScene in kinds,
            "expected UnreachableScene(c), got $kinds",
        )
        assertEquals(
            listOf(SceneId("b")),
            issues.filter { it.kind == LintKind.DeadEnd }.mapNotNull { it.sceneId },
        )
    }

    @Test
    fun `lint does not report dead end on unreachable terminal scene`() {
        // Ф1.7.0: `b` must be explicitly marked as an ending, otherwise
        // the "last scene of the last chapter" convenience no longer
        // applies and DeadEnd(b) fires.
        val a = scene("a", choices = listOf(choice("c1", "b")))
        val b = scene("b", isEnding = true) // reachable, terminal, explicitly an ending
        val orphan = scene("orphan")         // unreachable, terminal, mid-chapter
        val compiled = compile(
            adventure("a", chapter("ch", a, orphan, b)),
        )

        val kinds = Analyzer.lint(compiled).map { it.kind }
        assertTrue(LintKind.UnreachableScene in kinds)
        assertTrue(
            LintKind.DeadEnd !in kinds,
            "unreachable terminal scene must not be double-flagged as DeadEnd: $kinds",
        )
    }

    // ---------- integration: test_adventure.json is lint-clean ----------

    @Test
    fun `lint reports dead end as WARNING`() {
        // Revised 2026-11-07: DeadEnd is a WARNING (the reader warns,
        // does not block). Only EndingSceneWithChoices remains ERROR.
        val a = scene("a", choices = listOf(choice("c1", "b")))
        val b = scene("b") // terminal, no isEnding → DeadEnd
        val compiled = compile(adventure("a", chapter("ch", a, b)))

        val deadEnd = Analyzer.lint(compiled).single { it.kind == LintKind.DeadEnd }
        assertEquals(Severity.WARNING, deadEnd.severity)
        assertEquals(SceneId("b"), deadEnd.sceneId)
        assertTrue(deadEnd.message.contains("is_ending"), deadEnd.message)
    }

    @Test
    fun `lint reports ending scene with choices`() {
        val a = scene(
            "a",
            choices = listOf(choice("c1", "a")),
            isEnding = true, // contradictory: ending + choices
        )
        val compiled = compile(adventure("a", chapter("ch", a)))

        val issue = Analyzer.lint(compiled).single {
            it.kind is LintKind.EndingSceneWithChoices
        }

        assertEquals(SceneId("a"), issue.sceneId)
        assertEquals(LintKind.EndingSceneWithChoices(SceneId("a")), issue.kind)
        assertTrue(issue.message.contains("1 choice"), issue.message)
    }

        assertEquals(emptyList(), Analyzer.lint(compiled))
    }

    // ---------- Ф4.6: merge conflicts ----------

    @Test
    fun `merge conflict - merge point with no incoming branches`() {
        val m = scene("m", isMerge = true, isEnding = true)
        val compiled = compile(adventure("m", chapter("ch", m)))

        val issue = Analyzer.checkMerges(compiled).single()
        assertEquals(SceneId("m"), issue.sceneId)
        val kind = assertIs<LintKind.MergeConflict>(issue.kind)
        assertEquals(LintKind.MergeConflict.Reason.NoIncomingBranches, kind.reason)
        assertEquals(null, kind.sourceSceneId)
        assertEquals(Severity.WARNING, issue.severity)
        assertTrue(issue.message.contains("no choice"), issue.message)
    }

    @Test
    fun `merge conflict - declared source does not lead here`() {
        // Both sources are reachable, but only 'left' points at 'm'.
        val left = scene("left", choices = listOf(choice("to_m", "m")))
        val right = scene("right", isEnding = true)
        val start = scene(
            "start",
            choices = listOf(choice("go_left", "left"), choice("go_right", "right")),
        )
        val m = scene(
            "m",
            isEnding = true,
            isMerge = true,
            mergeSources = listOf(SceneId("left"), SceneId("right")),
        )
        val compiled = compile(adventure("start", chapter("ch", start, left, right, m)))

        val issue = Analyzer.checkMerges(compiled).single()
        val kind = assertIs<LintKind.MergeConflict>(issue.kind)
        assertEquals(LintKind.MergeConflict.Reason.SourceDoesNotLeadHere, kind.reason)
        assertEquals(SceneId("right"), kind.sourceSceneId)
        assertEquals(SceneId("m"), issue.sceneId)
    }

    @Test
    fun `merge conflict - declared source is not reachable`() {
        val start = scene("start", choices = listOf(choice("to_m", "m")))
        val island = scene("island", choices = listOf(choice("to_m", "m")))
        val m = scene(
            "m",
            isEnding = true,
            isMerge = true,
            mergeSources = listOf(SceneId("start"), SceneId("island")),
        )
        val compiled = compile(adventure("start", chapter("ch", start, island, m)))

        val issue = Analyzer.checkMerges(compiled).single()
        val kind = assertIs<LintKind.MergeConflict>(issue.kind)
        assertEquals(LintKind.MergeConflict.Reason.SourceNotReachable, kind.reason)
        assertEquals(SceneId("island"), kind.sourceSceneId)
        assertEquals(SceneId("m"), issue.sceneId)
        assertTrue(issue.message.contains("island"), issue.message)
    }

    @Test
    fun `merge conflict - source neither leads here nor reachable is reported once`() {
        // 'island' has no edge to 'm' and cannot be reached from 'start'.
        // Only the actionable "does not lead here" warning is emitted;
        // the reachability warning would be redundant noise.
        val start = scene("start", choices = listOf(choice("to_m", "m")))
        val island = scene("island", choices = listOf(choice("back", "start")))
        val m = scene(
            "m",
            isEnding = true,
            isMerge = true,
            mergeSources = listOf(SceneId("start"), SceneId("island")),
        )
        val compiled = compile(adventure("start", chapter("ch", start, island, m)))

        val issue = Analyzer.checkMerges(compiled).single()
        val kind = assertIs<LintKind.MergeConflict>(issue.kind)
        assertEquals(LintKind.MergeConflict.Reason.SourceDoesNotLeadHere, kind.reason)
        assertEquals(SceneId("island"), kind.sourceSceneId)
    }

    @Test
    fun `merge without conflicts - all sources lead here and are reachable`() {
        val start = scene(
            "start",
            choices = listOf(choice("go_left", "left"), choice("go_right", "right")),
        )
        val left = scene("left", choices = listOf(choice("to_m", "m")))
        val right = scene("right", choices = listOf(choice("to_m", "m")))
        val m = scene(
            "m",
            isEnding = true,
            isMerge = true,
            mergeSources = listOf(SceneId("left"), SceneId("right")),
        )
        val compiled = compile(adventure("start", chapter("ch", start, left, right, m)))

        assertEquals(emptyList(), Analyzer.checkMerges(compiled))
        assertTrue(Analyzer.lint(compiled).none { it.kind is LintKind.MergeConflict })
    }

    @Test
    fun `lint includes merge conflicts`() {
        val m = scene("m", isMerge = true, isEnding = true)
        val compiled = compile(adventure("m", chapter("ch", m)))

        val mergeIssues = Analyzer.lint(compiled).filter { it.kind is LintKind.MergeConflict }
        assertEquals(1, mergeIssues.size)
    }

    @Test
    fun `lint is clean on test_adventure_json`() {
        // test_adventure.json is the reference sample: every new user gets
        // it copied into their library on first launch. If the analyzer
        // flags something in it, either the sample is broken (fix the file)
        // or the new check is too aggressive (fix the check). This test is
        // the tripwire.
        val stream = javaClass.getResourceAsStream("/test_adventure.json")
            ?: error("test_adventure.json not on classpath")
        val raw = stream.bufferedReader().use { it.readText() }
        val adventure = assertIs<ParseResult.Success<Adventure>>(
            JsonToIr.parse(raw),
            "test_adventure.json must parse successfully",
        ).value
        val compiled = assertIs<CompileResult.Success>(
            Engine.compile(adventure),
            "test_adventure.json must compile successfully",
        ).compiled

        assertEquals(
            emptyList(),
            Analyzer.lint(compiled),
            "test_adventure.json must be lint-clean under current rules",
        )
    }
}

FILE: engine/src/test/kotlin/com/myapp/adventure/engine/format/GoldenIrTest.kt
================================================
package com.myapp.adventure.engine.format

import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Adventure
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.parse.ParseResult
import kotlinx.serialization.json.Json
import kotlinx.serialization.json.JsonElement
import kotlinx.serialization.json.JsonObject
import kotlinx.serialization.json.JsonPrimitive
import kotlinx.serialization.json.jsonObject
import kotlin.test.Test
import kotlin.test.assertEquals
import kotlin.test.assertIs
import kotlin.test.assertTrue
import kotlin.test.fail

/**
 * Golden test for the IR: parses the real `test_adventure.json`, serializes
 * the resulting [Adventure] back to JSON, and compares **semantically**
 * against `engine/src/test/resources/golden_ir.json`.
 *
 * **Why this test exists:** every commit that changes the IR (adds, removes,
 * or renames a field) or the parser (changes how JSON becomes IR) can silently
 * break every adventure file in the wild. This test is the tripwire: **if
 * it fails and you did not intend to change the on-disk shape, you found a
 * bug**. If you did intend to change it, regenerate the golden with
 * `./gradlew :engine:updateGolden` and commit both.
 *
 * **Comparison is semantic, not textual.** `JsonElement`-tree equality
 * ignores whitespace, key order, and insignificant formatting. That means:
 * - Reformatting `golden_ir.json` in an IDE does not break the test.
 * - Reordering fields in JSON (Kotlin data class or `@SerialName`) does
 *   not break the test if the semantic structure is unchanged.
 * - A real semantic change (missing field, different value, different type)
 *   **does** break the test, with a diff that points at the exact spot.
 *
 * **Not `encodeDefaults = false` only.** The comparison uses the same
 * `PRETTY_JSON` config as [GoldenWriter] (`prettyPrint = true`,
 * `encodeDefaults = false`) so that both sides strip default-valued fields.
 * The golden file is human-readable (good for code review), and both sides
 * are normalized before comparison (good for stability).
 */
class GoldenIrTest {

    private val prettyJson: Json = Json {
        prettyPrint = true
        encodeDefaults = false
    }

    private fun loadText(path: String): String {
        val stream = javaClass.getResourceAsStream(path)
            ?: fail(
                "Resource '$path' not found on classpath.\n" +
                        "If '$path' is golden_ir.json, run:\n" +
                        "    ./gradlew :engine:updateGolden\n" +
                        "and commit the result.",
            )
        return stream.bufferedReader().use { it.readText() }
    }

    private fun parseRealAdventure(): Adventure {
        val raw = loadText("/test_adventure.json")
        val result = JsonToIr.parse(raw)
        return when (result) {
            is ParseResult.Success -> result.value
            is ParseResult.Failure -> fail(
                "test_adventure.json failed to parse: $result",
            )
        }
    }

    private fun currentIrAsJsonElement(): JsonElement {
        val adventure = parseRealAdventure()
        val text = prettyJson.encodeToString(Adventure.serializer(), adventure)
        return Json.parseToJsonElement(text)
    }

    @Test
    fun `golden matches current IR`() {
        val goldenText = loadText("/golden_ir.json")
        val golden = Json.parseToJsonElement(goldenText)
        val actual = currentIrAsJsonElement()

        if (golden == actual) return

        // Produce a readable diff for the failure message. We do not have a
        // full JSON diff here (would need a library), but we can show the
        // first top-level key that differs, which is usually enough to tell
        // "IR shape changed" from "one value changed".
        val diffHint = topLevelDiffHint(golden, actual)
        fail(
            "IR differs from golden_ir.json.\n" +
                    "\n" +
                    "If you changed the IR (files in :engine/.../ir/), the parser\n" +
                    "(JsonToIr, ConditionParser), or test_adventure.json — and you\n" +
                    "**intended** the change — regenerate the golden:\n" +
                    "\n" +
                    "    ./gradlew :engine:updateGolden\n" +
                    "\n" +
                    "Then run `git diff engine/src/test/resources/golden_ir.json`\n" +
                    "to verify the change is exactly what you expected, and commit\n" +
                    "the golden alongside your code change.\n" +
                    "\n" +
                    "If you did NOT intend any of the above — you found a bug.\n" +
                    "Investigate before running updateGolden.\n" +
                    "\n" +
                    "Hint: $diffHint",
        )
    }

    @Test
    fun `missing golden is a clear failure`() {
        // The `loadText` helper fails with the exact instruction to run
        // `./gradlew :engine:updateGolden`. This test exists so that the
        // failure mode is exercised by CI, not discovered manually when
        // someone deletes golden_ir.json by accident.
        //
        // We do not actually delete the golden in this test (that would race
        // with `golden matches current IR`). Instead, we assert that
        // `loadText` on a nonexistent path produces the expected instruction.
        val missingPath = "/this-file-does-not-exist-golden-ir-test.json"
        val stream = javaClass.getResourceAsStream(missingPath)
        assertEquals(null, stream, "sanity: missing path should be null")

        // And the real golden loads fine.
        val realStream = javaClass.getResourceAsStream("/golden_ir.json")
        assertTrue(
            realStream != null,
            "golden_ir.json should exist; if this fails, run ./gradlew :engine:updateGolden",
        )
        realStream.use { it.readBytes() }
    }

    @Test
    fun `golden round-trips through IR serializer`() {
        // Sanity: the golden file was written by `Adventure.serializer()`
        // and must be readable by the matching deserializer. This catches a
        // specific failure mode: `@Serializable` produces valid JSON that
        // cannot be read back (e.g. a polymorphic sealed class with a
        // missing `@SerialName`, or a value class serialized as an object
        // but expected as a string). If that happens, the golden file is
        // internally inconsistent — useful as documentation, dangerous as a
        // test fixture.
        //
        // **Note on format:** the golden is an **IR serialization**, not an
        // adventure file. `JsonToIr.parse` (adventure format) would fail on
        // it, because IR conditions are structured (`{"type":"has",...}`)
        // while adventure conditions are strings (`"has_sword"`). This test
        // uses `Json.decodeFromString<Adventure>` — the IR deserializer —
        // which is the correct counterpart to `GoldenWriter`.
        val goldenText = loadText("/golden_ir.json")
        val irJson = Json {
            ignoreUnknownKeys = true
            coerceInputValues = true
        }
        val adventure = irJson.decodeFromString<Adventure>(goldenText)
        assertEquals(3, adventure.chapters.size)
        assertEquals("Тестовое приключение", adventure.title)

        // And the re-encoded form must match the golden semantically:
        // decode → encode should not change the IR representation.
        val reEncoded = prettyJson.encodeToString(Adventure.serializer(), adventure)
        val reJson = Json.parseToJsonElement(reEncoded)
        val originalJson = Json.parseToJsonElement(goldenText)
        assertEquals(
            originalJson,
            reJson,
            "IR serialization is not stable through decode→encode",
        )
    }

    // ---------- diff helpers ----------

    private fun topLevelDiffHint(expected: JsonElement, actual: JsonElement): String {
        val e = expected as? JsonObject ?: return "expected is not a JSON object"
        val a = actual as? JsonObject ?: return "actual is not a JSON object"
        val keys = (e.keys + a.keys).sorted()
        for (k in keys) {
            val ev = e[k]
            val av = a[k]
            if (ev != av) {
                return when {
                    ev == null -> "field '$k' present in actual, missing in golden"
                    av == null -> "field '$k' present in golden, missing in actual"
                    ev is JsonPrimitive && av is JsonPrimitive ->
                        "field '$k' changed: golden=$ev, actual=$av"
                    else -> "field '$k' differs structurally (golden type=${ev::class.simpleName}, actual type=${av::class.simpleName})"
                }
            }
        }
        return "no top-level difference found (differs somewhere nested; check full output)"
    }
}

FILE: engine/src/test/kotlin/com/myapp/adventure/engine/format/GoldenWriter.kt
================================================
package com.myapp.adventure.engine.format

import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Adventure
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.parse.ParseResult
import kotlinx.serialization.json.Json
import java.io.File

/**
 * Regenerates `engine/src/test/resources/golden_ir.json` from the current
 * parser and the current `test_adventure.json`.
 *
 * **Not** a test. Not part of `:engine` public API. Not shipped in the jar
 * (this file lives in `src/test/kotlin`). Its only purpose is to serve
 * `./gradlew :engine:updateGolden`, which developers run **after an
 * intentional IR change** and commit alongside the change.
 *
 * **Never** edit `golden_ir.json` by hand:
 * 1. Hand-edits can miss fields or introduce typos that pass a diff-by-eye.
 * 2. The golden is compared **semantically** by `GoldenIrTest` — hand-edit
 *    that preserves semantics but changes formatting is fine, but a
 *    hand-edit that *changes* semantics is a bug, not a fix.
 *
 * **Workflow when you change the IR:**
 * 1. Change the IR (files in `:engine/.../ir/`).
 * 2. Run `./gradlew :engine:updateGolden`.
 * 3. `git diff engine/src/test/resources/golden_ir.json` — verify the diff
 *    is exactly what you expected. If it contains unexpected fields, you
 *    have an unintended IR change; investigate before committing.
 * 4. Commit the golden alongside the IR change.
 *
 * **Workflow when you do NOT change the IR:**
 * If `GoldenIrTest` fails and you did not touch `:engine/.../ir/`, one of:
 * - Someone else changed the IR (in this branch, via merge). Review their
 *   change, then run `updateGolden` if it is intentional.
 * - The parser changed (`JsonToIr`, `ConditionParser`). The golden
 *   captures parser output too, by design: a parser change that alters
 *   IR output is a breaking change for every adventure file.
 * - `test_adventure.json` changed. That is also a deliberate act; update
 *   the golden.
 */
private const val GOLDEN_PATH = "engine/src/test/resources/golden_ir.json"

private val PRETTY_JSON = Json {
    prettyPrint = true
    encodeDefaults = false
}

public fun main() {
    val classLoader = object {}.javaClass.classLoader
    val stream = classLoader.getResourceAsStream("test_adventure.json")
        ?: error(
            "test_adventure.json not found on classpath. " +
                    "The copy task in engine/build.gradle.kts should have placed it " +
                    "in engine/build/resources/test/. Make sure :engine:processTestResources ran.",
        )
    val rawJson = stream.bufferedReader().use { it.readText() }

    val result = JsonToIr.parse(rawJson)
    val adventure: Adventure = when (result) {
        is ParseResult.Success -> result.value
        is ParseResult.Failure -> {
            System.err.println("Cannot regenerate golden: test_adventure.json failed to parse.")
            result.errors.forEach { System.err.println("  ${it.message}") }
            kotlin.system.exitProcess(1)
        }
    }

    val text = PRETTY_JSON.encodeToString(Adventure.serializer(), adventure)
    val out = File(GOLDEN_PATH)
    out.parentFile.mkdirs()
    out.writeText(text)
    println("Wrote $GOLDEN_PATH (${text.length} chars, ${adventure.chapters.size} chapters)")
}
